### 2026-09-30 - Fig 2G: abs-delta promoted from unreported control to a reported third state
**Changed/Found:** `Closedloop_edit/results.tex` body paragraph + Fig-2 caption. The text reported only motion and rel-delta and dismissed abs-delta as "shown but not interpreted"; user wants it reported because it has a distinct dynamic profile and is the third panel of 2G. Re-ran `imp_state_trialvar.m` (STV_MOTEXCL=false, pre window, n=1767, 4 sessions) to get the statistic with its CI rather than reading values off the panel. Stim vs matched stim-free control, Q4/Q1: **motion 0.71 [0.60-0.84] vs ctrl 0.79** (p=1.5e-7, 4/4); **rel-delta 1.10 [0.94-1.27] vs ctrl 1.00** (p=0.005, 3/4; ctrl rho +0.001 p=0.96, i.e. flat); **abs-delta 1.99 [1.69-2.37] vs ctrl 2.10** (p<1e-16, 4/4; ctrl rho +0.366). That is a clean three-way dissociation and is now the organising sentence of the paragraph: motion and rel-delta each BEAT their stim-free control, abs-delta does not. Also computed abs-vs-rel correlation on THIS dataset: **Spearman rho = 0.548** (n=1767), matching the 0.53 previously measured on the 613 controller trials - correlated but not redundant. Build clean, 0 undefined, 35 pp (was 34).
**Why:** Reporting abs-delta WITH its control is strictly stronger than omitting it - the comparison is what licenses the other two claims, and burying the steepest trend in the figure while not mentioning it in the text is the kind of thing a reviewer notices.
**Next:** **Number conflict resolved, flag for the user.** The caption previously said abs-delta ratio **2.04**; that was read off the drawn panel (Q1 0.679 -> Q4 1.387). The statistic `R.ratio`, which is what the 0.71 and 1.10 in the same sentence come from and the only one of the two that carries a CI, is **1.988**. Text and caption now both say 1.99. If the panel value is preferred, all three numbers must switch to panel values for consistency. Separately: `imp_state_trialvar.m`'s header still calls DPa "printed and greyed in the figure, never interpreted" and `R.verdict` returns "CONFOUND - not interpreted" - update that comment so the code and the manuscript agree on what abs-delta is for.


### 2026-09-30 - Delay-bandwidth argument moved Results -> Discussion, and corrected
**Changed/Found:** `Closedloop_edit/results.tex` + `discussion.tex`. The Results paragraph introducing the block diagram carried a long clause deriving a bandwidth limit from the loop delay (90 deg at 5.3 Hz, 180 deg at 10.6 Hz, "loop gain must fall below unity before 10.6 Hz"). Moved it out of Results - it is interpretation, not a measurement - and folded it into the Discussion's third limitation paragraph, which already made the same argument qualitatively. Three substantive corrections on the way: (1) the stability claim was WRONG - it assigned the whole 180 deg phase budget to the delay, but the identified plant is a lightly damped 2nd-order system resonant at 2.2 Hz (tab:tf_sessions) whose phase is already -165 deg at 5 Hz, plus integral action, so the loop crosses -180 deg far below 10.6 Hz; (2) the 35 Hz sample-and-hold adds an effective half-sample (14 ms), so tau_eff ~ 61 ms not 47 ms; (3) using the standard omega_c*tau <= 1 rad crossover criterion gives an achievable bandwidth of ~2.6 Hz, which lands on the 2-4 Hz band that Fig 4C/D identifies as the one disturbance feedback cannot reject. Arithmetic in the original was internally correct for tau = 47 ms (1/(4tau)=5.32, 1/(2tau)=10.64). Results now states only the bare fact (47 ms max, 1.6 control intervals). Build clean: 34 pages, 0 undefined refs/citations.
**Why:** User asked whether the passage belonged upfront or in Discussion, then said to move it. J Neurosci convention puts a measured apparatus number in Methods/Results and its mechanistic interpretation in Discussion; and the argument is worth far more next to the 2-4 Hz residual result it explains than as an aside in the architecture paragraph.
**Next:** UNRESOLVED CONFLICT for the user: `discussion.tex` stated the loop latency as **80 ms** in two places, both citing Fig 1F, while Methods and Results say **47 ms max** from the same figure. I unified toward 47 ms (removed one "80 ms" entirely, kept the other paragraph quantitative at 47 ms) but the true value must be confirmed - PAPER.md line 81 lists Fig 1F as a pending image with no generator, so it cannot be checked from this repo. If 80 ms is correct, tau_eff becomes ~94 ms and the predicted bandwidth drops to ~1.7 Hz. Separately: the ~2.6 Hz coincidence is currently hedged as suggestive; to make it a quantitative claim, discretize the fitted plant, append the delay, and report gain/phase margin at the gains actually used.


### 2026-09-30 - Lagged stim-blind predictor: DIP capture reaches 98% honestly; REBOUND caps at ~40% in every model tried
**Changed/Found:** New `impulse-analysis/imp_lagged_stimblind.m` (experimental). Causal-lagged contra->ipsi ridge, fit on spontaneous frames only, deployed unchanged on stim trials; reports held-out spont R2, dip capture, rebound capture, true-0V catch, AND a matched-random baseline at the same pixel count and the same lag count. Self-contained reimplementation with a SANITY GATE: at L=0 on the TF set it must reproduce f2_decomp (got 94/36 vs 91/34 dip/reb - passed; residual difference is baseline handling).
| K | L | spontR2 | DIP% | REB% | catch% | randDIP | randREB | dDIP | dREB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 91 | 0 | 0.929 | 94 | 36 | -7 | 82 | 25 | +12 | +10 |
| 91 | 8 | 0.934 | 89 | 35 | -6 | 78 | 22 | +11 | +14 |
| 70 | 2 | 0.927 | 94 | 36 | -8 | 83 | 26 | +12 | +11 |
| **50** | **2** | **0.913** | **98** | **40** | **-8** | 89 | 26 | **+9** | **+14** |
| 50 | 0 | 0.911 | 99 | 38 | -9 | 91 | 27 | +8 | +11 |
| 35 | 2 | 0.898 | 95 | 37 | -8 | 93 | 29 | **+2** | +8 |
**(1) LAGS DO NOT HELP.** Over L=0..8 the held-out spont R2 moves only 0.929 -> 0.934, and dip capture FALLS slightly as lags are added (a better ongoing model absorbs more of the evoked response). Rebound is flat at 35-40% at every K and every L. **The contra->ipsi coupling is effectively instantaneous** - which independently corroborates the Ye et al. 2023 instantaneous-SVD basis this stream was built on, and closes the "slow dynamics" explanation for the rebound leak.
**(2) THE DIP GOAL IS REACHABLE: 98% capture, honestly.** K=50 with L=1-4 gives dip 98%, matched-random 89% (**gap +9**), catch -8%, spont R2 0.913, i.e. capture is 98% AND still carries selection information AND the no-stim control passes. This is the first operating point in the project that reaches ~100% dip capture without the KKT/NATIVE tautology.
**(3) THE REBOUND GOAL IS NOT REACHABLE by any model tried.** Rebound capture never exceeds 40% across the whole space explored this session: zero-lag (34), lagged L=1..8 (35-40), rebound-aware masks (37), K from 140 down to 25 (26-38). The ONLY thing that moved it is `select_mode='subspace'` (56-59%), which projects out the evoked TRAJECTORY - i.e. it IMPOSES rebound-blindness rather than earning it, and costs dip capture (down to 73-79%) and R2 (down to 0.85).
**Why:** The user's goal is complete, not partial, capture of the local stim effect. These runs say the dip half is achievable and the rebound half is not - and the consistency of the ~35-40% ceiling across four structurally different approaches is itself the evidence that the post-inhibition rebound is a genuine network event present in the contralateral hemisphere, so a stim-blind contra predictor SHOULD predict it. "Dip local, rebound network" is a result, not a shortfall.
**Next:** (1) Cost of K=50: catch worsens -2 -> -8% (still inside the 15% threshold but no longer negligible) and R2 falls 0.931 -> 0.913. Decide whether 98%/-8% beats 91%/-2% for the supplement; I would report BOTH as an operating-point sensitivity rather than pick one. (2) The rebound claim needs the one measurement I have not got cleanly: a properly DETRENDED contra-vs-ipsi rebound comparison (the two attempts this session were drift-dominated, RESEARCH 2026-09-30). Until that exists, "the rebound is a network event" is an inference from model behaviour, not a direct measurement - do not state it as measured. (3) `imp_lagged_stimblind.m` is EXPERIMENTAL and is not wired into the supplementary figure; `imp_supp_residual.m` still uses f2_model at K=91.

### 2026-09-30 - Regenerated spatial_spread after the pxMM fix; the area panel looks unsalvageable
**Changed/Found:** Ran `impulse-analysis/spatial_spread.m` on AL_0033 2025-01-29 e1 with the corrected 0.0173 mm/px. Areas are now **0.00-0.91 mm2** across 0.18-1.80 mW; the old scale gave up to **91 mm2**, which is larger than the entire 9.7x9.7 mm (94 mm2) field of view, so the published numbers were physically impossible. Two further problems with the panel itself, independent of the scale bug: (1) the curve is **not monotonic** - near zero to 0.6 mW, a step up at 0.77-1.36 mW, then a plateau that slightly DECLINES at the top three amplitudes (0.91, 0.88, 0.85 mm2) - so the manuscript's "grew monotonically with laser power" is not supported; (2) the script's own header says "Quantitative area is not computed: mean resp_maps contain a large global hemodynamic component that cannot be separated from local inhibition via thresholding. The maps are exported as a qualitative illustration" - which directly contradicts the existence of the quantitative panel. The per-amplitude maps confirm it: the low-amplitude maps are dominated by a large positive global pattern and a focal blue suppression only emerges at 1.36 mW+, and the per-amplitude background offsets swing from -0.21 to -2.81 %dF/F.
**Why:** User asked for the figure to be regenerated after this morning's pxMM correction. Doing so exposed that the scale bug was masking a deeper problem: the quantification rests on an annulus background subtraction that the script's author had already judged inadequate.
**Next:** Recommend retiring `fig:spatial_spread` (the quantitative area curve) and keeping only the qualitative `fig:spatial_maps`, which is all the Methods actually needs - evidence that stimulation is focal and covers the readout kernel. If the quantitative claim is wanted, it needs hemodynamically corrected maps and a background taken from the contralateral hemisphere rather than a 0.6-0.9 mm annulus that sits inside the response at high power.

### 2026-09-30 - Bibliography audit: 4 fabricated references, 11 duplicates, 7 invented co-author lists
**Changed/Found:** Audited `Closedloop_edit/refs.bib` (52 entries) against the Crossref REST API by DOI or bibliographic title, comparing surnames AND given names, with web-search confirmation for the two suspected non-existent papers. The real Clancy 2014 paper (volitional modulation of calcium signals) was already present and correct as `clancy2014volitional`. (2) **11 duplicate entries** removed; in five pairs the two copies disagreed on metadata (`ren2021widefield` "Ren, Chengyu" vs correct "Chi"; `Newman2015` had four wrong first names; `zaaimi2023closed` wrong year). (3) **7 author lists carried invented co-authors.** The distinctive fingerprint: a co-author "Bhatt" inserted into FOUR unrelated papers with a different first name each time - in `kanta2019closed` it had replaced the surname of a real author while keeping the first name (Headley, Drew B -> Bhatt, Drew B). `allen2017global` had three fabricated names replacing Gradinaru/Deverman/Luo. All corrected against Crossref. (4) My own Methods cuts had left **7 dangling cross-references** from `discussion.tex` (eq:lpv_*, eq:aug_*, eq:emp_cost, eq:expected_cost, eq:regret); rewrote those three Discussion passages in prose. NOTE for the record: the Discussion DID lean on the LPV framing, so the earlier claim that the LPV block was entirely unused was too strong - it was unused for controller design but load-bearing rhetorically. ### 2026-09-30 — Methods math review: LPV block is unused and unidentifiable; RMSE-minimiser claim is false
**Changed/Found:** `Closedloop_edit/methods_edit.tex` (read-only, pushed `main` fc98561) — audit of the linear-algebra/state-space content. (1) The LPV subsection (L172-202) is never used downstream (no A_k/B_k estimated, rho never measured, no gain scheduling or LMI synthesis) AND is mis-stated: sum runs to n but rho is in R^p, no A_0 and no simplex constraint, so the (A_k, rho) decomposition is unidentifiable up to scaling and rho=0 gives x+ = w+d. (2) **The cost-equivalence claim is mathematically false for gains:** the grid score J_rms = (1/N) sum_i ||e_i||_2 is a MEAN OF NORMS, while sqrt(J_hat) is an RMS of norms; by Jensen these differ and need not share a minimiser over K. Per-trial ranking is fine; the across-gain claim (stated twice, L477 and L554) is not. (3) Augmented state (L445-470): xi integrates state error with an undefined/underdetermined x_ref, xi in R^n makes s in R^2n so K=[Kp,Ki] is dimensionally impossible, and u=+Ks with Kp>0 is positive feedback. (4) Assumption 1 is written as exact equality, which cannot hold for nonlinear f (E[f(x)] != f(E[x])); P/Q are also swapped between the lead-in paragraph and the assumption body. (5) "Under Assumption 1, J_hat -> J" misattributes the LLN; R(N,K) is sampling error, not regret, and is O_p(N^-1/2) not monotonically decreasing. (6) Kr = U Y-dagger regresses amplitude on output, the reverse of the L266 description; with dose-response R^2~0.8 the two slopes differ by ~25%. (7) The tfest model (2 poles, tau=271 ms, 2.2 Hz) is never connected to (Abar,Bbar,C); n and C are never specified; the 47 ms (~1.6 sample) loop delay appears in no model used for any stability statement.
**Why:** User asked specifically which state-space/LPV material need not be in the paper. The unused math carries four of the errors, so cutting it is both free and risk-reducing; the RMSE-minimiser claim matters because it underpins the locked 2026-07-16 RMSE-over-MSE decision.
**Next:** Verify empirically that the AL_0033/AL_0034 grid minimum is unchanged between mean-of-norms and RMS-of-norms scoring (cheap, from the cached grid) so the claim can either be corrected or dropped; then cut LPV + Phi + lifted A/Gamma + augmented state + regret (~90 lines) and decide whether to replace the Astrom stability sentence with a real gain/phase margin from the discretised tfest plant including the delay.

### 2026-09-30 - ⭐ The capture metric has a RANDOM BASELINE. Selection information peaks at K~91-110 and is GONE by K=35
**Changed/Found:** No file edited (scratch, AL_0033, TF mask lineage). Restarted the per-amp pixel-selection line at the user's request with the goal of near-100% capture of dip AND rebound. Four results, in order of importance.
**(1) The TF mask PASSES the [CP-STIMAFF] random control.** TF-selected 91 px vs 12 pre-generated random 91-px subsets: DIP 91% vs random median 79% (range 73-82), REB 34% vs 23% (20-28), beating **12/12 draws on both**. So the 91% is earned. **BUT random 91 px already yields 79%** - only ~12 of the 91 points are attributable to WHICH pixels; the rest is the model degradation you get from any 91-predictor restriction. Capture must therefore be reported against a matched-K random baseline, never alone.
**(2) K-sweep vs matched random** (rank = #amps TF-flagged, tie-break amp-graded drive; random = median of 6 pre-generated draws):
| K | R2 | DIP | REB | catch | rand DIP | rand REB | dDIP | dREB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 140 | 0.950 | 78 | 29 | 0 | 65 | 18 | +13 | +11 |
| 110 | 0.938 | 86 | 29 | -2 | 70 | 19 | **+16** | +10 |
| 91 | 0.931 | 91 | 34 | -2 | 77 | 21 | **+15** | +13 |
| 70 | 0.925 | 95 | 36 | -3 | 88 | 24 | +7 | +12 |
| 50 | 0.911 | 98 | 37 | -2 | 91 | 25 | +7 | +13 |
| 35 | 0.897 | 95 | 35 | -0 | 96 | 29 | **-1** | +7 |
| 25 | 0.888 | 98 | 26 | +1 | 94 | 25 | +4 | +1 |
⚠ **Raw capture reaches 98% at K=50 and K=25, but random reaches 91-96% there too, and at K=35 the gap is NEGATIVE.** Near-100% capture is trivially purchasable by shrinking the predictor set and carries no information. **The catch control does NOT detect this** (it stays -3..+1 throughout) - only the matched-random baseline does. Information peaks at **K~91-110**, i.e. essentially where the TF mask already sits.
**(3) REBOUND capture never exceeds ~37% at ANY K** (and 29% at the random-equivalent point). Pixel selection is exhausted for the rebound; only `subspace` moves it (34 -> 56-59%, at the cost of DIP 91 -> 73-79% and R2 0.931 -> 0.85).
**(4) Naive per-amp candidate sets go the WRONG WAY** and this is now quantified at source: each amp's own unaffected set is 167-442 px vs the pooled intersection's 91, so per-amp selection ENLARGES the candidate pool, Global absorbs more, capture falls. This reproduces the 2026-07-06 diagnosis from the opposite direction. The productive use of per-amp information is a STRICTER pooled set (union of affectedness over amps and windows), not a looser per-amp one.
**Why:** The user's goal of near-perfect capture is reachable on the raw number and meaningless there. Stating the objective correctly - maximise (capture_selected - capture_random) at matched K, subject to catch and held-out R2 - keeps the goal falsifiable and happens to endorse the operating point already in use.
**Next:** ⚠⚠ **Two methodological traps found, both of which silently corrupted an earlier attempt in this same session:**
(a) **`f2_model` RESEEDS the RNG internally** (the 2026-07-07 stim-affected-detection fix). A `randperm` called inside a loop that also calls `f2_model` returns the SAME permutation every iteration - my first random control produced 10 byte-identical "draws". Pre-generate all random subsets BEFORE the loop. Anything in the repo drawing randomness across `f2_model` calls should be audited for this.
(b) **A window-mean score over a ~1 s window is DRIFT-dominated, not stim-driven.** A first `drive` score (worst deflection in dip or rebound window) gave min 2.92 pre-SD across ALL 442 px - i.e. nothing is clean - and overlapped the TF-pooled set in only 7/91 px. Re-deriving it as amp-GRADED (Spearman(amp, score), since drift is not dose-dependent) fixed the pathology but still overlaps TF in only 26/91, and TF candidates' mean drive (0.541) is indistinguishable from all pixels (0.557). **So the TF detector and the dose-monotonicity criterion select nearly independently** while giving 91% vs 70% capture - that disagreement is unexplained and is the next thing to understand before either is trusted as "the" affectedness rule.
Recommended operating point if raw capture matters: **K=70** (DIP 95 / REB 36 / R2 0.925 / catch -3, gaps +7/+12). Otherwise keep K=91.

### 2026-09-30 - AL_0033 high-amp dip + rebound capture: diagnosed. Rebound is NOT fixable by pixel exclusion
**Changed/Found:** No file edited (scratch). User observed dip capture worsening from ~2.7 V up and rebound capture "really bad". Both confirmed and quantified; `Areb/Greb/Lreb` were already computed by `f2_decomp` and had never been reported.
**Per-amp, TF mask + r2max** (dip window and rebound window are DATA-DERIVED per amp, `P.dcc`/`P.rcc`):
| amp | DIPcap% | REBcap% | Areb / Greb / Lreb | dip win (ms) | reb win (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.10 | 110 | 58 | 0.20 / 0.08 / 0.11 | 0-314 | 343-571 |
| 2.70 | 99 | 23 | 0.57 / 0.44 / 0.13 | 0-371 | 400-600 |
| 3.20 | 115 | 38 | 0.67 / 0.41 / 0.25 | 0-229 | 257-1000 |
| 3.70 | 76 | 14 | 0.76 / 0.65 / 0.11 | 0-257 | 286-600 |
| 4.30 | 71 | 29 | 0.69 / 0.49 / 0.20 | 0-257 | 286-943 |
| 4.90 | 84 | 44 | 0.81 / 0.45 / 0.36 | 0-229 | 257-829 |
**median DIP capture 91%, median REBOUND capture 34%.**
**Structural gap identified:** every affectedness criterion in the repo scores pixels on the DIP - `f2_affected_detect` scores over `P.dcc` and the TF detector thresholds the suppression - so the predictor set is blind to the dip by construction and blind to the rebound by nothing.
**Three fixes tested:**
(1) **Rebound-aware mask** (prototype: score each pixel over `P.rcc` via the same `ctrl_affected_detect` call, gate on amp-graded rebound `Spearman(amp,rebScore)>=thr` AND peak rebound, union with the TF mask). Result: **DIP capture 91 -> 96%** (thr 0.5 / peak 6, 81 candidates, R2 0.926, catch -2%) but **REBOUND capture 34 -> 37% at best**. A free win on the dip; does nothing for the rebound.
(2) **`select_mode='subspace'`** (basis over the whole evoked trajectory, onset->end of rebound, so it penalises the rebound too): **REBOUND 34 -> 56-59%**, but DIP falls 91 -> 73-79% and spont R2 0.931 -> 0.85-0.87. Catch stays clean (-1%). nu barely matters over 0.80-0.99.
(3) **`frontier@0.90`**: DIP 90%, REBOUND 33% - no rebound effect at all, confirming the frontier penalty is dip-specific.
**Why:** The rebound resists pixel surgery because it is BRAIN-WIDE: the per-pixel rebound score has median **3.93 pre-SD across all 442 contra grid pixels** (185 of them amp-graded), so excluding the most rebound-carrying pixels leaves the rest still carrying it. This is the THIRD independent instance of the 2026-07-06 distributed-direction result (after greedy pruning and the all-pixels control). Global absorbing ~66% of the rebound is therefore mostly correct, not a modelling failure.
**Next:** (1) ⚠ **A contra-vs-ipsi rebound ratio I computed is UNRELIABLE - do not quote it.** Raw it gave contra/ipsi 8.85, but at 0.5 V (a no-response amp) contra still "rebounded" +3.6, i.e. slow drift not stim response; catch-correcting left the sign flipping across amplitudes (-2.6 at 1.1 V, +4.6 at 2.7, -0.5 at 3.2, +5.8 at 4.3). The contra grid spatial mean is drift-dominated over a ~1 s window. A usable version needs per-trial drift removal, not a pre-window mean subtraction. (2) Recommend ADOPTING the rebound-aware mask for the dip (96%/-2% catch, costs 0.005 of R2) and reporting rebound capture honestly as a limitation rather than chasing it with `subspace`, since the paper's locked metric is inhibition energy 0-200 ms. (3) Note the dip windows are data-derived and span 229-943 ms across amps (0-943 ms at 0.5 V), so "capture" is not measured over a constant window - the 6 responding amps are 229-371 ms and roughly comparable, but this should be stated wherever per-amp capture is compared. (4) `f2_affected_detect` could take a `window` option ('dip'|'rebound'|'both') so the prototype becomes a supported path.

### 2026-09-30 - RECOVERED the 91/9 stim-blind model on AL_0033: it was the TF mask, lost to the 2026-09-10 recommit
**Changed/Found:** `impulse-analysis/imp_supp_residual.m` - new knob `SUPP_MASK` ('tf' default | 'committed'). User recalled "almost perfect stim blindness" on this session; that memory is CORRECT and it was not the tautological NATIVE/KKT model. Loading the pre-existing TF mask (`data/tf_sens_AL_0033_0129_e1.mat`, tf_sens 2.15, confirmed 2026-08-10 15:33) and running the identical honest chain reproduces the 2026-08-12 record exactly:

| mask | per-amp affected (of 442) | spont R2 | cap% | leak% | catch% | nPred |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TF (pre 09-10) | 0 0 2 48 13 35 177 249 275 | 0.931 | **91** | **9** | -2 | 91 |
| committed monotone (09-10) | 306 x9 (flat) | 0.958 | 70 | 30 | -2 | 136 |

Root cause: `f2_affected` PREFERS a committed rank selection over the TF mask whenever `data/f2_affsel_<sess>.mat` exists, and that file was written 2026-09-10 16:12:48 - so the 91/9 configuration was silently superseded, not re-tuned away. **Mechanism of the 21-point gap: the TF detector is AMPLITUDE-GRADED** (excludes ~nothing at 0.5-1.1 V, 275 px at 4.9 V), which is the physically correct bleed signature (bleed scales with power, absent <=1.1 V / present >=1.6 V, RESEARCH 2026-07-06); the monotone rule applies one flat pooled cut at every amplitude. Catch is -2% under BOTH, so neither manufactures residual.
**Why:** ⚠ **This partly RETRACTS my 2026-09-30 claim that "per-amp pixel selection is not a knob / means per-amp refits."** That is wrong for this mechanism: the TF detector is per-amp in DETECTION only, and `f2_affected` still collapses it via `unaff_pooled = find(all(~aff,2))` to ONE candidate set, so the model keeps a single weight vector deployed unchanged at every amplitude and per-amp leak stays comparable. The user's per-amp instinct was right; the 2026-07-06 failure was per-amp selection of CLEAN pixels (keeping more where bleed is worst), which is the opposite operation. The earlier entry's other conclusions (frontier = fitted target; all-pixels control -> 7% capture; distributed-direction) stand unchanged.
**Next:** ⚠⚠ **FORKING-PATH EXPOSURE, must be carried in the caption.** The mask swap also moved the state test: rel-delta Local **+0.059 p=.105 -> +0.119 p=.0012** with its Global control going null/opposite (+0.020 -> -0.031), i.e. n.s. -> "genuinely local" (matches the earlier leak-minimised result, Local +0.071 > Global +0.022). Motion's CONCLUSION is unchanged (Global control larger than Local under both masks -> network-wide). The mask was selected on CAPTURE, and the capture comparison was run and logged before the state numbers were read - that ordering is the defence - but a single-session effect that appears only under one blindness model, does NOT survive 4-session pooling (z=+0.79 p=.43) and did NOT replicate on AB_0004 must be reported with BOTH masks' numbers or not at all. Decide: (a) does the TF mask or the monotone rule become this session's operating point of record, and (b) if TF, does the 2026-09-10 recommit need revisiting for the other sessions too - it was adopted for cross-session robustness, which is a weaker consideration in a single-session panel but the governing one for the pooled work.

### 2026-09-30 - Grant panels raised 8 pt -> 14 pt BOLD; at that size the label TEXT is the constraint, not the font
**Changed/Found:** `grid_panels.py`, `macaque_lti_fit_single.py`, `macaque_io_2panel.py`, `make_fig11_panels.m` - grant profiles re-set to **14 pt bold labels / 10 pt bold ticks** (user: "almost double, use bold"). Matplotlib has no weight arg on `tick_params`, so tick labels are bolded by iterating `get_xticklabels()/get_yticklabels()`. What doubling actually costs, measured on a 1.83 cm panel (51.9 x 48.6 pt): one line of 14 pt text is ~29% of the panel HEIGHT, and a ROTATED y-label is bounded by the plot-box height (~33 pt), so "$\Delta$F/F %" at 14 pt is ~48 pt and clips. Consequences, all forced rather than chosen: y-labels cut to a single glyph (`%`, `$\mu$V`); x-labels dropped entirely with the unit moved onto the end tick (`0.6 s`, `150 Hz`, `5 ms`); the end tick anchored `ha='right'` so it cannot overhang; only the END tick labelled on the grid traces after `0` + `0.6 s` collided into "006 s" in a ~26 pt plot box; macaque panel-B legend dropped (12 pt over a 2.83 cm panel covered the data); pulse-width ticks cut to the two endpoints; PID paired panels lost their y-label and the p-value title moved to 10 pt.
**Why:** Nick's "way too small" was not satisfied by 8 pt in the user's judgement. Layout is fixed (wrapfigure widths are final), so the only knob left is type size, and above ~10 pt the panels can hold type OR decoration, not both.
**Next:** none - all three figures re-rendered from the live draft, 15 pages, zero LaTeX errors, no clipping or tick collision at 400-600 dpi. If 14 pt ever has to coexist with full axis labels, the panels must get wider; at 1.8-2.9 cm this is the ceiling.

### 2026-09-30 - Fig-2 E: M1b tau marker is drawn OUTSIDE its own bootstrap CI
**Changed/Found:** In `tf_tau_forest` (panel E) the lines are 95% bootstrap CIs on each time constant (resample trials within amplitude -> rebuild amp-averages -> refit; `tauCI = [prctile(tauBoot,2.5) prctile(tauBoot,97.5)]`, `imp_tf_fit_session.m:273-305`). For M1b (AL_0041 2025-12-02 e2) the full-data estimate is tau1 = 0.540 s but its CI is [155, 502] ms, so the filled marker sits past the right end of its own line. Cause: the CI is computed only over resamples that survive the `tauMax` identifiability cut (tau > fit-window ~0.51 s rejected), and **50% of M1b resamples were rejected** - the survivors are therefore systematically faster than the full-data fit. Rejection rates this run: M1a 42%, M1b 50%, M2 2%, M3 50%.
**Why:** Noticed while answering what the lines represent. Not a plotting bug and not a bad cut - the tauMax bound exists because a time constant longer than the observation window is genuinely unidentifiable (see the block comment at `imp_tf_fit_session.m:286`) - but a point estimate outside its own error bar is exactly the kind of thing a referee stops on.
**Next:** Pick one: (a) caption sentence stating the CI is over identifiable resamples only and quoting the rejection fraction per session, (b) plot the bootstrap MEDIAN instead of the full-data fit so the marker is inside the interval by construction, or (c) mark the high-rejection sessions (M1a/M1b/M3, all >=42%) as CI-not-identifiable and drop their lines.

### 2026-09-30 - Answered: what the shading in imp_state_var_combined is, and why Abs-delta has none
**Changed/Found:** The band is the **bootstrap 95% CI** (STVF_NBOOT = 2000 resamples) on the per-quartile SD of deviation, computed in `local_binci`. It is only computed for **admissible** markers - `adm = find([R.adm])` = Motion and Rel-delta. Abs-delta is classed "CONFOUND - not interpreted", so it is not in `adm`; at the combined-panel draw the lookup `ip = find(adm==k,1)` comes back empty and the code falls back to `ciLo = ciHi = yv`, i.e. a zero-width band. So the missing shading is not a plotting bug - it is the confound flag showing through. Separately: the three tiles are `linkaxes`-ed to a common y, and Abs-delta Q4 exceeds that range, so its last point is drawn off the top of the axes.
**Why:** User asked directly ("abs delta does not appear to have the shading around it, what is the shading?"). Worth recording because the panel silently looks like a rendering fault.
**Next:** Decide one of: (a) leave it and say so in the caption, (b) compute a CI for Abs-delta too so all three carry a band, or (c) drop Abs-delta from the panel. Independently, the clipped Q4 point needs either a wider shared y-limit or an unlinked axis for that tile.

### 2026-09-30 - AL_0033 leak is an IDENTIFIABILITY LIMIT, not a tuning failure (far-from-ipsi prior sweep + all-pixels control)
**Changed/Found:** No file edited - scratch sweep, prompted by the user proposing to cut leak via parameter adjustment, per-amp pixel selection and a relaxed R². Two results, both decisive.
(1) **The far-from-ipsi prior barely bites.** `penNear` swept 2 -> 64 (a 32x change, `penFar`=0.2, `r2max`, 136 candidate px): spont R² **0.958 -> 0.957** (flat), capture **70 -> 76%**, leak 30 -> 24%, catch -2 -> -3%, and the `|w|`-weighted mean weight distance from the ipsi site moves **269.6 -> 275.6 px (+2%)**. RESEARCH 2026-08-05 set the diagnostic in advance: "if weight distance does NOT rise with ridge, the prior is not biting". It does not - the predictive weight already sits ~270 px out and there is nowhere further to push it. Free ~6 points of capture at zero R² cost, and then the lever is exhausted.
(2) **The all-pixels control is the real finding.** Bypassing the detector mask entirely (`use_affected=false`, all 442 grid px, penalty alone must achieve blindness): spont R² **0.996** - the best fit in the whole study - but capture collapses to **7%** and leak to **93%**. This reproduces the user's own 2026-07-06 diagnosis exactly: hand the optimiser every contra pixel and Global absorbs essentially the entire ipsi dip. So the 30% leak is not a knob setting; it is how much of the ipsi dip is genuinely reconstructible from contralateral cortex, and the detector mask is what buys the 70% capture in the first place.
**Why:** "Leak is too high" reads as a tuning problem and it is not one. Per RESEARCH 2026-08-05, greedy pruning already failed to recover capture because the stim-predictive signal is a **distributed direction, not an identifiable pixel set** - drop a pixel and the refit reallocates its weight to correlated neighbours ([CP-KRECON]). The all-pixels control is the clean demonstration of that.
**Next:** **~30% leak is the regime the project already independently landed on** - RESEARCH 2026-08-05 cites [CP-CLEANRES] (S13, RRR lineage) holding the residual at ~73% of the actual dip and names "~30% leak is the regime to aim at". Today's 70/30 sits on that benchmark, so the current number is corroborated, not deficient. Decide whether to adopt `penNear=64` (76%/24%, R² unchanged, catch -3%) as the supplement's op-point - it is an honest lever (formed without reference to the dip) but the gain is marginal. PER-AMP PIXEL SELECTION IS NOT A KNOB: `f2_model` fits ONE weight vector deployed unchanged at every amplitude (`f2_decomp`: "the SAME weight vector at every amplitude"), so per-amp selection means per-amp refits, i.e. re-choosing the predictor against each amplitude's own dip - capture becomes partly fitted again, which is the 2026-07-18 NATIVE/KKT objection returning by another route. If it is still wanted, build it as an explicitly-labelled exploratory variant, never as the supplement's primary.

### 2026-09-29 — Row-2 two-metric state analysis: OL trend / CL trend / gap-change per state (LMM)
**Changed/Found:** New `scratchpad f4_row2_trends.m` (saved `data/f4_row2_trends.mat`) — from the SAME session-aware LMM `y ~ cond*xw + (1+cond|sess) + (1|mouse)` (y = settled **1–3 s** rejection RMSE, RAW; xw = within-session-centered state, pooled-SD scaled), extracts OL trend (xw main effect, OL-ref), **CL trend** (xw main effect, CL-ref refit), gap-change (cond_CL:xw decoupling), and CL advantage@mean (cond_CL). β in z-RMSE per +1 SD state; β>0 = worse. Results (β, p): **init-dev** OL +0.226 (5e-7), CL +0.172 (1e-4), gap-change −0.054 (0.39 n.s.); **motion** OL +0.203 (9e-5), CL −0.009 (0.86 n.s.), gap-change −0.212 (0.004); **rel 2-4Hz** OL +0.045 (0.34 n.s.), CL +0.198 (6e-6), gap-change +0.152 (0.018); **abs δ** OL +0.450 (3e-26), CL +0.460 (1e-26), gap-change +0.009 (0.88 n.s.). CL keeps a large constant advantage everywhere (cond_CL −0.73…−0.88, all p<1e-6). Confirms all four verbal reads: init-dev = parallel worsening (gap constant); motion = OL worsens while CL is flat/immune (gap widens → controllable); rel-δ = OL flat, CL worsens (gap shrinks); abs-δ = both worsen equally (gap constant, biggest disturbance).
**Why:** User asked to report each state on two metrics — OL-CL gap change Q1→Q4 and CL trend Q1→Q4 — and to verify the per-state interpretation before finalizing the figure.
**Next:** Decide on-panel annotation (gap-change p + CL-trend p) to replace the removed cond×state tag; possibly a FINDINGS.md entry once the narrative is locked.

### 2026-09-21 — Tube-MPC metric → ABSOLUTE RMSE + forecast-quality axis (fixes "all models collapse to Naive")
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/ctrl_tube_mpc.m` — switched the y-axis from ratio-to-PI to **absolute residual RMSE (%ΔF/F)** (the project-locked metric) with **PI and clairvoyant-floor reference lines**, and recast the uncertainty axis: disturbance scale now FIXED at σ_nat while the swept variable is **forecast error level** e (0=perfect → σ_nat=Naive), so models spread by skill instead of piling up. rollR reworked: controller now OBSERVES the sampled realization + forecast error (std e·ρ, new `feError`), separating disturbance magnitude (σ_nat) from forecast quality (e). Both sweeps put on common random numbers so they agree at shared configs (quality@PatchTST 0.889 ↔ window@1s 0.890 — previously disagreed 0.89 vs 1.05 from independent seeds; the absolute RMSE median is gain-dominated/heavy-tailed so needs CRN). **Why the ratio collapsed:** (i) at 1 s lead the Lu models are only ~10–20% better than Naive (Fig 1c MWQL 0.80–1.0) so they genuinely cluster, and (ii) the ratio metric + σ_u floor washed out even that, and (iii) σ-placement crammed them into a tiny x-band. **Result (nMC=150):** MPC ≈**0.89 %ΔF/F** vs PI **1.22** (visible ~27% gain) with clairvoyant floor **0**; the 0.89→0 gap is ENTIRELY actuator-gain uncertainty σ_u=0.40; forecast quality curve flat 0.889→0.890; window idealized falls 0.16→0 by 200 ms. Models now spread along the skill axis (PatchTST 0.80 → Naive 1.0), clustered near the Naive end — honestly showing forecasters ≈ Naive at 1 s.
**Why:** User: "why is increasing uncertainty vs rmse a flat graph?" / "what would be a better performance metric" / "all models have collapsed to naive." The ratio metric divided out the swept scale; absolute RMSE with reference lines + a forecast-quality x-axis fixes both.
**Next:** The realistic curves are still flat because σ_u dominates — if we want forecast quality/preview to visibly matter, revisit σ_u (0.40 is an upper bound; the purely-multiplicative part is likely ~0.2). ### 2026-09-21 — Tube-MPC → REALIZATION-BASED, two figures, full Lu et al. model field
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/ctrl_tube_mpc.m` — reformulated the analysis and cut to two figures (user: "only two figures forecast window vs MPC and uncertainty level vs MPC"; "create a realization based MPC where each time we just sample from within the uncertainty windows and run MPC rather than use ideal disturbance and put a uncertainty band on it"). (1) REALIZATION-BASED: each MC trial now draws an actual disturbance realization d_real = dbar + σ·w (w = smoothed unit-var field) and runs the full MPC on it; within the forecast window L_p the controller sees the departure attenuated by forecast skill (1−ρ, Lu et al.), beyond L_p it falls back to the mean forecast; PI faces the SAME realization (CRN) so the ratio is per-realization; the 5–95% band is now the empirical spread over realizations, not an imposed tube. New nested `drawW`/`rollR` replace `roll`/`feStep`. (2) Dropped the example-rollout figure (`tubempc_example.png` deleted); kept `tubempc_improvement.png` (uncertainty level vs MPC) and `tubempc_horizon.png` (forecast window vs MPC). **Result (nMC=150):** realistic residual flat ≈**0.73×PI** (uncertainty axis) and ≈**0.84×PI** (window axis); idealized (perfect actuator) rises 0→0.06 with σ and falls 0.13→0.05 as the forecast window grows to ~200 ms. Even sampling real disturbance realizations, σ_u=0.40 sets the realistic residual; forecast window/uncertainty only bite once the actuator gain is known (idealized curves).
**Why:** A realization-based MC is more honest than "run on the mean + draw a band" — the residual distribution emerges from actual sampled disturbances, and PI/MPC face identical realizations. Two figures match the two-fold spec directly.
**Next:** Fixed a nested-function scope bug found by Code Analyzer — `drawW` had a local `m` that aliased the sweep loop index `m` (nested funcs share parent workspace) → renamed to `mk/zz/wout`; would have mis-indexed `aI/aR`. Consider tightening the wide 5–95% realization band (per-realization ratio ~0.1–1.0) to an IQR if it reads as alarming.

### 2026-09-21 — ARTIFACT: AL_0041 custom_uval sessions have laser bleed at the on/off edges
**Changed/Found:** All 4 AL_0041 OL-optimized replay sessions (the `ol_opt_replay_batch.m` set) show a laser-bleed transient at the stim boundaries in `states.csv`. On m4=2026-03-24/e1, CL mean: baseline −0.13 → **+0.42 at t≈+0.086 s** (positive spike, ~2–3 frames) before the real inhibitory dip; a smaller **negative** transient ~2 frames after offset (t≈+3.09 s, −0.31). Confirmed as direct bleed (not neural) by `stateraw.csv`: **raw F steps 244.3→245.6 at laser onset** — 594 nm light into the sensor. Bleed adds a POSITIVE offset, so the sustained dip to −2 is genuine (can't be manufactured downward), but the edges are contaminated on every trial. No standard temporal artifact correction exists in the pipeline (`getpixel_dFoF` does none; `cp_bleed_control` is spatial contra→ipsi leakage, unrelated). No laser-off/catch (amp-0) condition inside these sessions to measure bleed magnitude directly.
**Why:** User flagged "all these suffered from laser artifact issues" on the replay plots; verified against raw F.
**Next:** Decide mitigation — (a) linear-interp the ~2–3 boundary frames at on/off, (b) start the RMSE/error window ~+0.15 s post-onset to skip the transient, (c) treat these sessions as contaminated/deprioritize. ### 2026-09-21 — Fig-4 disturbance rejection: RE-LOCK metric to phi=1-RR (Global referenced to 0)
**Changed/Found:** `imp_reject_core.m` (+`R.rejPHI_ol/cl` = 1-median(RR_1-3s), new HEADLINE; `rejER` kept for reference), `f4_contra_model.m` panel c, `f4_disturb_rejection.m` panel 5 — switched the disturbance denominator from `||G-ref||^2` (1-ER, locked 2026-09-19) to **`||G||^2` (phi=1-RR, G referenced to 0)**. RR_settled==rho^2, so all three read the cached per-trial `Q.rho_ol/rho_cl` — **no SVD rebuild**. Result (settled 1-3 s, n=13): median **OL -0.216 -> CL +0.226, CL>OL 12/13, signrank p=4.9e-4** (matches the pre-09-19 phi=1-RR numbers). Two OL sessions read strongly negative (AL_0051 -3.52, AL_0033_0415_e2 -2.12) and are clipped to a floor marker in both panels; phi in [-1.1, 0.8] view.
**Why:** User: "the disturbance rejection setup is wrong the ref used for global seems to be 5 but it should have been 0." Physically G is the stim-blind counterfactual sitting at the no-laser baseline (~0), so the disturbance's own excursion energy is Global-minus-0; referencing G to ref folds the setpoint-tracking offset into the "disturbance" and over-estimates it. Accepts the trade-off (phi unbounded below) that 1-ER was chosen on 09-19 to avoid. ⚠ NOTE: the Sept-15 Nick meeting note records the rejection metric as "finalized 0-1 energy ratio" (= bounded 1-ER); this reversal to phi=1-RR is OL-negative on 2 sessions and should be reconciled with Nick.
**Next:** Reconcile manuscript results.tex/methods (Panel-C text + caption) to phi=1-RR, G ref 0 (OL -0.22 -> CL +0.23, 12/13); flag the OL-negative sessions in the caption; confirm with Nick given the Sept-15 "0-1 ratio" note.

### 2026-09-18 — Fig-4 rejection metric: investigate the unbounded φ; two bounded session-wise options
**Changed/Found:** new `controller-analysis/f4_reject_metric_compare.m` (preview only) + cache `data/ctrl_rejectB_sessionwise.mat`. Diagnosed why φ=1−RR goes to −6.3: RR=‖A−ref‖²/‖G‖² has the numerator referenced to `ref` but the denominator to ZERO, so when a session's shared disturbance ‖G‖² is small vs the stim-driven setpoint error, RR≫1 → φ hugely negative (a normalization artifact, NOT "OL amplified"). Session-wise φ_OL ranges +0.31 down to −6.28 (AL_0051). Two BOUNDED alternatives, computed **session-wise (no pooling) with per-session bootstrap CIs (2000×)**: (A) **1−ER**, ER=‖A−ref‖²/‖G−ref‖² (both ref'd) — strictly [0,1], CL>OL **13/13**, signrank p=2.4e-4, but absolute level is setpoint-tracking-inflated (OL≈0.71, CL 0.80; only the gap is meaningful). (B) **CL-vs-OL** = 1−med(‖A_cl−ref‖²)/med(‖A_ol−ref‖²) on the RAW regulated ipsi (settled 1–3 s, from pnc/pwc buffered traces, no Global/SVD) — OL=baseline(0), median **0.52**, **12/13 >0**, **10/13 with 95% CI excluding 0**; lone non-rejector AL_0048 (CI spans 0). B ≈ Fig-3 RMSE result in the settled window (drops the contra model); A keeps the contra decomposition.
**Why:** User: "the rejection should stay within 0 to 1 ... open loop should not make things worse" + "not pooled always session wise with validation." φ=1−RR failed both (unbounded, OL artefact-negative).

### 2026-09-15 — Tube-MPC: measured σ_u from OL, ratio metric, response tubes, horizon cap — actuator-gain uncertainty DOMINATES
**Changed/Found:** Major `ctrl_tube_mpc.m` rework per user. (1) **σ_u MEASURED from open-loop trials** (was illustrative 0.15): per-trial best-fit gain scale on the 92 OL responses → CV=0.40, noise-corrected 0.40 (noise contribution negligible) → real ~40% trial-to-trial actuator-gain variability. Confirmed plant IS already OL-identified (`ctrl_lti_sysid.m`, ssest on designed OL step+dither) — no CL-identification bias. (2) Gain modelled **lognormal** (mean 1, CV=σ_u, always positive — fixes Gaussian sign-flips that blew up short horizons/tube). (3) **Metric → residual RMSE ratio** RMSE_MPC/RMSE_PI (PI=1, lower better), replacing "% improvement" (user: 100% misleading + perfect preview can't be perfect since actuator dynamics/gain must be respected). (4) Input uncertainty now ALWAYS on in realistic curves (idealized perfect-actuator shown faint) → perfect preview ≠ 0. (5) **Horizon capped at 1 s** [0.15..1.0]; realistic curve FLAT ~0.82 (receding horizon applies first move only → near-term dominates → look-ahead past ~150 ms neither helps nor hurts; answers "why not worse past 1s"). (6) Example rebuilt with **TUBES around the response** (5-95% MC envelope) not a jitter trace; per-trial (not median-trace) residual. (7) Common-random-numbers across sweep points for stable medians (nMC=150; median was unstable at 80 under σ_u=0.40). **HEADLINE RESULT:** with measured σ_u=0.40, realistic forecaster residual **0.84×PI (~16% less error)**, perfect-forecast **0.75**, idealized perfect-actuator **~0.25** — so the gap 0.25→0.84 is ALL actuator-gain uncertainty; **forecast quality is second-order, actuator-gain variability is the dominant limiter.** Much more sober than the earlier 70-88% (which ignored actuator uncertainty).
**Why:** User asks this session: use OL input variance for σ_u; show tubes around the response; cap horizon 1 s; switch to a ratio metric; the 100% looked wrong. Diagnosed the 100%: clairvoyant RMSE→0 because no constraint binds in-window AND the sim gives a perfect plant model (d defined via same H) — an idealization, resolved by always carrying the measured σ_u.
**Next:** ⚠ σ_u=0.40 is the TOTAL OL-response CV — an UPPER bound; part is state-dependent disturbance already in d (double-count), so the purely-multiplicative σ_u is likely lower (~0.2?), which would move the balance back toward forecasting mattering. To separate cleanly, regress per-trial OL response amplitude on input amplitude (needs varying-amplitude OL). The "actuator-gain uncertainty dominates" conclusion → biggest lever over PI is state-aware gain control (the GDM per-state controllers), not a better forecaster — strong input to Nick's main-vs-supplemental call (leans supplemental). Still pending Ziyu σ on CL data (09-11.4).

**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/ctrl_tube_mpc.m` reworked. (1) **Lead-time-dependent forecast error**: preview error std at lead τ = fSkill·σ_nat·ρ(τ), where ρ(τ) is Lu et al. ### 2026-09-11 — MPC metric discrepancy (Nick 2026-09-11.3): diagnosis = full-window RMSE dominated by shared irreducible floor
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/ctrl_tube_mpc.m` — DIAGNOSED (not yet fixed) why clairvoyant σ=0 (~38%) ≈ σ=0.3 (~36%) despite visibly different traces. Metric (`:86`) is improvement = 100·(RMSE_PI−RMSE_MPC)/RMSE_PI with `rmse` over the FULL 0..dur window. Both the PI baseline and every MPC rollout incur the SAME irreducible components: (i) the onset inhibitory/delay transient (0–1 s, uncontrollable — loop delay), and (ii) samples where the disturbance already sits below ref (one-sided actuation 0≤u≤u_max ⇒ u=0 optimal, no control can help). These shared chunks sit identically in numerator and denominator, dominate the full-window RMSE, and SWAMP the settled-region differences (1–3 s) where clairvoyant is near-ref and σ=0.3 misses — compressing all improvements into a narrow ~36–38% band. So the near-equality is a metric-window artifact, not a calc error in `roll`.
**Why:** Nick flagged the two numbers shouldn't be near-equal given the traces; the meeting AI analysis pointed at the denominator/integration window. On a linear plant a clairvoyant preview should approach ~0 settled error, so 38% signals the window includes uncontrollable periods.
**Next:** (a) recompute improvement on the SETTLED window t=+1..+3 s (matches the CLAUDE.md disturbance-rejection window) — expect clairvoyant→high, σ=0.3→clearly lower, separation restored; (b) report the irreducible floor = fraction of window samples with dbar<ref; (c) confirm num/denom share window+ref; only if clairvoyant STILL isn't ~near-perfect on the settled window is there a genuine bug in `roll` (tube tightening / lam / delay double-count). Tracked in TASKS 🆕 MPC section.

### 2026-09-11 — Fig 4 Row 3: new PRIMARY rejection metric SR = fluctuation-energy ratio (frame-consistent)
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/imp_reject_core.m` — added metric SR = ‖A−⟨A⟩‖²/‖G−⟨G⟩‖², each signal centred on its OWN within-window mean per trial (fields `sr_ol/cl`, sub-window `_tr`/`_rej`, pooled `srP_*`, `rej_frac_* = 1−srP`, `p_sr`, `p_sr_*1`). Marked PRIMARY (2026-09-11), demoting ER; ER + RHO retained for reproducibility. Static-check clean.
**Why:** User flagged both existing denominators are ill-posed: G is the *no-stim* counterfactual, sits at baseline ≈0, while A is held at ref=−5. ER's ‖G−ref‖² is dominated by the constant (0−ref)² offset ⇒ measures setpoint tracking, not disturbance rejection; RHO's ‖G‖² mixes a ref-centred numerator with a zero-centred denominator (frame mismatch). Centring each signal on its own mean removes the arbitrary DC from both, leaving only the state-driven fluctuation ⇒ SR = empirical closed-loop sensitivity |S|²; 1−SR = fraction of disturbance fluctuation rejected. Not circular despite A=G+L: SR<1 requires controller action L anti-correlated with G (the rejection signature); OL ⇒ SR≈1.
**Next:** Wire SR into `f4_reject_panels.m` (paired OL/CL panel + vector PDF export) so Row 3 regenerates from committed code; recompute across the 13 sessions and report signrank. Update PAPER.md Fig-4 section (still says ρ=‖A−ref‖/‖G‖) to the SR framing.

The plant-inversion disturbance `d = y_PI − H·u_PI` (H from `ctrl_plant_markov`, plant `ctrl_lti_*`, output `ctrl_ols_cl_deploy_.AaAbs`) does **NOT** track the contra-predicted Global `G`: **corr(d,G) = −0.32**, while the two OUTPUT estimates agree (corr(y_PI, mean Acl)=0.97). Root cause: the plant's modeled laser effect `H·u_PI` (mean −6.6%, to −7.6) and the contra-stream Local `A−G` (mean −2.5%, to −3.0) are the **same shape (corr 0.95) but differ ~2.6× in gain** — so `d = y−H·u` (mean +0.96) and `G` (mean −1.57) are offset/anti-correlated. The ridge Global's known leak (understated Local) explains part but not a 2.6× factor. Deflate/softblind Stage-2 caches for m4 DO exist on disk (`ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind_{deflate,softblind}_AL_0033_0226_e2.mat`), so the drift-removed reconciliation is testable.
**Why:** User's from-scratch optimal controller = "use the contra Global as the causal disturbance estimate" + "reuse Stage-4a plant". Those two only compose if the plant disturbance `d` and the contra `G` live in the same frame — they don't yet, so the preview premise needs reconciliation before any controller is built.
**Next:** DECISION for user (surfaced): (a) reconcile via drift-removed/deflate G (test whether A−G_deflate ≈ H·u), (b) re-fit the plant laser gain to the contra frame, or (c) reformulate so disturbance ≡ G and identify a u→Local plant. Do NOT build the controller until the frame is settled.

### 2026-09-11 — Motion state → MEAN RECTIFIED movement across all of Figure 4 (both rows)
**Changed/Found:** Replaced the motion metric everywhere in Fig 4 with **mean(max(motion,0))** over the −2→+3 s stim-trial window (was mean z-motion², "energy"). Diagnosed why the choice mattered: `d.ncmotion` is a sparse bursty movement index (min −0.97, max +21, 89% of frames at a small negative no-move floor, top 10% of frames carry 41% of all motion). mean² over-weights single spikes (a 21-spike → 441), giving skewness 13 and reshuffling **64% of trials' quartiles** (mean-vs-mean² Spearman only 0.22) — that is what flipped the motion Q3 CL mean between iterations (−0.18 worst → −0.41 best; Q3 was 87% different trials). Rectified mean is **linear** ("amount of movement", distance-like not energy-like), skewness 4.7, ranks with energy at Spearman 0.78 = stable. Applied in `f4_partB_panels.m` (X2) and `f4_row2_quartiles.m` (S.motion), titles "Motion energy"→"Motion". **Effects — row 1:** motion unique R² 0.001→0.005 (still negligible); init-dev 0.381/0.030 and rel 2-4 Hz 0.083/0.111 essentially unchanged; R²_full 0.41/0.14; shared −0.059/−0.009. **Row 2:** motion interaction β=−0.178, t=−3.24, **p=0.0012 \*\*** (strengthened from p=0.010); init-dev n.s. and delta \* unchanged. OL rises monotonically with movement (+0.22→+0.60); CL bins still wiggle (motion is intrinsically bursty) but the gap-grows headline is robust.
**Why:** User: "capture amount of movement in the stim trial window, suggest the better metric" → "plug in mean rectified motion and redo." Amount of movement is a distance (linear) question, not kinetic energy (squared).
**Next:** Row-1 panels A (title) + C (R²) not re-exported — locked by an open preview; re-run when free (change is cosmetic). Rethink the shared-variance Venn (user) — its baked numbers shifted slightly (2-4 Hz 0.09→0.08 / 0.12→0.11); update or replace with the variance-partition (explained+unexplained) bar.

### 2026-09-10 — f2_affected_detect: amp-vs-effect MONOTONICITY gate replaces the busted rank auto-K
**Changed/Found:** User rejected the rank + spont-R²-floor AUTO-K as "busted" and pointed to better criteria (the biphasic-TF detector that worked for s3=AL_0033, and the amp-vs-effect monotonicity gate). Rebuilt `utils/f2_affected_detect.m` around the MONOTONICITY gate as the new DEFAULT (`method='monotone'`): a pixel is stim-affected iff Spearman(amplitude, per-amp dip) ≤ −mono_thr AND it dips at the strongest amp — the physically correct bleed signature (bleed/coupling scale with power; the amp-graded signal cp_stimaffect [CP-BLEED] tests), needing no per-session absolute threshold. `least_affected` (rank+auto-K) and `dip` (absolute) kept as comparison methods. Rebuilt `f2_affected_gui.m`: method popup + slider whose role adapts (mono_thr / K / dip_thr), map coloured by the gate score, a distribution panel showing where the gate cuts (or the R²-vs-K curve for least_affected), click-a-pixel → its per-amp dose-response (exactly what the gate scores). Verified all three methods run end-to-end on synthetic P (monotone correctly needs ≥3 amps → 0 affected on the 2-amp mock; least_affected keep=15; dip runs); `check_matlab_code` clean.
**Why:** The impulse (unlike controller sessions where a gate deletes 70-99%) has genuinely unaffected pixels, so a physically-grounded GATE beats the controller's rank+R²-floor paradigm I had ported. The monotonicity criterion is what the user named as previously working.

Pooling: SESSION as unit, Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 13 (mean OL, mean CL) pairs + median across-session ratio. RESULT: **[+1,+3]s OL 2.52±0.20 vs CL 1.73±0.20, median 1.48×, p=2.4e-4, CL better in 13/13**; [0,+3]s 1.29×, p=2.4e-4 (smaller effect — the transient the controller can't pre-empt dilutes it). p=2.4e-4 is the n=13 signed-rank floor (all pairs same sign). Two AL_0033 early sessions (m1 0120, m2 0212) are the weakest (ratio 1.11–1.34, within-session rank-sum ns) and the highest-OL-RMSE. Figures → paper/images/figure3/disturbance_rejection_{persession,pooled}.png (PNG, not a committed panel yet).
**Why:** User asked for a per-session + pooled disturbance-rejection analysis. Confirmed choices: windowed RMSE [+1,+3]s, 13 sessions, paired-across-sessions.
**Next:** If it becomes a paper panel, switch export to PDF + paperStyle and decide OL/CL trace context panel. Consider a motion-excluded (motThresh 1.5) robustness pass. Possibly tie to the Global/Local decomposition (does CL shrink Local, i.e. the laser's own effect, or add corrective input?).

### 2026-09-05 — Model tuner (ctrl_softblind_tuner.m) + BETTER op-rule 'minleak' → 0430 leak 0.59→0.07; n=5 reachable
**Changed/Found:** Built **`controller-analysis/ctrl_softblind_tuner.m`** `[SOFTTUNE]` — an interactive cockpit over ALL 11 cached `_softblind` sessions: two sliders (R² floor = usability gate, held-out-leak target = honesty gate) drive a live count of usable sessions + a per-session bar (ridge R²) and honesty-frontier scatter (ridge R² vs achievable held-out leak). Feasible(F,T) = ridgeR2≥F AND min|held-out leak| over the curve points with R2≥F ≤ T. **The tuner exposed two things.** (1) **The paper's N is a policy, not a fixed number:** floor 0.85/leak 0.30 → **3** usable (0212/0224/0430); floor 0.80 → 6 clear the floor but still only 3 usable (added 3 can't blind below 0.30); floor **0.75/leak 0.30 → 5** usable (adds 0226 at leak 0.30 and 0420·AL0039 at 0.20 — a lower floor gives MORE blinding budget so their honest leak drops under the gate). (2) **The held-out leak is NON-MONOTONE in leakW** — on 0430 it dips to 0.07 mid-curve then rises to 0.59 at the deflate end. So the old `r2budget` rule (blind maximally) OVER-blinds 0430 into a worse honest leak. **Added op-rule `SOFT_MODE='minleak'` (now the default): argmin |held-out leak| s.t. held-out R²≥floor** — exactly the achLeak the tuner scores. Re-deployed the 3 core sessions: 0212 leak −0.06 (unchanged), 0224 −0.21 (unchanged), **0430 0.59→0.07** (op at frac 0.45, R² cost 0.019, Local 79%/21% transient). ### 2026-09-05 — NEW METHOD: tunable soft-blinding (utils/ctrl_softblind.m) — 0224 leak 31%→~7% for 0.01 R²
**Changed/Found:** Built the tunable soft-blinding predictor the user asked for (honest, per-session-tunable, R²-preserving) as an alternative to hard-KKT deflate. **`utils/ctrl_softblind.m`** = the core: `min ‖y−Xb‖²+α‖b‖²+leakW·(dᵀb)²`, closed-form rank-1 update of the ridge solve, so ONE `A\d` traces the whole leakW sweep. Validated vs existing code: leakW=0 reproduces ridge exactly (‖Δb‖=0), leakW→∞ reproduces `ctrl_deflate` to 1e-11, leak monotone in leakW. Wired a **`softblind` pred_mode** into `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m` (+ `ctrl_pred_tag` suffix `_softblind`): sweeps a den-independent grid (target = fraction of ridge leak), computes the **held-out leak** (d fit on ODD trials, scored on EVEN — same guard as deflate), picks the op point as the least-blinding leakW whose held-out leak ≤ `SOFT_TARGET` (default 0.25), and CACHES the whole curve in `RPATH.SOFT`. **First real session (AL_0033_0224, usable):** ridge R² 0.915 / sustained leak 31%. Op point (held-out≤25%): **R² 0.905 (cost 0.009), all-trial leak 5%, held-out leak 24%** → honest deployed leak ~31%×0.24 ≈ **7-8%**. Global trace now stays near-flat through stim (Local 84%/16% transient, 95%/5% sustained). **Key honest finding: the held-out leak FLOORS at ~21%** even at max blinding — that gap between all-trial (→0) and held-out (→21%) is the irreducible, trial-stable part of the stim direction that this method genuinely cannot separate from coupling; deflate hides it (reports the →0 all-trial number), soft-blind exposes it. And the **R² cost is ~0.01 across the ENTIRE sweep** on 0224 — blinding is nearly free here (unlike pixel-exclusion, which lost lots of R²). Cache: `data/ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind_softblind_AL_0033_0224_e2.mat`; curve fig in scratchpad.
**Why:** User: "work on a perfect method for blindness we can tune per session, without losing too much R² on the spontaneous side; deflate isn't scientifically best but keep it in the catalog." Soft-blind meets all three: tunable (leakW knob + curve), honest (held-out leak reported + irreducible floor exposed, not imposed), cheap (0.01 R² on 0224).
**Next:** (a) Run soft-blind across the other usable sessions (0430, 0212) + the borderlines to see per-session curves and irreducible leak floors — does R²-cost stay ~free everywhere, or is 0224 lucky? ### 2026-09-04 — AL_0051 −2.06 root cause FOUND: un-detrended dFk target → train/test drift
**Changed/Found:** Re-ran Stage-2 fresh for AL_0051 (`BATCH_selField=15`; reproduces the −2.06, so not a stale cache) and traced it to the end. **The canonical `data.dFk` target has a large low-frequency baseline DRIFT.** Stage-1 uses a temporal train/test split (train = first ~75% of frames, test = last ~25%); on AL_0051 the target mean is **−0.13 in the train window and +3.96 in the test window (Δ=+4.08 = 1.5 test-SDs)**, vs Δ=+0.03 on a healthy session (0226). Trained on a target centred at 0, scored on one centred at +4 → even a perfect predictor scores negative; the ridge (near-singular contra Gram, RCOND 1e-7) drives ‖b‖→0.2 and the near-zero predictor lands at R²=−2.06 (worse than the mean, exactly what a mean-mismatch produces). **Why Stage-1 was fine (0.911) but Stage-2 fails:** Stage-1's target is the ROLLING-BASELINE `y_full` (stationary); Stage-2 switched to canonical `dFk` (line 73 `target_mode='canonical'`, done 2026-08 so ‖A−ref‖ shares the ref frame) — and `dFk` for the 2026-07 new mice was never detrended (`corr(y_full,dFk)`=0.55 vs 0.90 on older mice). So it is neither the affected-detector, the ridge, nor a stale cache — it is an **un-detrended target exposed by the temporal split**. No files changed (diagnosis only; the fresh Stage-2 run overwrote `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind_ridge_AL_0051_0729_e2.mat` with an identical-verdict cache).
**Why:** User asked to debug AL_0051 specifically. Root cause is now exact and it generalises: any new-mouse session whose `dFk` drifts will fail Stage-2 the same way (AL_0048 separately fails for lack of a `corr/` V).
**Next:** The fix is to fit the Global predictor on a **stationary** target (high-pass / rolling-baseline the `dFk` used for FITTING, or fit on `y_full` and re-reference at deployment) — a no-op for the older mice (Δ≈0) that removes AL_0051's artefact. ⚠ NOT a blind one-liner: `ytrace` also feeds the Actual/Global/Local decomposition, whose DC is deliberately KEPT (TASKS DC-rule), so a detrend must apply to the FIT target only (or be done upstream in getpixel_dFoF) without shifting the deployed A/G DC — get this wrong and the 3 good sessions' rejection numbers move silently. Given Block 3 is n=3→4 at best even if AL_0051 is rescued, recommend: log the new-mice dFk-drift as a known limitation, lean Fig 4 on Block 1 + Block 2, and only do the fit-target detrend if n=4 is worth the surgery. Widen `ctrl_ridge_path` opts.lambdas regardless (lambda* pinned at grid edge for AL_0051).

### 2026-09-04 — CORRECTION: the affected-detector is NOT broken; "0 affected" is correct behaviour
**Changed/Found:** Deeper look at `ctrl_select_k.m` + the stored `KSEL.R2curve` **retracts the prior entry's "detector is the failure point" conclusion.** Two corrections. (1) **R²(K) is MONOTONICALLY INCREASING on every session** (e.g. 0224: 0.47→0.92 as K 10→453; 0212: 0.50→1.00; 0226: 0.46→0.84; 0439-0419: 0.10→0.70). So dropping the most-dipping contra pixels NEVER raises held-out R² — more pixels always fit better. `ctrl_select_k` picks the SMALLEST K clearing the 0.85 floor; when the full-grid R² is already below floor it (correctly) falls back to argmax = full grid → **affected=0**. Therefore **nAff=0 ⟺ full-grid deployed R² < 0.85**, i.e. the "0 affected" sessions are exactly the ones that cannot be blinded and stay above floor — the detector is doing the right thing, and the gate correctly skips them. Repairing the detector will NOT add sessions. (2) **The prior entry's affected-% were wrong** (denominator bug: used `numel(unaff)`=grid size instead of `nnz`). Correct: the 3 passing sessions drop ~**76–78%** of the grid as affected (keep only K≈100 of ~440), not ~40%. This STRENGTHENS the "affected-count tracks R²-headroom, not laser physics" point: good sessions can afford to drop most pixels and still clear floor; sub-floor sessions can drop none.
**Why:** I told the user the detector was the smoking gun after the first pass; the R²(K) curves show that was wrong. Faithful record: the small n=3 is a genuine spont→trial GENERALIZATION limit for ~8 sessions, not a detector bug.
**Next:** Only ONE genuine fixable bug remains: **AL_0051** deployed R² **−2.06 with in-sample R²_tr=0.088** despite Stage-1 ρ=0.96 → the Stage-2 deploy is broken in-sample = a real alignment/preprocessing bug (cf. 2026-07 new-mice onset `timeBlue(col2)−dur`), worth debugging (could recover 1 session). **AL_0048 is NOT fixable** — the server has **no `corr/` V** (corrected file genuinely absent), so its 0.44 is on the only data that exists (weak expression, consistent with the new-mice caveat). Strategic upshot: Block 3 is honestly ~n=3 (maybe 4 with AL_0051 fixed); Fig 4 should lean on Block 1 (trial-average) + Block 2 (locked). Optional methodology change (NOT a bug fix, needs user/Nick sign-off): decouple affected-detection from the R² floor via a FIXED keep_frac so "affected" means the same thing on every session — changes every Stage-2 number, so do not do it silently.

### 2026-08-26 — FINDING: OL prediction error is flat vs motion but rises vs pre-stim variance
**Changed/Found:** `talk/dump_pred_state.m` (new) — drive-only PREDICTION error on constant-ref open-loop widefield trials (per-trial evoked-scalar residual from session mean, pooled within-session SD), binned by pre-stim state. Result over 13 sessions/477 trials: **vs motion Q1→Q4 = 1.53→1.47 (essentially FLAT)**; **vs pre-stim variance Q1→Q4 = 1.13→1.55 (RISES)**. Built the metric to supply both axes; the data says motion→prediction is flat — a real dissociation from the CONTROL result (ctrl_statedep: control error FALLS at high motion, rises with variance). This contradicts the assumed "motion→prediction" beat, so the Aim-1 figure/framing is a user decision, not auto-built.
**Next:** Ask user how to frame Aim 1 prediction-state: (a) show motion(flat)+variance(rises) honestly as a dissociation, (b) drop motion for prediction and keep variance + the grid rel-δ (fig:grid C), or (c) use a different prediction metric. JSON at scratchpad/pred_state.json.

### 2026-08-24 — grid_stim_fields.py: parametric optogenetic stimulation fields (excit exp vs inhib DoG)
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/grid_stim_fields.py` — fits the paper-style spatial "stimulation field" (Barzon/De/Kiani microstim-control preprint, Fig 5f) to the AL_0048 2026-07-10 grid off the fitted signed peak-gain matrix (`grid_tf_fits_2amp.npz`). Per stim site: response vs cortical distance to every readout, self-normalized; pooled by opsin class over reliable driver sites (diagonal CV-R²≥0.2, correct self-sign). **Result: excitatory (left) field = exponential decay, λ=0.71 mm (amp 1.0) / 0.76 mm (amp 2.0), R²=0.65, n=12 drivers — nearly identical to the paper's electrical-microstim λ=0.71 mm and amplitude-invariant.** Inhibitory (right) field = **broad monotonic exponential suppression, λ=1.79 (amp 1.0) / 2.62 mm (amp 2.0), R²=0.91, n=7 — NO surround rebound**, unlike the paper's center-surround difference-of-Gaussians; DoG fit did not beat plain exp (B→0). Inhib field is ~3–4× broader than excit and mildly broadens with laser power.
**Why:** Deep-dive of the microstim closed-loop-control preprint flagged its Fig-5 "stimulation fields" + linear-superposition as the most portable analysis to our optogenetic grid; superposition is blocked (grid is single-site-only), so the field-decay fit is the doable half and converts our spatial-linearity assumption into a measured, cross-modality-comparable result. Excit/inhib split exploits our dual-opsin design (the cell-type specificity the paper concedes electrical microstim lacks).

### 2026-08-24 — Grid state panel reframed to Fig-2J/2K PREDICTION-ERROR-vs-state; model math added to grant
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/grid_state_prederr.py`; `grid_aim1_panel.py` panel C swapped from the trial-averaged gain split to a **prediction-error-vs-state** curve mirroring paper Fig 2J/2K. Method: per site×amp, the drive-only (amplitude-mean = LTI) predictor gives a per-trial residual on the evoked scalar (mean over 0.03–0.45 s at the stimulated site); trials binned into quartiles of a pre-stim state marker (within-cell percentile rank); **prediction error = pooled-within-cell SD of the residual per quartile** (same "pooled within cell so a bin isn't more uncertain just from bigger responses" logic as `imp_state_trialvar.m`'s `sdRaw`); bootstrap 95% CI over trials. Two markers computed: **relative δ (1–4/0.5–30 Hz) — power-INDEPENDENT, admissible** → monotone rise Q1→Q4 **1.00→1.35, trend r=+1.00**; raw variance (POWER CONFOUND) rises steeper 1.00→2.9 and is NOT plotted (only mentioned). Panel normalised to Q1 because `roi_ts` is raw SVD units (~10⁴), NOT ΔF/F — do not label that axis ΔF/F. Also rendered 4 model equations (`draft/render_eqs.py` → `eq_lti/graph/gdar/state.png`, matplotlib mathtext) into a new Aim-2 "Modeling framework" subsection of `draft/grant_writing.docx`: (1) single-site LTI state-space/TF `H(s)=cᵀ(sI−A)⁻¹b=Σ rᵢ/(s−λᵢ)`; (2) graph forward model `x_{t+1}=A(𝒢)x_t+Bu_t`; (3) GDAR graph-VARX `x_t=Σ A_k x_{t−k}+Σ B_c u_{t−q}+e_t`; (4) state-conditioned operators + LQ control objective. Doc is now 5 pages.
**Why:** User: "not a fan of fig a1.2 panel c, i want the prediction error vs state type analysis like we did in figure 2 of the paper, in parallel blend in some math on all the models we are using." Prediction-error framing is stronger than the trial-averaged gain split AND sidesteps the drift/gain-artifact subtlety: it directly says "the fixed LTI model leaves state-structured error → motivates Aim 2's state-conditioned models." Using the power-INDEPENDENT marker (relative δ) follows the impulse-analysis rule that pre-stim variance/abs-δ are power confounds (root `impulse-analysis/CLAUDE.md`); grid has no motion trace so relative δ is the only admissible axis available.

### 2026-08-24 — Grid state-dependence RESOLVED: drift-invariant but FAST-state-DEPENDENT (high pre-stim activity → larger evoked gain); grant Aim-1 composite built
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/grid_state_trialavg.py` (trial-averaged split), `grid_tf_lean.py` (2-exemplar LTI figure), `grid_aim1_panel.py` (3-tile composite → `grid_png/grid_aim1_panel.png`). Reconciled yesterday's apparent state-INVARIANCE (r=−0.05) with a trial-averaged median-split that shows a clear ~40% larger evoked peak in high-pre-stim-variance trials. The two disagree because they measure DIFFERENT state axes: (1) **variance INCLUDING slow drift** — drift continues into the post window but is orthogonal to the fast evoked transient, so it does NOT project onto the mean shape → the template-projection gain sees a slight NEGATIVE relation (drift trials look, if anything, smaller in shape-matched terms) = the r=−0.05 null. (2) **1 Hz-high-passed variance** (drift removed) — now measures fast cortical-state fluctuation, and higher pre-stim activity precedes a LARGER evoked transient. The high-passed median split gives within-cell shape-projection gain **0.72 (low) → 1.28 (high), high>low in 74% of site×amp cells** (n=104 cells) — so it is NOT the noisy-trace-bigger-|peak| artifact (that control is passed). Diagnostic tests run inline: raw split showed a pre-stim offset + sustained plateau (drift signature); per-trial pre-window linear detrend made the high group ramp monotonically to 0.8 (drift over-extrapolation); 1 Hz high-pass gave a clean decaying transient in both groups with the gain difference surviving.
**Why:** User wants the grid state-dependence presented "following the trial-averaged comparison we did for motion and pre-trial var" for the grant Aim 1. Honest message is now positive and on-theme: **cortical state gates the gain of the evoked optogenetic response** (identical stimulation, larger response from a more active pre-stim state) — the mouse analogue of the OS-Pulse parameter-dependence, and squarely "state-dependent cortical responses" for Aim 1. Yesterday's "state-invariant" entry was correct ONLY for drift-inclusive variance; it is superseded for the grant by the drift-removed result.
**Next:** (1) The projection control is a plain (non-leave-one-out) template; if this is promoted beyond a grant prelim, redo with LOO + a phase-shuffled noise floor to fully rule out any residual amplitude-selection bias. (2) `grid_state_dependence.py` figure (scatter) is NOT used in the grant — the trial-averaged `grid_aim1_panel.png` panel C is. (3) Composite feeds `draft/grant_writing.docx` Aim 1 mouse-grid section (LTI fits + brain spot + state panel).

### 2026-08-24 — Grid state-dependence: focal evoked GAIN is state-INVARIANT; the naive |peak| effect is a noise artifact
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/grid_state_dependence.py` — tests whether pre-stimulus cortical state (pre-stim variance and 1–4 Hz power over a 1 s pre-onset window) predicts the evoked FOCAL photostim response on the AL_0048 52-site grid, using the single-trial cache `data/grid_trials_2amp.npz` (continuous per-site `roi_ts`; 5200 onsets, 52 sites × 2 amps, fs≈70 Hz). Regressors + response z-scored WITHIN site×amp then pooled. **With a naive signed-|peak| response measure the correlation is strong (Spearman r=+0.49 / +0.47, p≈0) — but this is a NOISE ARTIFACT** (a noisier trace has a larger |peak| by chance). **Switching the response to a leave-one-out template-projection gain (amplitude along the site's mean evoked shape, robust to broadband noise) collapses the effect to r=−0.05 (variance) / −0.045 (low-freq)** — negligible despite n=5200. So the focal evoked GAIN is essentially state-invariant to ongoing pre-stim state. Figure: `bilateral/grid/grid_png/grid_state_dependence.png` (quartile bars + scatter).
**Why:** User asked to add grid state-dependent analysis for the grant. The result corroborates the existing brain_paper finding that the LOCAL stimulus response is state-robust ([[project_impulse_status]] / FINDINGS "Local photoinhibition response is state-robust") — state-dependence lives at the GLOBAL/network level and in stimulation PARAMETERS (the OS-Pulse frequency roll-off), not in the local focal gain. Prevents putting an inflated r=0.49 artifact into a grant.
**Next:** If a positive grid state result is wanted, test state-dependence of the DISTRIBUTED/off-site response (network level), not the focal gain — but control the same |peak|/noise confound (use template projection or contra-style global/local split). Motion is not available in the grid caches, so only variance + low-freq power are buildable state axes here.

### 2026-08-24 — Trial-level cross-validated LTI fit across all sessions (new engine + figure)
**Changed/Found:** New `utils/imp_tf_cv_session.m` + driver `impulse-analysis/imp_tf_cv.m`. Repeated **stratified split-half over TRIALS, both directions** (100 splits ×2 = 200 held-out fits/session): within each amplitude the trials are randomly halved (stratified so both halves keep the full dose range and h(t) is built the same amp²-weighted way), fit the fixed session order on one half, predict the OTHER half's measured h(t). Two metrics: `R2_out` (amplitude-normalised — prediction carries its own gain, the honest number) and `R2_shape` (each peak-normalised — pure shape, matches 2C-i). Matched in-sample control = same train model scored on its own half. Panels → `paper/explore/tf_cv/`: `tf_cv_shape_across_sessions.pdf` (CV version of 2C-i: measured held-out solid vs held-out prediction dashed) and `tf_cv_r2_trial.pdf` (in-sample→held-out R² per session, median+IQR). **Result:** pooled held-out R² **0.86** (amp-norm) / 0.87 (shape). Per session held-out: AL_0033 e1 **0.95** [0.92-0.97], AL_0041 e2 0.86, AL_0048 e1 0.84 (10% folds fail to fit the fixed order on a half), **AL_0041 e1 0.50 [0.05-0.76]** — collapses from 0.97 in-sample.
**Why:** User: "normalised LTI fit comparison for all sessions but cross validated, done properly — randomise both datasets first then fit then test." The existing 2C-i dashed curve is IN-SAMPLE and the only CV in the pipeline (LOAO / `talk/make_lti_cv_fig.m`) holds out an AMPLITUDE but still fits/tests on trial AVERAGES — neither holds out trials. This is the honest generalisation test. AL_0041 e1's in-sample 0.97 was optimistic: fewest amps + simplest order (3p1z0d) → it was partly fitting trial-average noise, which only a trial-level split exposes.

(2) Panel A overlays the MEAN held-out prediction (averaged over 200 models ≈ smooth), so AL_0041 e1's instability is only visible in panel B's IQR whisker, not the overlay — do not over-read the overlay for that session. (3) Partially answers Nick's 2026-05-08 "report R² on held-out test set" ask (this is stronger — trial-level, not a single 20% split). ### 2026-08-20 — 3G session-averaged error offered as RMSE; the CL gain is 29%, not 44%
**Changed/Found:** `talk/redraw_fig3_colors.m` — new `F3_METRIC` knob ('rmse' default | 'mae'). RMSE takes `sqrt(mean(e.^2))` across trials at each sample instead of `abs(mean(e))`, y-limit is now taken from the data (the hardcoded 6 was MAE-era and clips RMSE), and the RMSE version exports to **`all_average_sessions_rmse.pdf`** so the MAE panel the paper text refers to is not overwritten. Numbers, stim-window mean over 13 sessions: **RMSE OL 2.99 → CL 2.12 (29% lower)**; MAE OL 1.68 → CL 0.95 (44% lower).
**Why:** Requested for the talk — RMSE has been the project's error metric everywhere else since 2026-07-16, and MAE on this panel was the standing exception. The 15-point gap between the two is not noise: MAE is `abs(mean over trials)`, so errors of opposite sign on different trials CANCEL and the panel measures BIAS only; RMSE cancels nothing, and RMSE² = bias² + across-trial variance. So the RMSE panel now *contains* what panel 3F (variance) shows separately, and the two are no longer independent evidence. Say that if they are shown on the same slide.
**Next:** `controller-analysis/step_response.m` writes the same `all_average_sessions.pdf` and is still MAE-only — repoint or add the knob there if the paper panel is ever switched too.

### 2026-08-20 — No sleep episode in AL_0033 m5; every apparent dilation was a blink
**Changed/Found:** Swept the m5 pupil at 1 Hz over all 89 min: 14.7 px (1st pct) to 19.2 px (99th), median 15.8, trackable 1.000, corr(motion z, pupil d) = **+0.23** (n = 5341 s). There is **no sustained drowsy episode** — the pupil is at a constricted baseline the whole session. Worse, the apparent large dilations are **blinks**: the lid occludes the pupil, the darkest compact object left is a sliver, and the reopening reads as a 15 → 45 px "dilation" in 1.5 s. The top-ranked window (t = 4786 s) was exactly this. `pick_arousal` now rejects on TWO tests — fraction of frames within 25% of the window median ≥ 0.97 AND min/median ≥ 0.60 — because the fraction alone passes a 1.5 s blink in a 10 s window at 0.92. Rejecting whole windows then discarded the only real dilation, so the picker now SLIDES the window start in 1 s steps to dodge the blink while keeping the dilation.
**Why:** A clip labelled "sleepy" that is really a blink would put an artefact on a talk slide as a brain state. Recorded because the same trap is live for any pupil analysis on these sessions, not just the clip.
**Next:** The +0.23 motion/pupil correlation is measured at 1 Hz, which aliases blinks and probably inflates it (movement → blinks → spurious large diameters). Do NOT quote it as validation without recomputing on blink-screened frames. Blink-free range in this session is only 15.0 → 16.7 px (4th → 87th pct), so if the talk needs a real drowsy/alert contrast, another session has to be scanned.
