### 2026-08-20 — CV R² panel rescaled; the negative folds are fit failures, not overfitting
**Changed/Found:** `talk/make_lti_cv_fig.m` panel 2 rewritten — y clipped to [−1.2, 1] with off-scale folds drawn at the floor and labelled with their true in-sample/held-out values, plus the paired drop (median `R²_in − R²_out`) added to the title and a `talk/tf_cv_stats.mat` dump of every fold's stats. **Finding:** on the worst folds the in-sample R² is essentially as negative as the held-out one (AL_0033's weakest amplitude: −2.75 in-sample, −2.75 held out — the connecting line is flat), so those amplitudes are ones the model fits badly whether or not they were held out. In AL_0041 e2 the −7.90 fold's *measured* trace has no inhibitory dip at all — it rises monotonically to +2.4 %ΔF/F — so the model is being scored against a response that is not an impulse response.
**Why:** The first render let a −7.9 and a −6.7 fold set the ylim, squeezing the other 17 folds into a ~5%-tall band and hiding the in-sample-vs-held-out comparison the panel exists to show. Clipping with labelled off-scale folds relocates them rather than hiding them. The paired drop is the statistic that answers "does it generalise"; comparing the two medians conflates generalisation loss with amplitudes the fit never captured.
**Next:** Check AL_0041 e2's positive-going amplitude before quoting the −7.90 anywhere — it looks like a bad amplitude (wrong stim detection or too few trials), not a model failure, and if so it should be excluded from the fold set rather than explained away.

### 2026-08-19 - State panels re-expressed as PREDICTION ERROR in %dF/F
**Changed/Found:** `imp_state_trialvar.m` now also computes `R(k).sdRaw` - the SD of the RAW
deviation from the amplitude mean, pooled WITHIN each (session x amplitude) cell - and
`imp_state_trialvar_fig.m` gained `STVF_UNITS` ('sd' default = published 2J/2K axis, 'raw' =
%dF/F). `talk/make_state_panels.m` runs 'raw'. The bootstrap CI is carried over by the per-bin
conversion factor. Numbers (Q1->Q4, %dF/F):
  motion, all trials      2.78 -> 3.18 -> 3.08 -> **2.08**
  pre-trial var, mot-excl 1.11 -> 2.06 -> 3.21 -> **4.09**
**Why:** user, 2026-08-19: "sd of dev is not a great explainer ... use prediction error in its
correct units". The published y is the deviation scaled by the within-amplitude SD, so it is
~1 by construction and unitless - it can say wider/narrower but never HOW wide, which is the
whole point of the slide.
**Next:** pooling within (session x amplitude) cells is load-bearing, not cosmetic - a plain SD
over the bin would inherit the between-amplitude spread of response SIZE, so a bin holding more
high-amplitude trials would read as more uncertain purely because its responses are bigger.
That is the same reason the DV was scaled per amplitude originally; this keeps the protection
and the units. The panels now state the claim directly: prediction error falls to **2.1 %dF/F**
in the top motion quartile and climbs to **4.1 %dF/F** in the top pre-stim-variance quartile -
a ~3.7x span across variance quartiles. Caveat unchanged: pre-trial variance is the 2026-07-02
signal-power confound, and here the confound is MORE visible, not less, because larger ongoing
signal mechanically inflates a residual measured in absolute units. Present it as the confound.

AL_0041 12/02 e2 generalises WORSE THAN ITS OWN MEAN across amplitudes. The 0.67 median over 21

### 2026-08-19 - BUG: state quartiles were binned GLOBALLY, not within session; motion panel now reproduces the published one exactly
**Changed/Found:** new `talk/verify_motion_quartiles.m` (read-only audit) + fix in
`talk/state_quartile_panels.m`. `motion_analysis.m` computes its quantile edges INSIDE the
session loop - quartiles are WITHIN-SESSION and only the resulting bins are pooled.
state_quartile_panels.m used one global edge set over all pooled trials. With within-session
edges the motion panel now reproduces the published one to the decimal: OL 30.4 / 29.8 / 29.6 /
32.1 and CL 24.5 / 24.9 / 24.6 / 21.3 on the old un-normalised scale (x sqrt(106)).
Two further fixes in the same pass: (a) the per-session slope is now regressed on the
WITHIN-SESSION PERCENTILE RANK of the state, not the raw state - a raw-unit slope is not
comparable between sessions whose state ranges differ 5x, which is why the median slope used to
contradict the panel it annotated; (b) both median and mean slope are printed, because the
pooled quartile curve tracks the MEAN while the signed-rank test is about the MEDIAN.
**Why:** user spotted that the Q1/Q2 profile did not match the previous analysis. It did not -
global edges sorted trials largely by SESSION (motion medians span -0.29..-0.03, maxima
0.99..4.78, so Q1 was fed by only 7 of 9 sessions) and manufactured a Q2 spike out of session
difficulty. dur = 3 for all nine sessions and all three stored window widths cross-check, so the
window and motion definition were never wrong - only the binning.
**Next:** corrected numbers (RMSE, Q1->Q4, slope-per-rank med/mean, interaction p):
  motion  OL +0.16 (2.95->3.12) CL -0.31 (2.38->2.07) | OL +0.905/+0.761 CL -0.030/-0.131 | **p=0.0039**
  prevar  OL +0.84 (2.51->3.35) CL +0.77 (1.99->2.77) | OL +0.730/+1.03  CL +0.173/+0.622 | p=0.203
  1-4 Hz  OL +0.13 (2.96->3.09) CL +0.24 (2.21->2.45) | OL -0.253/-0.265 CL +0.142/+0.253 | p=0.098
  1-2 Hz  OL -0.42 (3.15->2.73) CL +0.10 (2.22->2.32) | OL -0.193/-0.316 CL +0.034/+0.037 | p=0.074
  2-4 Hz  OL +0.23 (2.80->3.03) CL +0.21 (2.22->2.43) | OL -0.151/-0.126 CL +0.118/+0.298 | p=0.129
**The earlier "2-4 Hz carries the whole delta effect" claim from this morning is WITHDRAWN** - it
was an artifact of the global binning. On the corrected panels every delta variant is nearly flat
and no delta interaction reaches significance. What survives: motion (CL flattens a +0.9
dependence to -0.03, p=0.0039) and pre-stim variance (both loops rise together, CL offset below OL).

### 2026-08-19 - State-quartile OL/CL panels (pre-stim variance, relative delta) on motion-clean trials
**Changed/Found:** new `talk/state_quartile_panels.m` - the state twin of the motion-quartile
panel. Motion cut first (|mean z-motion, onset-2 s .. trial end| <= 1.5 = motThresh), then trial
RMSE pooled into quartiles of a PRE-onset state measured over [-2, 0) s: variance, and relative
1-4 Hz power (P(1-4)/P(0.4-10), a ratio, so power-independent). Lean - loads only `data` from
each cache, one session at a time. **Only 9 of the 13 sessions have a motion trace** (m1, m3, m7,
m8 have none), so these panels are n=9, not n=13. Motion removes just 24/990 trials (2.4%).
Numbers: prevar Q1->Q4 OL 2.42->3.81, CL 1.93->3.33, per-session slope OL +0.089 vs CL +0.038,
interaction signrank p=0.25. Delta Q1->Q4 OL 2.83->3.45, CL 2.00->2.78, slope OL -0.436 vs
CL +0.328, p=0.13.

OL rises Q1->Q4 while the median per-session OL slope is NEGATIVE, i.e. the rise is between-session
difficulty leaking into a raw-trial pool (exactly the effect cl_factor_olcl_panels.m removed on

within-animal state effect until it is redrawn session-normalised. Pre-stim variance agrees in

below OL at every level of state", not "CL flattens the state dependence".

### 2026-08-19 — GIF jitter was a palette artefact, not the data
**Changed/Found:** New `presentation/gif_utils.py` with `save_gif()` and `tsmooth()`. PIL quantises every GIF frame independently by default, so a smooth widefield gradient lands on a slightly different 256-colour palette each frame and shimmers. `save_gif()` builds ONE palette from a strip of 16 evenly-spaced frames, quantises every frame against it with `dither=NONE` (per-frame dither patterns are themselves a source of shimmer), and uses `disposal=1`. `make_brain_gif.py` also gained `--tsmooth` (default 3): a moving average applied to the SVD temporal components before projection — 200 components instead of 19 600 pixels, and identical to smoothing the frames since the projection is linear. Side effect: the GIF shrank 12.9 MB -> 9.7 MB, because a shared palette compresses far better.
**Why:** User reported the slowed-down GIF looked jittery.
**Next:** `--tsmooth 3` at 35 Hz is an 86 ms window — fine for display, but do not measure onset latency off this GIF.

### 2026-08-18 — Fig-4 Part 1 added to the talk as the IMP argument with data; deck now 16 slides (later 15, see above)
**Changed/Found:** New slide 11, *"What the loop can reject — and what it makes worse"*, from the Fig-4 Part-1 / Block-2 factor analysis (`cl_factor_slope_panels.m`, `cl_rmse_factor_windows.m`, `cl_factor_decomp_panel.m`). Three paired-slope panels (n=15 sessions, four mice; motion n=11): **motion OL +0.686 → CL −0.016, p=0.0020**; **relative 2–4 Hz OL −0.511 → CL +0.813, p=0.0125**; **relative 1–2 Hz null control p=0.76 n.s.** Plus the unique-R² decomposition (613 CL trials / 11 sessions, 2000-boot CI): initial deviation 0.381 → 0.029 late (13× collapse), motion 0.001 → 0.001, relative 2–4 Hz 0.089 → 0.122, so rel-2–4 Hz goes from 22 % of explained variance early to **93 % late**.
**Why:** This is the internal model principle stated in data, and it is the missing bridge between the rejection slide and the MPC close. A PI integrator *is* an internal model of a constant, so motion — slow and quasi-DC — is decoupled completely. The loop has no oscillatory mode at 2–4 Hz, and the slope there does not merely survive: it **flips sign**, which is the discriminating observation. A controller that simply lacked a model of that band would leave the OL slope untouched (S≈1: no rejection, no harm); a flip means feedback is *actively making that band worse* — the Bode sensitivity integral / waterbed effect, not a null. The 1–2 Hz control makes it band-specific rather than generic. Together: the loop models DC and rejects it, has no model of the oscillatory band, and pays for its low-frequency suppression — which is exactly the argument that MPC with a learned network model is what the theory prescribes.
**Next:** Two panel-hygiene items carried into the notes. (a) The 1–2 Hz null **must** be shown as `factor_slope_delta12` (per-session paired slope), never `claim2_delta_lo12_late` — in the pooled-quartile form the 1–2 Hz series rises almost identically to 2–4 Hz through between-session baseline structure, so side by side they argue *against* the dissociation; only the paired-slope form has picture and statistic agreeing. (b) `factor_slope_motion` and `factor_slope_delta24` are still exported with **different y-ranges**, which blunts the contrast between the two strongest panels — fix at source before paper assembly. ⚠ Budget: the talk is now ~13:30 against a 12:00 target; a cut decision is pending with the user.

### 2026-08-18 — Talk gains a contra→ipsi setup slide; carries the filter-vs-pattern correction
**Changed/Found:** New slide inserted before the rejection slide (deck now **15 slides**), at user request: the coloured contra→ipsi kernel plus a statement of what the method actually does — fit on **spontaneous, laser-off frames** using only contra pixels the laser does not affect (stim-blind by construction), then deployed during trials to give **Global**, the counterfactual "as if no laser" ipsi trace, with **Local = Actual − Global**. Panels cropped from `hemi_coupling_maps_sq.png` (per-pixel R² map, contra → dFk, target site marked) and `ctrl_spatial_pattern_AL_0033_0226_e2.png` (FILTER vs Haufe forward PATTERN). Budget held at ~12:00 by trimming slides 2, 5, 6 and 7.
**Why:** Global had been used on two slides (pivot, rejection) without ever showing how it is built, and ER is meaningless until the disturbance is defined. The slide also carries a correction the project already made but that had not reached the talk: **the raw regression filter is not a spatial map.** On m4 `ρ(filter, pattern) = −0.020` with **47 % of pixels flipping sign** — the filter map is salt-and-pepper, the forward pattern is a coherent posterior-lateral contra region. A filter is optimised to predict, not to localise, so it will place large opposite-sign weights on correlated neighbours. Worth the 15 s in this room specifically: Amy Orsborn is an organiser and BCI decoder work is where this distinction is best known (Haufe et al. 2014).
**Next:** The pattern figure is single-session (m4). If anyone asks for generality, that is the honest answer. Also note `hemi_coupling_maps_sq.png`'s right panel plots signed OLS weight² — i.e. a filter map — so it should not be shown as "where the information is" without the same caveat.

### 2026-08-18 — ⚠ MPC HAS run on m4; the talk's "no numbers" guard was wrong. `_global` batch is n=2 and unusable
**Changed/Found:** Correcting the 2026-08-14 talk-plan claim that `ctrl_optimal_xsess.m` is "built and UNRUN" and that slide 9 may carry no numbers. **`ctrl_optimal_control.m` HAS run on m4** and the figure is on disk (`paper/images/predictor_saga/ctrl_optimal_AL_0033_0226_e2.png`, plant nx=2, u_max=2.06, ref=−5, trial-averaged): **steady RMSE (1–3 s) PI 1.202 → causal optimal 0.146 (−87.8 %), non-causal 0.000**; full window 1.510 / 0.994 / 0.927; **mean laser command PI 1.563 → optimal 1.300**; measured disturbance drifts +1.82 % over the trial. Two readings matter more than the headline: **causal ≈ clairvoyant**, so nearly all the gain is reachable causally and the PI gap is not about future knowledge; and the optimal controller achieves it with **less command**, which is the empirical payoff of the minimum-energy framing in the talk's opener. **Separately, the `_global` cross-session batch is NOT usable**: `f4_mpc_rmse_global.png` reads **n=2, p=0.5**, and `f4_mpc_traces_global.png`'s exemplar is **AL_0033_0212_e2 — the session already flagged for exclusion** (frame transposed at load, laser ~5× weak, spot straddling the midline; its transmission goes the wrong way, OL 0.99 → CL 1.27).

The m4 numbers are `'residual'`, hence quotable only as a single-session, trial-averaged, explicitly-flattered demonstration.
**Next:** Run `ctrl_optimal_xsess.m` with `src='global'` across sessions once the Stage-2 rebuild clears — that is the number that would turn this from a ceiling calculation into a control claim. **Changed/Found:** User: *"promote more of the internal model principle and disturbance rejection story alongside showing that MPC can do even better."* Added **slide 8 — disturbance rejection + IMP**, now the empirical centre of the second half and the strongest cross-session result in the talk: **ER median OL 0.291 → CL 0.203, CL better in 13/13 sessions, signrank p = 2.4e-4**; per-session significant in 11/13, the two misses being exactly the two new mice with weak predictors (so their inclusion is conservative); per-trial transmission β m4 OL 0.97 → CL 0.56; rejection **state-INVARIANT** (state-dependence returned null — [IMP-STATE-QUARTILE] all four r_s null, [IMP-XSTATE] 7 sessions no surviving slope, Friedman n.s.). Deck rebuilt: **14 slides**, validates clean.
**Why:** The IMP is the rigorous bridge the talk was missing. A PI controller's integrator is an internal model of a **constant**; ongoing cortical activity is not constant; therefore ER floors at ≈0.20 rather than 0 **because the model is missing, not because the tuning is bad**. That makes MPC a *prediction of the theory* rather than a wish — and it makes the opener's minimum-energy promise land, since the optimal controller tracks better on less light. Also reframes what the residual means: not controller failure, a missing model.
**Next:** Panel prep note — the `f4_reject_*` panels carry a burned-in `UNGATED (no R² floor, n=13)` annotation that **collides with their own titles**; the deck crops the top band and carries the caveat in the slide caption instead. ### 2026-08-14 — Aerospace analogy adopted for the talk opener (rocket) and close (gust rejection)
**Changed/Found:** `TALK_neuroai_2026.md` slide 1 gains an opening-analogy block, at the user's suggestion and drawing on their own background (PhD, aero/astro + control). Split deliberately across the talk so neither analogy overstays: **powered descent / rocket landing in slide 1** for the *actuation* structure — one-sided thrust ↔ a laser that can only inhibit (`0 ≤ u ≤ u_max`), minimum-fuel ↔ minimum-energy, bounded non-convex thrust solved as a convex program ↔ the one-sided **QP, not LQR** — and **aircraft gust-load alleviation in slide 9** for the *forecasting* structure, since forward-looking gust sensing feeding a feedforward controller is exactly preview control generalized to a predicted disturbance. Three disanalogies written in as the scientifically interesting content: (1) no first-principles plant — it must be identified per animal, which is why slide 4 exists; (2) **the disturbance IS the system** — unlike wind, ongoing cortical activity is the object of study, so you are rejecting a signal you also want to measure; (3) **the reference is unknown** — a rocket's desired trajectory comes from the mission, but what trajectory *should* neural activity follow is an open scientific question.
**Why:** The user asked how to frame "a control problem like rocket landing or aircraft flight, but with so much variability it's too hard — so how do we figure it out?". The answer written onto the slide is that the talk's own structure IS the answer: identify the plant from data → close the loop and measure how much variability feedback removes → characterize the residual and its source → model the disturbance and go model-predictive. That is the standard control-engineering program applied to a plant with no first-principles equations, and stating it on slide 1 hands the audience the whole talk in one sentence.
**Next:** Two guards recorded on the slide. **Dosage** — use each analogy once and drop it; half the room is neuroscientists and an extended aerospace metaphor reads as engineering-imperialism, with the three disanalogies as the insurance. **Citation** — spoken as analogy nothing needs a reference, but if lossless convexification / powered-descent guidance (Açıkmeşe & Ploen) appears on a slide as a citation it must be verified first; not in `refs.bib`.

### 2026-08-13 — Rainier rig: `input_params.csv` `kk` is the trial END, not the onset — new `kk_onset` column (the real bug behind the "kkTemp divergence")
**Changed/Found:** `StLab_Rainier` — `BaseController._log_trial` now appends the true stimulus onset (`self.inp`) as a **`kk_onset`** column, and `_save_data` builds the CSV header from the **actual row width** so it can never disagree with the data. **The defect:** the long-standing `kk` column carries `kkTemp2`, which `_mp_reader` rewrites *every control sample* (`mp_controller.py:235`) as a free-running index — it is not a trial anchor at all. Because `_log_trial` runs after the stimulus window, the logged value is the index at the **end** of the stimulus, so `onset ≈ kk − dur·35`. This is exactly the compensation already recorded in the project memory for the 2026-07 builds ("col2 = trial END"), now traced to its cause in the rig code. Worse, the same-looking column means different things across scripts: `controller_analysis.py` logs a genuine onset under the name `kk_start`, while `Main_experiment`/base/`bilateral_main` log the end under `kk`. `kk` is left **untouched** (downstream analysis compensates for it, and redefining it would silently break those loaders); the unambiguous value is added alongside. Four scripts now route through `_log_trial` and gain `kk_onset`; `characterization.py` and `impulse_bilateral.py` deliberately do not — neither is an OL/CL protocol, both already capture their own true onset before firing, and neither has a controller mode the demo panels could bin by. Documented in `EXPERIMENTS.md` (Saved Outputs) and `README.md`.
**Why:** looking for the `kkTemp` divergence flagged earlier today turned up something more consequential — a per-trial index whose name says onset and whose value is the end, differing in meaning between scripts.
**Next:** ⚠ **Rig check, one line:** after a session, `kk_onset` should equal `kk − dur·35` to within a sample or two. If it does not, the `kk`-as-end reading is wrong and every analysis that compensates for it needs revisiting. Also worth deciding whether `controller_analysis`'s `kk_start` should be renamed to `kk_onset` for consistency (not done — it would break anything reading that column by name).

### 2026-08-13 — CORRECTION: the `kkTemp` "divergence" is benign; base and Main unified on `_trial_begin()`
**Changed/Found:** Reverses this morning's claim (entry below) that unifying base's and Main's trial-start code "would change which sample index a trial is anchored to" and that base's trials "may be anchored to a stale index". They are not. Tracing every read and write of `kkTemp`/`kkTemp2`/`inp` shows the **acquisition thread is authoritative**: on the `start_exp` rising edge `_mp_reader` sets `kkTemp = inp = kk` (`mp_controller.py:185-186`), overwriting whatever the control thread put there within one control period. So both variants converge on the same onset and the difference is confined to a ~28.6 ms window before the reader fires. Within that window Main's extra `kkTemp = last_logged_k` is **strictly better** — it is the consumer of `kkTemp` for custom-avg waveform indexing (`_sync_params_to_shm`, `step = kk - kkTemp`), so leaving it stale would index the previous trial's waveform. Base omits it and gets away with it only because base has no custom-avg path. New `BaseController._trial_begin(a)` encodes Main's version (flags, gain, mode capture, index seeding) with the authority/placeholder relationship written down, and is now used by base, `Main_experiment`, `bilateral_main` and `controller_analysis`.
**Why:** the earlier caution was right to stop the refactor, but the conclusion drawn from it was wrong, and it was left as an open question about possibly-corrupt trial windows — which would have sent someone auditing recorded sessions for a problem that does not exist.
**Next:** none for the divergence itself — resolved. The genuine index problem it uncovered is the entry above.

### 2026-08-13 — Fig 4 Part 2: rejection resolved in FREQUENCY — the waterbed crossover is real (`ctrl_sensitivity_freq.m`)
**Changed/Found:** New `controller-analysis/ctrl_sensitivity_freq.m` `[SENS]` — per trial, over the response window, with the contra-derived Global as the measured disturbance: T(f) = ⟨|E(f)|²⟩/⟨|D(f)|²⟩ per condition and **S(f) = T_CL(f)/T_OL(f)** = what feedback changed. 13 sessions (the two without Stage-2 caches skip). Exports to `paper/images/figure4/supp/` — **supplementary, PNG only, pending approval** (user). Band restricted to 1–10 Hz per user (below 1 Hz is out of scope). Two bugs caught while building: `cell2mat(arrayfun(@(a) a.X(kb).', ...))` transposed the CONTENTS instead of the cell array, silently producing one long column (out-of-bounds on the first use, a 10⁵-scale nonsense ratio on the second); and a band-shading patch with hardcoded y-corners hijacked every axis — the same failure mode as `ctrl_fit_figs`'s laser patch earlier today, now fixed with a helper that shades to limits the data already set.
**Found — the IMP prediction holds, and the crossover sits where Part 1 said it would:** S(f) = **0.936 at 1–2 Hz** (suppression, n.s. p=0.11, 4/13 above 1) → **1.089 at 2–4 Hz (p=0.021, 10/13 above 1)** → **1.131 at 4–10 Hz (p=0.0024, 11/13)**. Feedback suppresses below ~2 Hz and **amplifies above it** — the Bode waterbed, and the mechanism behind Part 1's sign flip (CL error rising with 2–4 Hz power while OL error falls). ∫log S df over 1–10 Hz = **+0.665**, i.e. net amplification inside the measured band; the compensating suppression sits below 1 Hz, excluded by design. Steady-state offset from ref over 2–3 s: **OL +1.38 → CL +0.38 %ΔF/F, signrank p=0.008, smaller in 12/13 sessions** — the integrator's internal model of a constant, working.
**Found — all three controls pass, and one of them retires a planned worry:** (a) [SENS-NULL] the same estimator on the matched PRE-STIM window (laser off in both conditions) is **flat at 1** — 1.016 / 1.026 / 0.995 across the three bands — so the ratio-of-ratios is not an artifact of the estimator; (b) [SENS-DIST] the OL and CL disturbance spectra ⟨|D|²⟩ overlie each other, so both conditions genuinely see the same disturbance and it cancels in S; (c) [SENS-LEAK] **the stim-locked (leak) component is only 1–3% of disturbance power above 1 Hz.** That measures the leak-bias concern directly instead of bounding it — the leak is slow, so restricting the claim to ≥1 Hz removes it, and the planned deflate-Global bound is not needed for this claim.
**Why:** ER is a scalar over 0–3 s and cannot separate "rejects everything by 30%" from "rejects DC and amplifies 3 Hz" — which is the whole IMP result. User approved building all the proposed additions, supplementary until reviewed.
**Next:** (1) ⚠ Above ~8 Hz the disturbance power has fallen ~3 decades and both T curves shoot up — the 4–10 Hz band partly rides on that noise-dominated top end. **2–4 Hz is the safe claim**; either cap the band at 8 Hz or state the caveat. (2) The predicted-vs-measured S(f) panel (1/(1+CP) from the Fig-2 plant TF and the real Kp/Ki) is NOT built — per-session gains are not in the session structs (`d.params` holds only pixel/laser/dur/horizon/kernel); they live in the controller-tuning rig config and must be recovered first. (3) Panel (c) shows a slight CL excess of disturbance power in 2–4 Hz — check it is not the controller *injecting* at that band, which would be a different story from amplifying an existing disturbance.

### 2026-08-13 — Rainier rig: `timer_dt` stores absolute epoch time, not per-frame dt (found while planning live-GUI demo panels)
**Changed/Found:** No code change yet. In `StLab_Rainier/experiment_core/mp_controller.py` `_mp_reader`, `T = 0` is set once before the acquisition loop (line 161) and **never reassigned**, so `self.timer_dt[0, self.kk] = time.time() - T` (line 170) writes an absolute epoch timestamp every control sample rather than the inter-frame interval the name implies. Consequence: any past reading of `timer_dt` as a latency trace was wrong; but `np.diff(timer_dt)` recovers the true inter-sample interval, so the array is still a usable jitter instrument. Relevant because the planned live-GUI demo panels (trial-locked tracking trace + per-mode running average, video-style) add work to the plot thread inside **Process A**, which shares the GIL with the time-critical `_mp_reader` that copies each frame into shared memory and releases `_frame_sem` for the PID process — the one place a plotting change can actually cost control latency.
**Why:** The user's constraint is "without losing latency". `timer_dt` is the only existing per-sample timing record, so fixing/renaming it and dumping p50/p95/p99/max of the inter-sample interval turns that constraint into an A/B measurement (panels off vs on, 28.57 ms nominal at 35 Hz) instead of an assertion.

### 2026-08-13 — Reframe: Part 1's delta result is a WATERBED signature, not just "a factor feedback fails on"
**Changed/Found:** No code change — a reinterpretation of an existing result, recorded before it gets written up the weaker way. In `factor_slope_delta24` the two loops have **opposite signs**: OL slope **−0.474** (open-loop error *decreases* with relative 2-4 Hz power) vs CL **+0.847** (closed-loop error *increases*). A controller that merely lacked an internal model of that band would leave the OL slope untouched (S≈1, no rejection, no harm); a slope that flips sign means feedback is actively making 2-4 Hz **worse** — which is the Bode-integral/waterbed prediction, not a null. Meanwhile motion, a slow quasi-DC nuisance, is fully decoupled (OL +0.652 → CL −0.016, p=0.0020), which is the integrator's internal model of a constant doing its job. So Part 1, read through the Internal Model Principle, already says: the loop contains a model of DC and rejects it; it contains no oscillatory mode, and pays for the low-frequency suppression at 2-4 Hz.
**Why:** Fig 4's argument is being built as an IMP argument, and this is the strongest existing evidence for it — currently presented as a state-dependence result, which undersells it.
**Next:** The claim is not established until rejection is resolved in FREQUENCY — the current Part-2 metric (ER, a scalar over 0-3 s) cannot distinguish "rejects everything by 30%" from "rejects DC perfectly and amplifies 3 Hz", and that distinction *is* the IMP result. Proposed: empirical sensitivity S(f) = T_CL(f)/T_OL(f) with T = ⟨|E(f)|²⟩/⟨|D(f)|²⟩, E = A−ref, D = G−ref, from `imp_build_session`'s Aol/Gol/Acl/Gcl. ⚠ Two things to check first: (a) the ridge Global leaks ~23% and the leak is SLOW, which inflates D at low f and therefore biases S *downward* there — i.e. anti-conservative for the DC claim, so it must be bounded (the retired deflate Global is the natural bound); (b) 3 s windows give ~0.33 Hz bins, so below ~1 Hz there are only 1-3 cycles and the estimate is weak.

### 2026-08-13 — Diagnosed and FIXED the quartile-panel artifact: within-session normalization + session-level error bars
**Changed/Found:** Diagnosed the 1-2 Hz control panel problem properly and fixed it rather than working around it. **The mechanism is not what my first note said.** Session-mean δ predicts session-mean CL RMSE about equally for BOTH bands (rel 2-4 Hz r_s=+0.66 p=0.009; rel 1-2 Hz r_s=+0.61 p=0.019, n=15 sessions), so pooling raw trial RMSE lets each session's overall difficulty leak into the quartile means — **and it leaks by a different amount per band, in opposite directions**. Replicating the panel's own binning exactly and splitting each trend: **2-4 Hz** pooled Q4−Q1 = +0.32 but session-centred **+0.43** (between-session structure was *hiding* 25% of the real effect); **1-2 Hz** pooled +0.34 but session-centred **+0.16** (between-session structure *manufactured* 52% of it). Two errors pointing opposite ways, compressing effect and control to look identical (+0.32 vs +0.34) when the within-session truth is +0.43 vs +0.16 — a 2.7× difference. Per-session Q4−Q1 confirms: 2-4 Hz median +0.27, signrank p=0.018, 11/15 sessions positive; 1-2 Hz median +0.02, p=0.76, 8/15 (a coin flip). **Second, independent defect: the error bars were the wrong unit** — trial-SEM 0.042 vs session-SEM 0.120–0.131, i.e. **~3× too small**, because trials within a session are not independent; this affected every panel in the family, including the good ones.
**Changed:** `cl_factor_claim_panels.m` and `cl_factor_olcl_panels.m` now accumulate per-session bin means and each session's level, and plot session-centred means with the grand mean added back (axis stays %ΔF/F) and **SEM across sessions**. The session level is the mean over its OL *and* CL trials together, so subtracting it removes difficulty without touching the OL−CL gap or the quartile trend. `CLM_WITHIN` reverts. **Result: the 2-4 Hz CL series rises 1.88→2.21 while the 1-2 Hz CL series is flat (2.04, 2.09, 2.08, 2.07)** — the dissociation is now visible, and the two panels can sit side by side, which is the clearest statement of it in the figure. Two z-score leftovers also caught and fixed in the same pass: the claim-3 slopes were still z-scored per window (printed +0.297/+0.089; now raw **+0.275/+0.042**, matching `cl_factor_slope_panels` exactly), and the mixed-effects outcome was z-scored (now raw: **+0.158 %ΔF/F per SD of rel24 [0.065, 0.251], t=3.33, p=0.00092** — t and p unchanged, only units).
**Why:** user asked for a fuller explanation of the flagged problem and a suggestion. The honest answer needed the decomposition, not an assertion — and once measured, the fix was obvious and better than the workaround (which was "never show the control panel next to the effect panel").
**Next:** (1) The `_slope` panels are unaffected (they were always per-session) — the two families now agree by construction rather than by luck. (2) PAPER.md red-flag line replaced with the resolution. (3) Shared y-axis for `factor_slope_motion` / `factor_slope_delta24` still outstanding.

**Changed/Found:** New `utils/cl_quartile_line.m` — shared neuroscience-style quartile panel (mean ± SEM as points joined by lines, y-axis fitted to the data rather than anchored at 0, box off / ticks out / 6 pt bold, legend northoutside). `cl_factor_claim_panels.m` (`mk_ol_cl`, `mk_earlylate`) and `cl_factor_olcl_panels.m` now both call it; ~60 lines of duplicated bar-drawing deleted. **The mark type had to change before the axis could be cropped:** a bar encodes value as length from zero, so a cropped bar chart misstates every ratio on it; a point encodes position and carries no claim about zero, which is what makes the crop legitimate. ### 2026-08-13 — PROJECT RULE: RMSE is never z-scored. Removed from every Fig-4 Part-1 script; two effects strengthen
**Changed/Found:** Per user ("RMSE needs to be positive, and individual-session variability should not be normalized"), stripped outcome z-scoring from the whole Part-1 family: `cl_factor_slope_panels.m` (pooled OL+CL `zpool` → identity; the within-CL Early/Late z-scoring in the init-dev branch → raw; y-label `z-RMSE` → `RMSE`), `cl_factor_olcl_panels.m` (per-session pooled z removed from the slope stat), `cl_factor_claim_panels.m` (`zwin` → identity), `cl_factor_decomp_panel.m`, `cl_rmse_factor_windows.m`, `cl_mse_factors.m` (all three: `y = zscore(...)` → raw). Also dropped the `_z` panel variants from `cl_factor_olcl_panels.m` and `cl_factor_claim_panels.m` — they plotted the same panels in the forbidden units — and moved the 14 stale `_z` files to `paper/images/figure4/_archive_zscored/` (moved, not deleted; they are no longer reproducible since the code paths are gone).
**Found — removing the normalization made two results STRONGER and changed none of the decomposition:** **rel 2–4 Hz OL-vs-CL went from p=0.0125 \* to p=0.0067 \*\*** (OL −0.474 / CL +0.847) and the **init-dev Early→Late slope collapse went from ~3× to ~7×** (+0.275 → +0.042, late still ≠0 at p=0.002), which now sits much closer to its 13× unique-R² collapse. Motion unchanged (p=0.0020 \*\*), and the 1–2 Hz specificity null stayed null (p=0.76). The **unique-R² decomposition is bit-identical** (init-dev 0.381/0.029, motion 0.001/0.001, rel 2–4 Hz 0.089/0.122, R²_full 0.407/0.132) because R² is invariant to linear rescaling of the outcome — the change is that the code no longer *looks* like it normalizes away session variability, and the slope panels (which are not scale-invariant) are now consistent with it. Mixed-effects on the current pool also improved: **rel24 +0.127 [0.052, 0.202], t=3.33, p=0.00092, 852 trials / 15 sessions / 4 animals** (was p=0.004 on 752 / 13 / 2).
**Why:** the pooled z divided each session by its own SD, which left the within-session OL/CL ratio intact but rescaled every session onto a common yardstick — discarding the across-session spread in tracking quality that the figure is partly about. It also put a positive quantity on a signed axis.
**Next:** grep the Fig-3/Fig-5 scripts for the same pattern before drafting — this rule was applied to Part 1 only, and `variance_mse.m` / the sine panels have not been checked.

### 2026-08-13 — LOCKED: ridge is the project predictor; rank and deflate retired
**Changed/Found:** `utils/ctrl_pred_tag.m` — default mode flipped `'rank'` → `'ridge'`, so any script run without `CTRL_PRED` set now reads the ridge caches (verified: `ctrl_pred_tag()` returns `ridge`/`_ridge`, 13 caches present). Header rewritten: ridge documented as THE project model, `'rank'` and `'deflate'` marked RETIRED but still reachable as revert switches (all three keep their own cache suffix, so nothing was overwritten — 13 rank + 13 ridge + 13 deflate caches all intact on disk). `run_fig4.m` `RUN_PRED` comment updated to say locked-not-provisional. `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m:223-224` deflate branch tagged retired. `ctrl_deflate_check.m` and `ctrl_reject_models.m` given RETIRED headers — kept as the *record of why* deflate was rejected and as the robustness exhibit, not as pipeline steps. Confirmed `data/imp_reject_across_sessions.mat` is byte-equal to the `_ridge` aggregate, then re-ran `f4_reject_panels.m` under ridge so the exported figure-4 panels match the locked model: OL 0.291 [IQR 0.172] → CL 0.203 [IQR 0.116], CL better 13/13, signrank p=0.000244, mean gain +0.100 [95% CI +0.069, +0.136].
**Why:** user decision ("keep ridge only") after the three-way comparison. Ridge is the only one of the three that is *fully stim-blind* — neither the fit nor the λ selection ever sees a laser-on trial — whereas deflate's constraint direction `d` is measured on stim trials, which makes its flat Global and 100% Local the constraint restated rather than a result. Every residual bias ridge carries points away from the conclusion: its Global still leaks (median 23%), which understates the disturbance and therefore *under*-reports rejection. A one-model pipeline also removes the mixing hazard — a ridge Global scored against a rank decomposition compares nothing.
**Next:** none for the switch itself. The deflate work is not wasted and should be cited, not re-derived: leak is driven by the single scalar `b'·dip` (Spearman −0.91 with leak%, 0.89 with the Global trough, vs 0.51 for ‖b‖), and the CL/OL contrast moves only 0.682 → 0.697 across models (signrank p=0.305, CL better 13/13 under both) — that pair is the answer to "did the model choice choose the answer".

### 2026-08-12 — Disturbance rejection under both models: the OL-vs-CL CONTRAST is model-independent, the absolute level is not
**Changed/Found:** ran `imp_reject_across_sessions` under both disturbance models (ridge and deflate), saved both aggregates, and added `controller-analysis/ctrl_reject_models.m` `[REJMOD]` to compare them paired over the 13 common sessions. **Absolute ER moves a lot** — OL 0.291 → **0.205**, CL 0.203 → **0.139** (medians) — because the leak sits in the ER denominator: a dipping Global is closer to ref, understating the disturbance. Under the leak-free model the Global dip drops from −1.033 ± 0.815 to **+0.098 ± 0.115 %ΔF/F**, and the fraction of trials doing work rises to OL 100% / CL 100% (was OL 98%). **The CL/OL ratio barely moves: 0.682 → 0.697 (median), signrank p = 0.305, CL better in 13/13 under BOTH models.** Per session the leak was hiding a median **19%** of the OL rejection (range 5–68%, worst on 0304 at 68%, 0226 53%, AL_0039_0419 50%).
**Why:** this is the algebra made explicit and it is the most useful robustness result so far. The leak lives in the denominator that OL and CL SHARE, so it scales both ER values together and cancels in the contrast. That means the paper's actual claim — closed loop rejects more than open loop — does not depend on which contra predictor is used, while any absolute "the controller removes X% of the disturbance" statement does. Quote the contrast; treat the absolute level as bracketed by the two models (OL 0.205–0.291, CL 0.139–0.203).
**Next:** decide which model supplies the Fig-4 numbers. Recommendation: ridge for the headline (conservative — it under-reports rejection) with deflate as the stated upper bound, since deflate's flat Global is imposed rather than measured.

### 2026-08-14 — Fit-window scoping test: two runs killed, then designed properly (`opts.forceOrder`)
**Changed/Found:** `utils/imp_tf_fit_session.m` gains `opts.forceOrder = [np nz nd]`, collapsing the (nd,np,nz) sweep to a single fit. Reason: the question "is the 0.5 s fit window too short to identify τ_slow?" was attacked twice by re-running `imp_tf_run` at `tFit_s` 1.0/1.5 s, and **both runs exceeded 30 min and had to be killed** (one at nBoot=300, one at nBoot=50). The cost driver is not the bootstrap — it is the **~100 `tfest` calls per session** in the order sweep, each of which slows with window length. The sweep is irrelevant to a question about the window, and holding the order fixed also removes a confound: with a free sweep, a τ change between windows could be the selected ORDER moving rather than the window. Scoping script staged at `scratchpad/tf_window_scope.m`: orders pinned at the ones AIC/R²h chose at 0.5 s ([3 1 0; 4 3 0; 4 3 0; 4 2 0]), windows 0.5/1.0/1.5 s, nBoot 40 — 12 cells at ~1 fit each instead of ~100.
**Why:** the rejection fractions at 0.5 s are 42/50/2/50%, so three of four sessions have a τ CI whose upper bound is the censoring bound rather than a measurement. Whether that is fixable by a longer window is the difference between reporting τ with a caveat and reporting it properly.
**Next:** run the staged script (not yet run — MATLAB was still busy with the second killed job). If rejection collapses at 1.0–1.5 s, move `RUN_TFIT` and re-fit; if it does not, τ_slow is simply weakly identified in this preparation and the panel must say so. Do NOT re-run the full sweep to answer this.

### 2026-08-13 — τ bootstrap was blowing up, and it was manufacturing the "one shared time constant" conclusion
**Changed/Found:** `utils/imp_tf_fit_session.m` — with 4 sessions the trial bootstrap returned non-physical time constants: **25% of resamples above 1000 s in AL_0041 e1, 17% in AL_0048, 3.4% in AL_0041 e2** (AL_0033 clean at 0%), max 9.5e15 s. Cause: a resample whose slowest pole lands marginally stable (real part → 0⁻) gives τ → ∞. Consequences, both bad: (a) `tauCI` upper bounds of 1e9–1e12 s, so TF-A's x-axis ran to 1e10 s and the panel was unreadable; (b) `tauSD` = **1.4e14 s**, and since the reported between/within RATIO divides by that SD, the summary printed **"ratio 0.00 → consistent with ONE shared time constant"** regardless of the data. That conclusion was an artefact of the blow-up. Fix: resamples with τ longer than the **fitted window** are dropped as non-identifiable (`opts.tauMax`, default = window length — a time constant longer than the observation window is not measurable from it), with the rejected fraction counted and printed. **After the fix the conclusion reverses: ratio 1.55 → "mild inter-session variability", within-session SD 0.097 s, between 0.151 s.**
**Why:** found while adding τ_fast to TF-A — reading `tauCI`'s definition to get row 2 exposed both this and the column-major slip logged below.
**Next:** **the rejection fractions are 42 / 50 / 2 / 50%** at the current `tFit_s = 0.5 s`, so for three sessions the CI's upper bound is essentially the censoring bound (471/502/478/498 ms against a 510 ms cut), not a measurement. That is because τ_slow is 0.30–0.54 s, i.e. the fit window is barely ONE time constant long. Added `RUN_TFIT` to `imp_tf_run.m` to test a longer window; **the 1.5 s test run has not completed** — it is far more expensive than the 0.5 s fit (more samples × 5 poles × 4 zeros × 4 delays × 300 bootstraps × 4 sessions) and exceeded 30 min. Re-test with `RUN_NBOOT = 60` for scoping before committing to a window change. Until then, quote τ point estimates with the rejection fraction, not the upper CI.

**Changed/Found:** `utils/imp_tf_robust_fig.m` — `imp_tf_fit_session` returns `tauCI` as **[maxPoles × 2]** (row = pole, col = bound). ### 2026-08-12 — imp_state_trialvar.m: matched sham-peak control — motion tightens the RESPONSE, not just the measurement
**Changed/Found:** `impulse-analysis/imp_state_trialvar.m` — the stim-free control was a ~34-sample mean of the whole pre window, SD-normalised, compared against a DV (`Peak_imp`, `peak_mode=3`) that is a **7-sample window mean**. Different statistic, different length, both forced to SD≈1 — so the magnitude comparison was meaningless. Replaced with a **matched sham peak**: same statistic, same 7 samples, window at −1.0 s (i.e. OUTSIDE the −0.5→0 s baseline `dfImp` has already had removed; a sham inside the baseline is partially constrained toward zero — measured var 8.0 inside vs 17.3 outside). Added a variance decomposition in RAW ΔF/F at the motion threshold split, by **regression not subtraction** (obs and sham correlate r≈+0.39, so `var(obs) − var(sham)` assumes an independence that does not hold): fit `obs ~ b·sham` on low-motion trials, apply that b to both groups, compare residual variance. Result — var(obs) hi/lo **0.14**, var(sham) **0.25**, var(**residual**) **0.18**; per session 0.25 / 0.36 / 0.14. Correlation-row control also moves: Motion ρ −0.128 (stim) vs −0.083 (control), stim now the larger; threshold split SD ratio 0.38 stim vs 0.58 control.
**Why:** the user's objection (2026-08-12) was right about framing — the claim is that motion makes the *stim response* more predictable, and a quieter baseline "is of no consequence". My original control was posed as a specificity test, which is the wrong test. But a control is still needed for a *different* reason: `dev` is measured on the raw trace, so var(dev) = response variability + ongoing activity sitting inside the window. If motion only shrank the second term, the measurement would be cleaner without the response being more reproducible — and the two look identical in var(dev) alone. The residual falls MORE than the ongoing signal does (0.18 < 0.25), so the response itself is genuinely more reproducible.

### 2026-08-12 — ctrl_deflate_check.m: the four non-circular numbers behind the deflated model; bigger dips ARE more removable
**Changed/Found:** new `controller-analysis/ctrl_deflate_check.m` `[DEFCHK]` — read-only, needs both ridge and deflate caches. Four panels, chosen because the deflated model's headline (Global flat, Local 100%) is the constraint and therefore says nothing: **(a)** held-out leak removal per session, **(b)** the R² price of blindness, ridge vs deflate, **(c)** the **bracket** — ridge Local as a lower bound against deflate Local as the ceiling, **(d)** removal vs the leak it started from. Also drew the deflate fit figures for all 13 sessions. **New result in (d): sessions with a bigger ridge leak lose more of it out of sample, Spearman r_s = 0.58, p = 0.040.** So the constraint is not removing a constant amount of noise — it bites hardest exactly where there is a real dip to remove, which is the pattern a genuine stim direction should produce and trial-noise fitting should not.
**Numbers:** held-out removal median 69% (range −16…93, 6/13 below 50%); R² cost median 0.017, worst 0.199; **Local bracket median 77% → 100%, median width 23 points.** The seven sessions above 69% removal are 0212, AL_0039_0420, 0320, 0224, 0304, 0226, AL_0039_0419 — and they are also the ones with the widest brackets, i.e. where the ridge leak was doing the most damage.
**Why:** panel (d) is what turns "the constraint works on average" into an argument. Without it, a median 69% removal is equally consistent with the constraint soaking up trial noise on every session. The correlation with the pre-existing leak is the discriminating evidence. Fixed a legend bug on the way (13 grey bracket bars were entering the legend as data1…data13).
**Next:** decide whether to report the bracket as the headline for the Local-share claim. If so, quote median 77–100% with the per-session held-out removal as the quality flag, and never the deflate figure alone.

### 2026-08-12 — Leak traced to ONE scalar (b'·dip); new 'deflate' model zeroes it — but the resulting "Local 100%" is DEFINITIONAL, not a result
**Changed/Found:** diagnosed what actually drives the Global dip across the 13 ridge sessions. It is not `‖b‖`: it is **`b'·dip`, the alignment of the weights with the per-pixel contra co-suppression pattern** — Spearman **−0.91** with leak% and **0.89** with the Global trough, against 0.51 for `‖b‖` and 0.34 for R². Shrinkage was only ever an indirect handle. Added `utils/ctrl_deflate.m` and a third `CTRL_PRED` mode **'deflate'** = ridge plus one linear equality constraint `d'b = 0`, closed-form (`b_c = b − A\d (d'A\d)^{-1} d'b`), where `d` is the contra stim direction built in the same z-scored coordinates and with the same per-trial baselining as a real trial — so `d'b` *is* Global's stim-window deflection. Built for all 13; caches are `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind_deflate_*.mat`, so ridge and rank are untouched.
**Result, and the caveat that governs it:** sustained leak is **0% on 13/13 and Local reads 100%** — **by construction, because that is the constraint.** Those numbers must never be quoted as a finding. The only honest number is the held-out test (`d` estimated on ODD trials, leak scored on EVEN trials, both cached): **median 69% of the leak removed, range −16% to +93%, with 6/13 sessions below 50%** and AL_0048 actually worse out-of-sample. R² cost: median 0.017, but 0.199 on AL_0033_0305_e2 and 0.120 on AL_0039_0419_e1.
**Why:** `d` can only be measured with the laser on, so this predictor is no longer stim-blind in the strict sense the rank and ridge models were — it is fit on laser-off frames but forbidden a direction measured with the laser on. Forcing Global flat mechanically inflates Local, which is precisely the circularity a referee would attack, hence the odd/even guard.
**Next:** do NOT promote 'deflate' to primary. Best use is as a **bound**: ridge (leak present, Local under-reported) and deflate (leak removed, Local at its ceiling) bracket the true Local share. Report the pair. Also: the constraint targets the 0–3 s window, so the transient sub-window still leaks 0–16% — that residual is real and worth reporting rather than tightening away.

### 2026-08-12 — RAW state units in `imp_state_trialvar.m` — and the motion threshold split REVISES H1: the effect is not specific to the stimulus
**Changed/Found:** user: "lets not z score the states as they seem uninterpretable". `imp_state_trialvar.m` now uses RAW state values by default (`STV_ZSTATE=false`), so axes read in physical units — motion z-score, pre-trial variance (ΔF/F)², abs δ (ΔF/F)², rel δ as a fraction of 0.5–30 Hz. Row-2 x-positions moved to each bin's MEDIAN RAW VALUE, row-3 now plots the stim bar BESIDE its stim-free control bar. Raw pooling can in principle be manufactured by between-session offsets, so added a **session-stratified ρ** (weighted mean of within-session correlations, which never compares sessions) plus a sign-agreement count. All four markers: pooled and stratified agree to ≤0.01 and 4/4 sessions agree in sign, so between-session structure is not driving anything.
**Raw pooled results:** Motion ρ=−0.128 (strat −0.115), SD ratio 0.64 [0.53–0.76]; Pre-var +0.445 (ctrl **+0.526**); Abs δ +0.417 (ctrl **+0.442**); Rel δ +0.078, BF p now **0.057, n.s.** (ctrl +0.222). Per session, motion: −0.195\*, −0.210\*, **−0.057 n.s. (AL_0033)**, −0.147\* — the primary session no longer reaches significance on its own under raw scaling.
**⭐ NEW SECTION (2b), and it changes the H1 verdict.** RAW motion is threshold-shaped: median −0.196, q75 −0.158, only 56 of 1767 trials (3%) exceed z=1.5. Equal-count quartiles therefore put bins 1–3 inside a **0.10-wide sliver** of motion, so the quartile "trend" across them is noise and the quartile SD ratio is not a clean contrast. Added a two-group split at the LOCKED project constant `motThresh = 1.5`:
| | low motion (n=1711) | high motion (n=56) | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| SD, impulse response | 1.007 | 0.385 | **0.38** (BF p=2.7e−5) |
| SD, **stim-free control** | 1.007 | 0.402 | **0.40** (BF p=1.3e−5) |
**⚠ REVISION TO H1.** Motion genuinely lowers trial-to-trial variability — 2.6× compression, robust, replicating in the 3 sessions with enough high-motion trials (0.37 / 0.44 / 0.31; AL_0048 has only 2 such trials). **But the stim-free baseline compresses by the SAME factor.** So it is NOT a statement about how the stimulus is processed: motion reduces the variability of the ongoing signal and the impulse response inherits it. The earlier "PASS, beats its control" verdict came from the quartile contrast, whose bins are degenerate; the threshold split is the cleaner test and it shows no specificity. The script now prints this as an explicit warning.
**Convergence:** three independent routes now agree that the motion effect is not local/stimulus-specific — (1) signed Peak dev has zero directional component (r=0.003), (2) matched-DV `f2_state` gives ACTUAL −0.154 ≈ GLOBAL −0.157 > LOCAL −0.099, (3) this threshold split, 0.38 stim vs 0.40 control.
**Why:** interpretable axes were the ask; the degenerate binning it exposed was not visible while the states were z-scored, which is itself an argument for the change.
**Next:** the defensible H1 is "motion reduces variability of the widefield signal generally, including the impulse response", NOT "motion reduces variability of the impulse response specifically". Decide whether that is worth a panel. `STV_ZSTATE=true` restores the old scaling for comparison. Code Analyzer clean.

### 2026-08-12 — ⭐ NEW `imp_state_trialvar.m`: H1 (motion → lower variability) CONFIRMED in 4/4 sessions; H2/H3 fail their stim-free control
**Changed/Found:** NEW `impulse-analysis/imp_state_trialvar.m` — merges the state analyses of `motion_analysis.m` and `prestim_variance.m` into one script that tests the user's claim directly. DV = SIGNED `Peak_imp − mean(Peak_imp)` scaled by the within-amp SD (signed for display, so the funnel is visible); statistics are SCALE tests (Spearman of |dev| vs state, a Levene score about the within-amp centre) because 2026-08-12 established these are spread effects with no directional component. All four markers computed from the SAME strictly pre-onset window [−1, −0.03] s, so no marker overlaps the response the DV is measured in (RESEARCH A4: strictly-pre reproduces 'peri'). State markers z-scored within session × amplitude. 1767 trials, 4 sessions.
**⭐ THE STIM-FREE CONTROL is what makes the claim falsifiable.** Every test is repeated on a pre-onset, stim-free quantity built identically (deviation of the pre-window mean from its amp-mean). If a state predicts the spread of the stim-free control as strongly as the response, the effect is ongoing signal amplitude, not stimulus processing.
| marker | ρ(&#124;dev&#124;, state) | p | SD ratio top/bottom [95% CI] | stim-free ctrl ρ | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Motion** | **−0.135** | 1.3e−8 | **0.68 [0.56–0.79]** | −0.099 | **PASS** |
| Pre-trial variance | +0.453 | ~0 | 3.11 [2.79–3.55] | **+0.544** | POWER CONFOUND |
| Abs δ power | +0.416 | ~0 | 2.39 [1.99–2.93] | **+0.440** | POWER CONFOUND |
| Rel δ | +0.082 | 5e−4 | 1.25 [1.09–1.42] | **+0.213** | pass, but BELOW its control |
**H1 CONFIRMED.** Motion lowers trial-to-trial variability: SD ratio 0.68 with a bootstrap CI excluding 1, Brown-Forsythe p=1.9e−11, monotone trend −0.80, and it **replicates in all four sessions** (−0.173\*, −0.184\*, −0.119\*, −0.137\*, all p<0.05). It also exceeds its stim-free control (0.135 vs 0.099) — though only modestly, and the binned curves overlap in bins 1–3, so part of the motion effect is a general signal-amplitude effect and the claim should be stated as "larger for the response than for baseline", not "specific to the response".
**H2/H3 are NOT supported in the sense intended.** Pre-var and absolute δ ARE signal power and the DV is a spread, so "same or higher" is close to true by construction — and decisively, **their stim-free control EXCEEDS the stim effect** (0.544 > 0.453; 0.440 > 0.416). Same for relative δ, the power-independent marker: **+0.082 stim vs +0.213 control, a 2.6× larger effect on baseline than on the response.**
**The interesting reframing this exposes:** for every high-power state marker the impulse response is LESS state-modulated than ongoing activity is. Rather than "delta/variance leave variability the same or higher", the defensible statement is that **the impulse response is relatively STABILISED against high-power states compared with the baseline signal** — a stronger and more interesting claim than H2/H3 as posed, and one the stim-free control actually supports.
**Why:** user asked to finalise the two scripts into one that checks the claim and makes figures. Figures → `impulse-analysis/figs/state_trialvar/` (`stv_claim.png` 3×4 panels: funnel, spread-vs-state with control, effect size vs claim; `stv_persession.png` replication). Power confounds are greyed in the figure and never interpreted. Code Analyzer clean.
**Next:** decide whether the paper states H1 as "motion reduces response variability" (supported, 4/4) and replaces H2/H3 with the stabilisation framing. `imp_state_trialvar` supersedes the state analyses in `motion_analysis.m`/`prestim_variance.m`; those still own their other panels, so do not delete them.

### 2026-08-12 — ⭐ SIGNED Peak dev in motion_analysis + prestim_variance: both "state effects" are pure SPREAD, with ZERO directional component
**Changed/Found:** user asked for `Peak_imp − mean(Peak_imp)` **without the absolute value**, to expose directionality. Applied to `impulse-analysis/motion_analysis.m` and `impulse-analysis/prestim_variance.m` at every deviation site (5 in motion, 4 in prestim), plus: symmetric y-limits about 0 (the old `ylim` clamp `max(yl(1),−2)` assumed a floor at 0 and would have CLIPPED real negative trials), zero reference lines, `|Peak dev|` → `Peak dev` labels, and a metric-aware `dev_ylabel` in prestim_variance (its labels hard-coded "Prediction error" even after the cperr→peakdev fallback flips the metric). Sign convention documented in-file: **>0 = SHALLOWER dip than the amp average (less inhibition), <0 = DEEPER**.
**⚠ Computed from `Peak_imp` directly, NOT from `imp.Peak_imp_dev`** — that field is `abs(...)` in `load_experiments.m:355` but **signed** in `load_bilateral_impulse.m:224`, so it does not mean the same thing across sessions. Latent inconsistency, still unfixed at the loader level; also consumed by `spectral_heatmap.m` and the two detail callbacks.
**RESULT — MOTION: the directional effect is exactly zero.** Pooled all sessions/all amps **r = 0.003, p = 0.894 (n=1767)**, vs a strong effect under `|Peak dev|` (the 2026-06 headline: median |Peak dev| No-mot 1.23 vs Mot 0.59, p=9e−11). AL_0033 per-amp r spans −0.09…+0.04, all n.s. The scatters show why: high-motion trials cluster TIGHTLY on zero while low-motion trials spread ±10 in BOTH directions. **Motion compresses the deviation distribution symmetrically — `abs()` converted a variance effect into an apparent mean effect.**
**RESULT — PRE-STIM VARIANCE: same story, and worse.** AL_0033 (the only session judged valid) is n.s. at all 10 amplitudes (r −0.15…+0.10, p 0.17–0.97). AL_0041 e1 has significant effects with BOTH SIGNS across amplitudes (0.80 V r=−0.39 p=0.008; 1.60 V r=**+0.32** p=0.027; 2.40 V r=−0.35 p=0.007), which reads as noise rather than an effect. AL_0048 1.00 V r=−0.32 p=0.001. Quintile curves are mostly inverted-U with Q5 dropping — the signature of symmetric spreading, not a directional shift.
**Why this matters:** it corroborates today's independent f2 result (matched-DV `f2_state`: motion ACTUAL −0.154 ≈ GLOBAL −0.157 > LOCAL −0.099) from a completely different code path and DV. Both routes now say the motion effect is about SPREAD and lives in the network. **The "motion → more predictable" finding is a VARIANCE claim and must be stated as one** — `|Peak dev|` is a spread statistic presented as a mean.
**Verification:** both scripts run clean (Code Analyzer: only a pre-existing preallocation info at motion_analysis:132). `paperRoot` was redirected to the scratchpad for the test run, so **no paper asset was overwritten**. Two pre-existing standalone-run blockers surfaced in prestim_variance: `fs` (line ~354) and `nBands` (line ~376) come from the monolith's parameter cell and are not set by `load_experiments`.
**Next:** re-export 2F/2G/2H from the signed version once the metric question is settled. Fix the loader-level `Peak_imp_dev` abs-vs-signed inconsistency, or delete the field so nothing can consume it ambiguously. Decide whether the paper states motion as a variance effect (supported) or drops the directional framing entirely.

### 2026-08-12 — 🔴 `dev_metric='cperr'` SILENTLY FALLS BACK to peakdev: paper panel 2F is labelled "Prediction error" but plots |Peak dev|
**Changed/Found:** `motion_analysis.m` and `prestim_variance.m` both default to `dev_metric='cperr'`, guarded per-amp by `strcmp(dev_metric,'cperr') && isfield(imp_e,'cp_err') && ~isempty(...)`. **`imp.cp_err` is never produced anywhere in the repo** — a full-repo grep finds only consumption sites in these two scripts (plus an unrelated `utils/cp_error_heatmap.m`), and `allExperiments(k).imp` carries `Peak_imp / Peak_imp_dev / Peak_imp_mean` but no `cp_err`. It is created only by `contra_prediction.m`, which a plain `load_experiments` run never invokes. So the guard fails and every plot falls through to `Peak_imp_dev` — while `dev_tag` stays `'cperr'` and `dev_ylabel` stays `'Prediction error'` (that label is only corrected when `dev_metric=='peakdev'`).
**Evidence:** `prevar_vs_dev_allamps_motexcl_{,cperr_,peakdev_}AL_0033_2025-01-29_en1.pdf` are all exactly **23807 bytes** (different MD5 only because PDFs embed a creation timestamp) — three filenames, one plot. `imp_motion_devscatter_all_sessions_cperr.pdf` (panel **2F**, an ACTIVE Fig-2 paper panel per PAPER.md line 93) was regenerated today 15:10 under the mislabel. Supplementary `imp_motion_devscatter_cperr_*.png` likewise.
**Fixed:** added a loud fallback guard to both scripts — if no session carries `imp.cp_err`, warn and set `dev_metric`/`dev_tag` to `'peakdev'` so the axis label and filename match what is actually plotted. **Output content is unchanged**; only the tag/label are corrected. Panels exported before today under a `_cperr` name must be re-exported or re-labelled.
**Why (the question that surfaced it):** user asked whether the earlier trial-vs-trial-avg analyses used `L1DEVz`. **They do not.** `motion_analysis.m` / `prestim_variance.m` use `|Peak_imp − mean(Peak_imp)|` — a single PEAK scalar's deviation from the amp-mean peak, on the **ACTUAL** trace, in raw units. `L1DEVz` is `mean|r(t) − μ(t)|` over the whole dip window, on the **RESIDUAL**, z-scored within amplitude. Three differences at once (peak vs window-mean, Actual vs residual, raw vs z-within-amp), so numbers from the two streams are NOT comparable. Note `cp_agl.m` DOES use matched L1-dev across Actual/Global/Local, but normalises as a RATIO to the amp-mean (`x./mean(x)`) rather than z-within-amp — rank-identical within an amplitude, different once pooled ACROSS amplitudes.
**Next:** decide whether `cperr` should be implemented (run `contra_prediction.m` in the chain so `imp.cp_err` exists) or retired as a dead option. Re-export 2F. Corroborating note for the existing PAPER.md ⚠ on 2G/2H: with the matched L1 DV, pre-stim variance gives ACTUAL ρ=+0.721 and GLOBAL ρ=+0.700 vs LOCAL +0.287 — the power confound at its most extreme, exactly as those panels were flagged.

### 2026-08-12 — ROOT CAUSE of "only 9 ridge sessions": the 60000-frame cap DECIMATES the spontaneous list, killing every catch window
**Changed/Found:** rebuilt the ridge model for all sessions and the four missing ones failed identically — `ctrl_ridge_path: only 0 admissible catch windows`. Cause: `ctrl_ols_spont.m:319` caps the spontaneous set with `frames = frames(round(linspace(1,numel(frames),maxFrm)))`, an **evenly spaced decimation**. Above the 60000 cap that leaves no two consecutive samples anywhere, and catch windows require a contiguous peri-stim-shaped run entirely inside the laser-off set — so zero are admissible. It failed on exactly the four sessions sitting at the cap (0212, 0224, 0226, AL_0039_0419, all reporting 60000 frames) and succeeded on all nine below it (14598–59189). **Fix:** `ctrl_ridge_path` now takes `opts.spontMask`, and `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind` passes the UN-decimated laser-off mask rebuilt from the stim onsets via a new `local_spont_mask` helper replicating `ctrl_ols_spont`'s own rule. The ridge fit still uses the decimated `frames` through the Gram — only window admissibility needed contiguity, and contiguity is a property of the recording, not of the subsample. All four now build; the ridge set is **13 of 14** sessions.
**Why:** this had been an open question for two sessions of work ("why only 9?") and was unanswerable because the build log lived in a cleared workspace. It is a silent-truncation bug of the worst kind: the cap is a performance measure with no obvious connection to window contiguity, and the failure mode is total rather than degraded.
**Next:** AL_0039_0420_e2 (m13) is the one remaining failure and is unrelated — `data.dFk` is 91800 frames against 91875 in the SVD, a 75-frame gap that the ≤10-frame rounding tolerance rejects. Diagnose that separately; it has never had a Stage-2 cache in any mode.

### 2026-08-12 — ⚠⚠ BUG in the GLOBAL negative control: it used a MISMATCHED DV. Fixed — and it flips the MOTION verdict
**Changed/Found:** `utils/f2_state.m`. `local_globaldip` always returned the SIGNED dip mean, while the primary Local DV is `L1DEVz`, an UNSIGNED deviation from the amplitude mean. Those are different quantities, so "Local ρ vs Global ρ" was never a comparison — a signed level has no reason to track state the way an unsigned deviation does, which made **every** Global control look reassuringly small. Replaced with `local_compDV(tr, dcc, dv)`, computing the control with the SAME definition as `opt.dv` (L1DEVz / GAINz / DVz). Also added the **ACTUAL** (un-decomposed, trial vs trial-average) row using the same DV, because the ORDERING across Actual/Global/Local is the real result and Local alone cannot distinguish the two cases.
**AL_0033 e1, matched L1 DV, partial Spearman on `dev_pre` (n=748):**
| state | ACTUAL | LOCAL | GLOBAL | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Motion | −0.154 | −0.099 (p=0.0067) | **−0.157** | Actual≈Global > Local ⇒ **GLOBAL effect, decomposition DILUTES it** |
| Rel-δ | +0.095 | **+0.114 (p=0.0018)** | +0.056 (ns) | Local > Actual > Global ⇒ **ENRICHED by decomposition** |
| Pre-var | +0.721 | +0.287 | +0.700 | confound, plainly global |
| Abs-δ | +0.674 | +0.241 | +0.639 | confound, plainly global |
**⚠ RETRACTION.** Earlier today I reported "Motion ρ=−0.099 vs GLOBAL −0.037, ~3× the control, which is the point in its favour." **That margin was an artifact of the mismatched DV.** With the control matched, GLOBAL (−0.157) is LARGER than LOCAL (−0.099) and `f2_state`'s own leakage warning now fires. The motion effect is NOT local. This independently agrees with `f2_state_var`, which flagged motion as leakage by a completely different route (BF p Local 0.0027 vs Global 0.0066; trend −0.80 vs −1.00). **Any Global-control number quoted before this fix is void**, including the GLOBAL columns of the 4-session pooled table logged earlier today.
**Why it matters for Fig 2:** the Actual/Global/Local ordering is now the decisive display. Rel-δ is the ONLY marker where the effect is larger in the residual than in the un-decomposed trial — the only one where the decomposition buys anything. That is the first genuinely independent support rel-δ has had, and it lands at the same moment motion (the fallback ending proposed earlier today) is eliminated.

### 2026-08-12 — "CL+preview makes trials more reference-SHAPED" tested eight ways and is false; the trade-off plane is the honest version, and it is strong
**Changed/Found:** Scratch probes. **Every shape-normalised metric names OL+preview, in 3/3 sessions** — per-trial Pearson r with the reference (pooled medians OL 0.253 / OL+p **0.438** / CL 0.366 / CL+p 0.351; OL+p-vs-CL+p p=0.001, CL-vs-CL+p **p=0.56 n.s.**), phase-tolerant max-xcorr (OL+p 3/3), |1−T| at 1 Hz (OL+p 3/3), error power at f0 (OL+p 3/3), ensemble coherence (OL+p or no separation), leave-one-out template correlation (CL+p is **worst** pooled, 0.360, p=0.005 vs OL+p), and across-trial dispersion of the z-scored trace (CL+p worst on s2/s3). The one absolute-units measure that favours CL+p, "time on target" (fraction of window within ±2 %ΔF/F), ranks it first pooled (0.393 vs CL 0.375, OL+p 0.343, OL 0.329) but **CL-vs-CL+p p=0.58, OL+p-vs-CL+p p=0.15** — only OL-vs-CL+p reaches p=0.044. **Root cause, and it is structural: "shape" means dividing out offset and amplitude, and the offset term is exactly where CL+preview's advantage lives** (lowest DC error in 3/3 sessions, and 40–65% of total error power sits there). A shape metric cannot show a feedback benefit — by construction. **The defensible panel is the trade-off plane**: x = |1−T| at 1 Hz (waveform fidelity, preview moves a mode left), y = across-trial variance (reproducibility, feedback moves it down). Mode means OL (0.990, 22.34) · OL+p (0.406, 23.51) · CL (0.678, 17.52) · CL+p (0.556, 16.25). **CL+preview DOMINATES plain CL on both axes, and OL is dominated by both closed-loop modes; only OL+p and CL+p are non-dominated — in all 3 sessions.** Draft panel built (5.4 × 5.0).
**Why:** user asked for a marker showing CL+preview squeezes trials into the reference's shape. It does not, and I stopped generating new metrics rather than continue until one favoured the preferred mode — eight framings with a consistent answer is a result, not a failure to find the right statistic.
**Next:** the trade-off plane gives the intended claim rigorously — *CL+preview is the only mode that is simultaneously close in waveform and reproducible, and it beats plain closed-loop on both counts* — without asserting it is best on any single axis (it is not: OL+preview is the more faithful tracker). If adopted, it replaces or joins 5H (4.2 × 5.4 slot is free) and the Results/Discussion text needs the "only mode to engage both mechanisms" sentence upgraded to the dominance statement.

### 2026-08-12 — CORRECTION to the 0212 diagnosis: the frame is rotated, and the real defect is that the midline bisects the LASER SPOT
**Changed/Found:** the earlier entry today claimed AL_0033_0212_e2's midline "splits A/P, not L/R". **That rationale was wrong and is retracted.** `cp_roi_masks` bisects by the signed cross product of the midline direction, so the split is orientation-agnostic — a rotated midline is legitimate when the session's imaging frame is itself rotated, and 0212's *laser-effect map* is visibly rotated ~90° relative to every other session (the cerebellar notch sits on the right edge instead of bottom-centre). So the 90° angle is a property of the data, not an error. Two things are nevertheless established: (1) swapping `bx`↔`by` takes 0212's midline 90°→0° and its outline aspect 1.07→0.93 (others 0.89–0.95), i.e. its stored geometry is a coordinate-order **transpose** relative to the other files — it and 0224 are the only two legacy ROIs with no `frame`/`view_used` field, predating the 2026-08-10 `native_rc` convention; (2) the decisive defect is that **its midline passes 2 px from the laser centroid** — drawn straight through the stimulated territory, so the laser centroid lands outside `ipsi_mask`. Every healthy session puts the laser 74–134 px from its midline.
**Why:** the angle test I first used is frame-dependent — it would fail any legitimately rotated session while passing a midline drawn through the spot. Distance from the laser centroid to the midline is frame-independent and separates 0212 (2 px) from all 13 others (≥74 px) with no overlap. The user spotted the transpose from the contact sheet.
**Next:** redraw 0212 (`XD_SESS=2; XD_REDRAW='all'`) with the midline clear of the spot; its Stage-2 R² = 0.855 is invalid until then.

### 2026-08-12 — Coherence at 1 Hz REJECTED as a Fig-5 panel; |1−T| at the drive frequency proposed instead
**Changed/Found:** Scratch probes (not committed). **(a) Coherence fails three ways.** Ensemble magnitude-squared coherence across trials at 1 Hz, γ² = |⟨YR*⟩|²/(⟨|Y|²⟩⟨|R|²⟩), with 2000-resample bootstrap CIs: s1 OL 0.54 / OL+p 0.71 / CL 0.72 / CL+p 0.64; s2 0.74 / 0.75 / 0.71 / 0.62; s3 0.69 / 0.75 / 0.57 / 0.59. CIs are ±0.10 and overlap almost completely, so nothing is separated; where an ordering exists it runs **against** the claim (**CL+p is lowest in 2/3 sessions**); and γ² is an SNR-at-f0 measure, so **CL is penalised for deliberately running a smaller-amplitude response** (|T| 0.70 vs OL's 1.08 on s2) rather than for tracking worse. Per-trial coherence at a single bin is not even defined (one trial, one frequency ⇒ γ² ≡ 1); the closest well-defined per-trial quantity, the R² of a 1 Hz sinusoid fit, gives the same non-result (medians 0.30/0.28/0.29/0.22 on s2, CL+p lowest). **(b) `|1 − T(jω₀)|` works.** T = Y(f₀)/R(f₀) per trial, so |1−T| = 0 is perfect tracking in both amplitude and phase; it is referenced to the REFERENCE rather than to the response's own power, which is exactly the confound that sinks coherence. Pooled over 3 sessions: **OL 0.974 (n=136) → OL+p 0.408 (110), p=6.8e-24; CL 0.673 (100) → CL+p 0.563 (132), p=0.0038; OL vs CL p=2.5e-11; OL+p vs CL+p p=4.1e-5.** Every pairwise contrast significant, ordering identical in 3/3 sessions. Two draft panels built: per-trial distribution (4.2 × 5.4) and the complex plane with distance-from-(1,0) as the error (4.6 × 4.6).
**Why:** user asked for a coherence-with-the-drive panel to support "CL+preview is best". Coherence cannot carry it, and would visibly contradict it; |1−T| is the standard control-theory statement of the same question and separates cleanly.
**Next:** ⚠ **|1−T| makes the same correction the phase data already made, but with far more power: OL+preview is the most accurate tracker at the drive frequency, not CL+preview** (0.408 vs 0.563, p=4.1e-5, 3/3 sessions). Combined with CL+p's phase overshoot (−9°/+4.6°/−24°, i.e. LEAD, where OL+p sits near 0°), the supportable claim is a **trade-off plus a design result: the fixed 5-sample lookahead is matched to the open-loop plant, so it overcorrects once feedback has already removed part of the lag.** A horizon scheduled on loop configuration is the fix. Do not write "CL+preview is best on all axes" — no mode is: at-f0 → OL+p (3/3), broadband/variance → CL (2/3), offset → CL+p (3/3), total error power → CL+p (2/3), per-trial RMSE median → CL (2/3).
**Also answered:** the dots in the draft error-decomposition panel are the **per-session totals** (summed bar height for s1/s2/s3), not per-segment values — ambiguous as drawn; either drop them or split them per segment if that panel is adopted.

### 2026-08-12 — 🔴 AL_0033_0212_e2's MIDLINE IS DRAWN HORIZONTALLY — its "contra" mask is the anterior half of the whole brain
**Changed/Found:** added a brain underlay to the kernel panel of `ctrl_fit_figs.m` (Stage-1 `ipsi_mask`/`contra_mask` as a truecolor background, ROI outline + midline over it, hemispheres labelled), and it exposed the bug on sight. Dumped `mx`/`my` from all 14 `cp_roi2_ctrl_*.mat`: **AL_0033_0212_e2 is (row 282, col 158) → (row 282, col 352)** — constant ROW, so the midline runs along columns and bisects the brain **anterior/posterior**. Every other session has a near-constant column (270–316) with the row sweeping 100→370, i.e. a proper left/right split. Consequence: 0212's "contra" grid is the anterior half of the *whole* brain and includes ipsi-hemisphere pixels, so its held-out R² = 0.855 is partly a same-hemisphere self-prediction, not a contralateral one — and 0212 is one of only **three** sessions clearing the 0.85 floor.
**Why:** the midline is what defines contra vs ipsi (`cp_roi_masks` bisects by the signed cross product of the midline direction), so a 90°-rotated midline silently redefines the entire model input while every downstream number keeps looking healthy. Nothing in the numeric pipeline could catch this — it took drawing the brain.
**Next:** re-draw the ROI for AL_0033_0212_e2 (`ctrl_roi_draw_all.m`, redefine that session) and re-run Stages 1–2 for it; until then treat its R², leak and Local% as invalid, and re-check whether the 0.85 floor still has 3 passers or 2.
