Interior 24: rank **24/24**, cond **7.5e4**, 99% in 10. That retires the rank-deficiency caveat that qualified every connectivity claim in this thread — 24 ROIs read out of a 50-component SVD basis are no longer a degenerate set. **Model G re-run: the density result is not a rank artefact.** Held-out ell still monotone to **552/552 edges (100%)**, eBIC 516 (93%), all 69 lattice edges recovered, 75% of the graph off-lattice, cross-midline 52% = chance. **The weak locality signal is GONE on the interior nodes** — mean edge length 2.64 mm vs a null of 2.64, z ≈ 0 at every λ, against z = −3.4 to −5.9 on the full grid. So the only spatial structure the free fit ever found was carried by the perimeter sites, which is consistent with them being the anomalous channels rather than the informative ones. **Model H re-run: the apparent coupling was largely a perimeter effect** — off-diagonal coupling drops from **72.3% to 16.0%** of the self term, and the injection map cleans up markedly (left/right means +0.43/−0.69 → **+0.76/−0.85**, mixed-sign sites 25% → 17%). Synthetic recovery on the full-rank subset is essentially exact (edge AUC 1.000, corr(W) **0.999**, corr(B) 0.961, corr(h) **1.000**). **What does NOT change: the Green's-function failure** (on-site +0.334, peak map +0.089, off-diagonal +0.041, versus +0.33/+0.06/+0.04 on all 52) and the delta-collapsed kernels. Held-out MSE/ell are not comparable across node sets (different target), so only the structural statistics transfer.
**Why:** the perimeter sites are where the galvo spot can fall outside the imaged cortex, making them the least trustworthy channels both as stimulation targets and as readouts.
**Next:** **Use `--interior` as the default from here on** — full rank is worth more than the 28 discarded channels, and every previous claim about W or B was qualified by the deficiency. Two things to revisit under the new mask: the 2.63× on-site input-locality contrast and its excitatory/inhibitory split (logged earlier today on all 52, where the inhibitory half was carried largely by perimeter sites), and whether the GDAR/GVAR lattice comparison changes when the lattice is the interior-only one. The Green's-function failure is confirmed as a property of the objective, not of the node set, so the output-error refit remains the blocking item.

### 2026-08-10 — Model H (`hetgraph.py`): estimator verified on synthetic data, but the one-step objective collapses the node kernels to a delta and the fitted model fails the Green's-function test
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/hetgraph.py` — heterogeneous node LTI wrapped in a free directed graph, no topology imposed, per the approved spec. Node i is a bank of P=5 FIXED poles (τ 30 ms–2 s, log-spaced) with its own readout weights `w_i`; `v_i = Σ_m B_im u_m + Σ_j W_ij y_j`; stacked this is `x[t+1] = [(I⊗F) + (W⊗e)R] x[t] + (B⊗e)u[t]`, exact Kronecker when homogeneous. **8,320 parameters against GVAR-free's 27,040**, and it is simulatable. Fitted by ALS on precomputed pole-filtered cross-Grams (`G[r][s] = S^(r)S^(s)ᵀ`), so after one pass a sweep touches no data. Input uses `amp_mode='split'` (M=104, one channel per site×amplitude) so no dose linearity is assumed. **The estimator is verified: on data simulated from a known (Ω, W, B) at this record's length and SNR, edge-detection AUC = 1.000, corr(W)=0.961, corr(B)=0.921, corr(h)=0.876** — so the B-vs-W confound I flagged in the proposal IS separable by timing when the model is correct, and ALS converged to an identical SSE from 3 different random inits (not a local-optimum problem). **On the real data the model fails, and the failure is diagnostic. All 52 fitted kernels are the SAME near-delta** (sharp peak at lag 1, decayed by 100 ms, tiny undershoot; kernel peak time identical across every node) — the heterogeneity the model exists to provide is not used, and the model degenerates to a VAR(1) with 156 coefficients per equation. Consequently **its Green's function does not match the measured one: corr(on-site time course) = +0.33, corr(52×52 peak map) = +0.06, corr(off-diagonal peaks) = +0.04**, against the +0.93/+0.94 that trigger-averaged X gets versus the same H. Held-out one-step MSE 0.616 vs the VAR's 0.148; ρ = 1.0097. **The cause is the objective, not the model:** a one-step equation-error criterion rewards whatever maximises lag-1 predictability, and a delta kernel does exactly that, while multi-step behaviour is never scored. This is the same lesson as `freegraph.py` from the other direction. **Two findings survive and are worth keeping.** (1) **The injection map recovers the dual-opsin polarity with nothing about the midline anywhere in the fit**: mean injection balance **+0.43 on the left (excitatory) and −0.69 on the right (inhibitory)**, i.e. left sites drive positive and right sites negative, purely from B's fitted signs — and **25% of sites are mixed-sign (|balance| < 0.5)**, which is the signature the opsin-overlap hypothesis predicts. (2) **The dose response is sublinear, independently confirmed: median ‖B‖ ratio 1.64 for a 2× power step** (the VAR-side estimate was ~1.4, and `amp_mode='weight'` assumes 2.0); left-hemisphere ‖B‖ is also visibly larger than right, consistent with today's earlier finding that inhibitory-side direct drive is ~3× weaker. **One structural bug found and fixed by measurement:** the first version forbade self-loops (`W_ii = 0`) on the reasoning that self-dynamics belong in the kernel — but that forces all persistence to arrive from other nodes, and against a propagator already known to be ~96% diagonal it gave test MSE 0.62 and **ρ = 14.0**. `W_ii` is now free and is the node's own feedback; only W's off-diagonal is a network claim. Second bug: `_scale_to_rho`'s stability target must sit above max(pole) — at α=0 the open loop already has ρ = 0.986, so the initial 0.95 target bisected α to zero and silently produced a **"0 true edges"** synthetic test that reported nothing.
**Why:** user approved the model and said to run it. The Green's-function check was added because `freegraph.py` had already established that one-step likelihood is not a model-selection criterion on this data — and it is the check that caught the degeneracy.
**Next:** **Refit against the impulse response, not one-step prediction.** The fix is an output-error objective — fit (Ω, W, B) directly to the measured H, or add a multi-step prediction term — plus an explicit ρ < 1 constraint, which the pole-bank parameterisation makes enforceable (unlike the VAR fits). Until that is done: ⚠ **do not quote the injection-balance map or the W edges.** The polarity result is encouraging *because* it matches known biology, but a model that misses the measured Green's function has not earned an interpretation of its parameters, and the hub-like convergence of W's strongest edges onto one node in panel C looks like a degeneracy rather than anatomy. The 1.64 dose ratio is the one number here that is safe to reuse, since it is a property of B's per-amplitude channels rather than of the dynamics. Also untested: whether P=5 poles is the binding constraint (try a denser bank once the objective is fixed — under the current objective it would change nothing, since the fit does not use the poles it already has).

### 2026-08-10 — Model G (`freegraph.py`): with the lattice removed there is NO sparse graph — coupling is dense, long-range, and survives global-mode removal
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/freegraph.py` — free-topology VARX: same X/U/lags/split/diagonal-Σ as `gdarx_grid.py`, but the A support is chosen by a **group lasso over the K_a lags of each directed edge** instead of by `lattice_graph`. Self terms and the whole B block are left unpenalised deliberately (shrinking B would bias the fit toward local injection, which is the question being asked). Implementation notes worth keeping: with a diagonal Σ the N equations separate exactly, so this is 52 independent group lassos sharing one 520×520 Gram, solved by FISTA vectorised across equations; and **`block_grams()` accumulates 20 per-block Grams in one pass** so the train Gram, the test Gram and every stability-selection subsample are sums of blocks rather than fresh O(D²T) passes. **The result is negative and it is robust. Neither selector produces a sparse graph:** held-out log-likelihood is *monotone* in edge count and runs to **2580 of 2652 possible edges (97%)**, converging on the unconstrained VARX; eBIC (γ=0.5), which has a term that can stop, picks **1966 (74%)**. Held-out likelihood is therefore **not a topology selector on this data** — any correlated channel improves a one-step prediction whether or not it is a connection. **What the graph looks like when forced to lattice size (265 edges, chosen by neither criterion): only 36 of them are lattice edges (14%).** Across the whole path all 168 lattice edges are eventually recovered but they are 13% of the selected graph. **There IS a weak locality signal and it is at the wrong scale:** mean selected-edge length is 3.3–3.6 mm at sparse λ against a random-support null of 3.80 (z = −3.4 to −5.9), i.e. significantly shorter than chance — but lattice edges are ≤1.41 mm, so the data's own length scale is ~2.5× the imposed one. **Zero midline preference at any sparsity: 51% of selected edges cross the midline at every λ, exactly the chance rate** (26/52 nodes per side ⇒ 0.51). Marginal value of edges: 116 edges buy 19% of the autonomous→dense MSE gain, 265 → 41%, 443 → 61%, 939 → 86%. **Global-mode control run, and it does not explain any of this** (`--drop-pcs 1`): the top PC carries **69.5% of channel covariance** with a near-uniform loading (sd 0.036 across nodes vs 0.139 for uniform), i.e. a genuine global component — and projecting it out leaves every topology conclusion **unchanged** (dense 95%, cross-midline 51%, mean length 3.73–3.79 vs null 3.80). Two implementation traps fixed while building it: stability subsamples must use the **same absolute λ** as the full fit, not their own λ_max×frac, or supports are not nested and "stable" exceeds "selected" (it did, 1214 vs 1202); and the group lasso is not scale invariant, so regressors are rescaled to unit rms and targets to unit sd before penalising (A is percent dF/F, B is an impulse train that is zero 88% of the time).
**Why:** user approved dropping the topology assumption. The lattice had to be tested rather than swapped out, and the answer changes what Model H is allowed to claim.
**Next:** ⚠ **Do not report "the learned graph" from Model G as connectivity** — a 74–97% dense support with chance-level midline structure and a 3.7 mm length scale is what a shared low-rank drive looks like, and the rank-50 basis guarantees some support is unidentifiable regardless of estimator. The PC-1 control rules out *one* global mode, not the low-rank basis itself. **MSE/ell are NOT comparable between the two runs** (removing a PC changes the target), so only the topology statistics transfer. Open: whether scoring against the empirical Green's function H (multi-step, not one-step) selects a sparser graph — that is the selector this data may actually support.

**Changed/Found:** Selection is now "keep the K **least-affected** contra pixels", with K picked per session as the **smallest K whose deployed held-out R² clears `ctrl_r2_floor()`** — the most stim-blind predictor that is still usable. The dip score is untouched; only the gate changed. New/changed code: `utils/ctrl_affected_detect.m` gains `method='least_affected'` (`keep_n`/`keep_frac`, optional `max_bleed` hard guard) plus `R.rank`, `R.bleed_kept`, `R.bleed_worst`, `R.nKept`; new `utils/ctrl_gram_build.m` + `utils/ctrl_fitsub.m` (the subset-fit Gram and solver, lifted out of `ctrl_affected_gui.m`'s inline `[COMPUTE-GRAM]`/`local_fitsub_` so the GUI, the selector and Stage 2 share one solver); new `utils/ctrl_select_k.m` (coarse sweep then exhaustive search **inside the bracketing interval** — R²(K) is not guaranteed monotone, so no bisection — returning `K_star`, `R2_ceiling`, the full K→(R², bleed) curve, and `reachable=false` when no K clears). `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m` default method is now `'least_affected'` with automatic K; `ctrl_affected_gui.m`'s slider is now K, starting at K\* and marking it on the sweep; `ctrl_residual_build.m` defaults to `mode='auto'`. **Verified:** `'dip'` regression is bit-identical (`isequal(affected)` = true vs the retired formula); `ctrl_fitsub` reproduces a direct subset fit to `max|Δb| = 0` and `ΔR² = 1.1e-16`; kept sets are exactly top-K by score and **nested** as K grows; `max_bleed` guard, `keep_frac`, and unreachable-floor flagging all behave. **Two guards added against silent misreads:** a pre-2026-08-10 `ctrl_aff_thr_*.mat` holds a dip-score threshold with no `det` field, so Stage 2 now **ignores** any committed selection whose method differs from the one in force (reading 1.13 as a K, or as a threshold under the rank rule, would build a completely different pixel set from the one that number ever meant); and the GUI writes the slider value to `det.keep_n` rather than `det.thr` under the rank rule.
**Why:** Under the absolute cut the deployed R² measured how strongly a session co-suppressed rather than anything about the model (Spearman −0.819, p=0.0011), and 12 of 13 sessions were left with 2–26 predictor pixels. Ranking decouples selection from co-suppression severity: every session keeps a set chosen the same way, K is comparable across sessions, and the tradeoff becomes two reported numbers instead of a hidden one. User decision 2026-08-10: keep unaffected-pixel selection, use the least-affected pixels up to a threshold, and quantify the residual bleed rather than modelling it away (per-pixel TF de-bleeding was offered and **rejected**).
**Next:** Residual bleed is now REPORTED, not assumed zero — `bleed_kept` (median dip score of the kept set) and `leak` (how much the Global trace itself dips) go into the Stage-2 cache and must be quoted with every Local share, because a dipping Global means Local **under**-reports. Four sessions have a full-grid ceiling below the floor (0.838/0.828/0.781/0.647) and will come back `reachable=false`; that is a capacity property of those sessions, and the exclude-vs-revisit-the-floor call is deferred until Phase 3 confirms it.

### 2026-08-10 — `gdarx_graph_fig.py`: the "learned graph" is an imposed lattice, and its A is 96% self-term
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/gdarx_graph_fig.py` — 6 panels drawn from the existing `grid_gdarx_fits.npz`, no refit. Built because "what graph do we learn" has an answer the summary figure does not show: **for every GDAR/GVAR fit the topology is IMPOSED** (`make_spec`'s `a_mask` is `lattice_graph(...)`, 8-connectivity + midline bridge = **168 edges, 22 crossing the midline**) and only the edge weights are fitted; the sole fit free to learn its own support is VARX. **The substantive numbers, on ΣₖA_k: coupling is negligible next to the self term.** Mean |self| 0.948 for autonomous / GDAR / GVAR alike, while rms on-lattice coupling is **0.009 (0.9%) for autonomous AND for GDAR+B-free** — i.e. the symmetry-tied fit adds essentially nothing over no coupling at all, max |edge| 0.025 — versus **0.036 (3.8%) for GVAR+B-free**, max |edge| 0.087. So GVAR's whole advantage over GDAR is a 4× larger but still ~4%-of-diagonal coupling term. **This is the missing mechanical explanation for why free-B wins so decisively in every family:** A carries almost none of the spatial spread, so `(I − ΣA_k)⁻¹` cannot deliver the response to a non-stimulated node, and the fit has nowhere to put the observed off-site drive except B. The B-diag-vs-B-free comparison was never a fair fight given how little propagation A is allowed to express. **Second finding: the learned coupling is strongly DIRECTED and GDAR's symmetry assumption is not mildly wrong but anti-correlated** — corr(A[i,j], A[j,i]) over the 168 edges = **−0.14**, and **53.6% of edge pairs have opposite signs**, which is why tying them drives both toward zero (panel C is visibly blank on panel B's colour scale). **Third: VARX does not learn a support.** Its |ΣₖA_k| is rms **217 on-lattice vs 217 off-lattice** with matching distributions — the rank-deficient design spreads identical magnitude everywhere, confirming from a second angle that its coefficients must not be read as connectivity. Self term also blows up (mean |diag| 147 vs 0.95). **Fourth, on the ρ>1 puzzle: the instability is in the DIAGONAL, not the graph.** GVAR's per-node self term spans 0.85–1.03 with several nodes at or above 1 while all coupling is ≤0.087, so the explosive mode is a near-unit-root self-decay, not the lattice over-connecting things.
**Why:** user asked to see the graph. Drawing it makes the imposed-vs-learned distinction impossible to misread, and the panel-D comparison surfaced the A-is-almost-diagonal fact that reframes the headline free-B-beats-diag-B result.
**Next:** ⚠ **The free-B-vs-diag-B conclusion needs a fairer test before it is quoted as "the stimulus injects broadly".** With coupling pinned at ~4% of the diagonal, B-free may be winning because A is too weak to propagate anything, not because the drive is genuinely distributed — refit with a longer A lag set or a denser/unconstrained-magnitude graph and check whether the dEll gap survives. Also: the ρ>1 diagnosis now points at the near-unit-root diagonal, so the right follow-up is the 20 s detrend (a slow residual component the self-term is chasing), not the graph — test by re-fitting at a shorter detrend window and watching the diagonal. Not yet drawn: coupling weight vs inter-site distance, which would say whether the 8-connectivity radius is even the right scale.

### 2026-08-10 — The 2.63× input-locality contrast is an EXCITATORY-side effect; the inhibitory half is barely local
**Changed/Found:** No file edited — read-out of the existing `grid_gdarx_fits.npz` (VARX B) while reviewing `gdarx_summary.png`. The bottom-left "input locality" panel has an asymmetry the pooled number hides: own-site `‖B‖` runs 0.4–1.5 for site indices 0–25 and collapses onto the grey mean-other-sites trace for 26–51. `sites[:,0]` confirms the index is sorted by x, so **0–25 is x<0 = LEFT = excitatory and 26–51 is x>0 = RIGHT = inhibitory** (26 each). Splitting the on-site-vs-off-site contrast by hemisphere: **ALL own 0.432 / other 0.165 → 2.63× (the logged headline); LEFT excitatory own 0.654 / other 0.214 → 3.06×; RIGHT inhibitory own 0.211 / other 0.116 → 1.82×.** Direct drive at the stimulated node is therefore **3.1× weaker in absolute terms on the inhibitory side** (0.211 vs 0.654) and its locality contrast is nearly gone. Two readings, not yet separated: either inhibitory photostim genuinely gives a weaker and more diffuse direct injection, or the inhibitory-side dF/F is small enough that B there is mostly fitting noise — the second is the boring explanation and should be tested first. Either way the pooled 2.63× should not be quoted without the split.
**Why:** the point of the with-input extension is to decide whether the stimulus enters only at the stimulated node; a contrast present on one hemisphere and absent on the other is a different answer than a uniform 2.63×, and it falls exactly on the dual-opsin boundary that already motivates the GDAR-vs-GVAR comparison.
**Next:** Test the noise-floor explanation before treating this as biology — compare per-site peak |H| left vs right, and refit B per hemisphere to see whether the inhibitory-side own-site term survives its own held-out score. If it is real it argues against a site-local B prior on the inhibitory side specifically, and the `gdarx_grid.py` docstring caveat (which reports only the pooled 2.63×) needs the split written into it.

### 2026-08-10 — The Stage-2 R² collapse is CONTRALATERAL CO-SUPPRESSION, not a mis-tuned threshold — pure unaffected-pixel selection does not scale
**Changed/Found:** Followed up the 1/13-clears-the-floor audit by testing what actually drives it, and the first hypothesis was WRONG. (1) **Trial count is not the cause.** The dip score normalises by the SD of the *trial-averaged* pre-window, which shrinks as 1/√nTrials, so a session with more trials should flag more pixels at a fixed threshold. It does not: Spearman(nTrials, %affected) = **+0.220, p=0.47** (n=13), and Spearman(nTrials, median dip score) = **−0.206, p=0.50**. Recorded as a killed hypothesis. (2) **The real cause: the MEDIAN contra pixel dips.** Median dip score per session runs **−0.95 to −4.17** — i.e. in most sessions the typical contralateral pixel is suppressed by 1–4 pre-window SDs during the laser. That is not a detector artefact; it is the known distributed contra co-suppression (cf. the impulse-side 95% co-suppression and `stim_network_coupling.m` `[SNC]`, where it is treated as evidence that Global IS a shared-network disturbance). (3) **The deployed R² is a readout of co-suppression, not of predictor quality:** Spearman(%contra flagged affected, deployed R²) = **−0.819, p=0.0011** (n=13). The three mildest sessions (29/45/59% flagged) are exactly the three best predictors (R² 0.756/0.799/**0.865**); the three worst (97/98/100%) give R² 0.311/0.474/0.278. The one session that clears the 0.85 floor is simply the session where the contra hemisphere is least suppressed.
**Why:** This reframes the blocker. Pure unaffected-pixel selection asks for contra pixels that do not see the laser; in 10 of 13 controller sessions those pixels barely exist, so any threshold strict enough to be meaningful deletes the predictor (down to 2–26 pixels) and the R² floor becomes unreachable **by construction**. Raising or lowering `aff_dip_thr` per session cannot fix this — it only trades stim-blindness against capacity along a curve whose whole range sits below the floor. Stage 2's own header already anticipated the mechanism ("the best predictors — the homotopic midline pixels — are precisely the ones that dip and get dropped"); what is new is that at 13 sessions the tradeoff is fatal rather than merely costly.
**Next:** The alternative is already designed and unbuilt — TASKS "[DESIGN — settled 2026-07-18] use per-pixel TF de-bleeding instead": fit a per-pixel plant `h_j(t)` (laser→pixel j), then de-bleed every regressor as `z_j_clean = z_j − (h_j * u)` and KEEP the whole grid, instead of dropping pixels. Capacity is preserved because the homotopic predictors stay in. Decision needed from the user before building: de-bleeding vs KKT subspace projection vs lowering the floor. Do not tune thresholds further until that fork is settled.

**Changed/Found:** Read every `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind_*.mat` on disk (13 sessions; `AL_0039_0420_e2` has Stage 1 but no Stage 2) before running any combined statistic. **Deployed held-out R²: 1 of 13 clears `ctrl_r2_floor()` = 0.85** — only `AL_0039_0430_e3` (0.865). The rest: 0.278–0.799, and `AL_0051_0729_e2` is **−2.119**, i.e. worse than predicting the mean (a broken fit, not a weak one). Cause is the detector, not the ROIs: at the DEFAULT `aff_dip_thr = 1.33` it marks **70–99% of the contra grid as affected**, leaving 2–26 predictor pixels on most sessions (`AL_0033_0305_e2`: 431 affected / **2** kept; `AL_0033_0224_e2`: 443/10; `AL_0039_0419_e1`: 444/15). Only 2 of 13 were ever tuned (`ctrl_aff_thr_*.mat` exists for `AL_0033_0226_e2` thr 1.13 and `AL_0039_0430_e3` thr 2.56) — and the one that passes is the one tuned to a **much higher** threshold. **The ROIs are fine and are NOT the explanation**: contra/ipsi mask ratios are 0.81–1.15 (all near-balanced, so no midline is on the wrong side), sites sit at plausible coordinates, and `nG` is 408–473 everywhere. What IS suspect per session is `corr(Actual, data.dFk)`: AL_0033 is healthy (0.82–0.96) but **AL_0039 reads 0.617 / 0.617 / 0.700 and AL_0051 0.550**, all below the 0.7 warning threshold Stage 1 prints. Separately, m4 (`AL_0033_0226_e2`) now reports 332/448 affected where RESEARCH 2026-07-19 logged **23/427** — its grid was rebuilt on a redrawn ROI (427→448 px) and its cached threshold is an under-tuned 1.13, so the historical 23/427 and the current cache are not comparable numbers.
**Why:** The user asked how to run the combined statistics on the existing caches. `ctrl_ols_xsess.m` applies the floor and would have reported **n = 1 qualifying session** — but `imp_state_across_sessions.m` and `imp_reject_across_sessions.m` apply **no R² gate at all** (grepped: neither mentions `ctrl_r2_floor`), so they would silently pool all 13, including 12 whose Global fails the floor. That is precisely the failure the floor exists to prevent: everything the predictor misses is assigned to Local, so a weak Global manufactures a large Local out of prediction error, and a cross-session state-dependence slope built on it would be measuring predictor weakness varying with state.
**Next:** Do NOT quote cross-session state-dependence or rejection numbers off the current caches. Re-tune per session in `ctrl_residual_build.m` (Phase B) — target is the LOOSEST threshold clearing 0.85, which the passing session suggests is ~2.5, not 1.33. Then decide whether the low-`r_match` sessions (AL_0039 ×3, AL_0051) are admissible at all before they enter a pooled statistic. Open question to settle with the user: add the `ctrl_r2_floor` admission gate to `imp_state_across_sessions.m` and `imp_reject_across_sessions.m` so all three cross-session scripts qualify sessions identically.

**Changed/Found:** The affected/unaffected decision existed as TWO byte-copies of the same formula — `local_dip_score` in `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m` and `dip_score_` in `ctrl_affected_gui.m` — so the threshold tuned in the GUI and the rule that actually built the predictor were free to drift apart with any edit to one of them. Both are deleted and both scripts now call the new `utils/ctrl_affected_detect.m`. ### 2026-08-10 — Laser-effect map now drawn UNDER the ROI cursor (`cp_site_overlay.m`, `cp_roi_masks` `opts.draw_overlay`)
**Changed/Found:** ROIs were being drawn on a bare mean image. New `utils/cp_site_overlay.m` renders the data-derived laser effect — contours of `cp_find_stim_site`'s trial-averaged inhibition map at 35/55/80% of its depth — plus a green `+` on the detected site and a magenta `x` on `d.params.pixel`, all mapped through the session view `T` so no marker can drift off what it marks. `cp_roi_masks.m` gained `opts.draw_overlay` (a `@(ax)` handle called on the draw axes before the first click), `opts.fig_pos` and `opts.name_extra`; existing callers are unaffected (defaults `[]`). `ctrl_ols_spont.m` builds the overlay from the cached/computed `st.map` and passes it, so both interactive and batch draws get it.
**Why:** The midline the user clicks is what assigns contra (predictor) vs ipsi (target). Drawn blind, a midline on the wrong side of the laser spot silently puts the stimulated hemisphere INTO the stim-blind predictor, and nothing downstream errors — the held-out R² can even look better, because the leaked stim coupling is predictive. The spot has to be visible at click time, not verified afterwards.
**Next:** `params.pixel` sitting far from the green `+` is expected (rim-prone, RESEARCH 2026-07-19); the green `+` is the one that governs. If a session's contours and `+` disagree, the site detection is wrong and the ROI should not be drawn until that is resolved.

### 2026-08-10 — Controller state-dependence sweep split into two phases; `ctrl_roi_build_all.m` retired
**Changed/Found:** `ctrl_roi_build_all.m` (untracked, never committed) interleaved ROI drawing with affected-pixel tuning inside one loop, so a sitting alternated between mechanical clicking and detector judgement calls, and thresholds were being chosen on early sessions before later ones had been drawn at all. Deleted and replaced by two scripts. **PHASE A `controller-analysis/ctrl_roi_draw_all.m`** (`[XDRAW-CFG/AUDIT/LOOP/GATE]`): draws every eligible session's outline + midline over its own laser-effect map, runs the unattended Stage-1 spontaneous fit while that session's 500-component SVD is still in RAM, and ends with a hard gate that re-audits DISK (not its own log) and names every session still missing an ROI or a Stage-1 cache. Donor-seeded geometry (byte-identical outline+midline to another session, from `imp_xsess_build`) counts as NOT drawn. **PHASE B `controller-analysis/ctrl_residual_build.m`** (`[XRES-CFG/PRECHECK/LOOP/REPORT]`): one session at a time, GUI-tune → build → `[n]ext/[r]etry/[s]kip/[q]uit`, and it errors out unless Phase A is complete for every eligible session (`RB.require_all`, overridable). `RB.detect` passes detector opts straight through, `RB.sess` + `RB.rebuild` target a single session for re-iteration.

Drawing must be finished across ALL sessions before any detector threshold is chosen, or the threshold is being tuned against a partial view of the data. Stage 1 stays in Phase A rather than moving to B because it commits no tunable choice and its held-out R² is the number that says whether the ROI is any good — and deferring it would pay the (dominant) SVD load twice per session.

Neither script has been executed yet — this is a code-structure change only, no data was rebuilt. Six of the seven currently-built AL_0033 ROIs carry m4's seeded geometry and will be flagged SHARED, i.e. they need redrawing.

### 2026-08-10 — GDAR-with-input on the grid: the near-zero B was a GLS pathology, not a result; whole comparison table superseded
**Changed/Found:** The `gdarx_grid.py` model comparison reported **`dEll(B=0) = 0.000` and a diagonal input gain of `|B_jj| ≈ 0.0004`** — i.e. "the stimulus does nothing," which is absurd for a photostimulation experiment. It was neither a bug nor a finding but an **artefact of the GLS weight**, and the chain to it is worth recording because every step ruled out a plausible alternative. (1) The fitted impulse response for GDAR+B-diag correlated only **+0.094** with the cached empirical Green's function H, while free-B fits correlated **+0.89** — so the problem was specific to the constrained-B fits. (2) An apparent 100× amplitude mismatch turned out to be a unit convention, not a discrepancy: **`H` in `grid_cross_response_2amp.npz` is fractional dF/F** (`(F-F0)/F0`, no percent) while `X` in `gdarx_grid.py` is percent. (3) The `joint` and `alt` estimators agreed on the same ~0.0005, ruling out a method bug. (4) With `gls=False` the same spec gives `|B_jj| = 0.3924`, matching a hand-rolled per-equation `lstsq` to four decimals — so mask, selector algebra and solver are all correct and the difference is entirely the weight matrix. (5) The cause: **Σ has condition 3.2e7, and 95.5% of the stimulus-response power sits in its top-10 eigenvectors with 0.0% in the bottom-10 — yet the 1/eig GLS metric hands the bottom-10 6.1% of the weight and the top-10 only 29.3%.** The objective was mostly about directions containing no signal. (6) The structural origin is upstream and affects far more than this fit: **`cross_response.py` reconstructs ROIs as `roi_ts = V @ spat.T + mI` from `N_COMPS = 50` SVD components, so the 52 ROIs are a rank-50 image of a 50-dimensional basis** — cov(X) condition **4.1e13**, 99% of variance in **17** of 52 components, participation ratio 2.0. (7) Shrinking Σ toward `(tr Σ/N)I` was tried and **failed**: sweeping `sigma_shrink` from 1e-6 to 0.2 moved `|B_jj|` only 0.0004 → 0.119, never near the OLS 0.40. Recorded as a negative result — shrinkage caps the damage but does not fix the objective. **Fix: a diagonal Σ**, now the default (`sigma_diagonal=True` in `run()`, `--full-sigma` to reproduce the old behaviour). In-sample SSE drops ~35%, the family is monotone again, and `|B_jj|` is a stable **0.40–0.42 across every input mask**. `logdet` now follows the noise model (summed per-channel log-variance) so it stays comparable across models instead of being set by near-zero eigenvalues. **Regenerated table** (held out, 20% contiguous blocks): autonomous MSE 0.1909 / ell −27.80; GDAR+B-diag 0.1902 / −27.67 / dEll 0.147; GDAR+B-local 0.1879 / −27.30 / 0.621; GDAR+B-free 0.1839 / −26.88 / 1.216; GVAR+B-diag 0.1707 / −25.13 / 0.151; GVAR+B-free 0.1656 / −24.37 / 1.239; VARX 0.1464 / −20.89 / 1.490. **Science that now reads cleanly: the stimulus does NOT enter only at the stimulated node.** Free-B beats diagonal-B by ~8× in likelihood gain (dEll 1.24 vs 0.15) in every model family; on the one stable fit, direct injection `|B|` is 2.63× stronger at the stimulated site than elsewhere but off-site drive is far from zero (0.165 vs 0.432), and after propagation the DC-gain contrast falls to 1.46. **Non-symmetric GVAR beats symmetric GDAR everywhere** (0.166 vs 0.184), consistent with the dual-opsin sign flip making a symmetric A untenable across the midline. Ablations: 8-connectivity beats 4- everywhere, and **bridging the midline helps everywhere** (~0.002–0.005 MSE) despite the sign flip. **Three caveats found and written into the module docstring:** every graph-constrained fit is formally **unstable (ρ = 1.12–1.96)**; only the unconstrained VARX lands below 1 (0.987, itself close enough to inflate DC-gain magnitudes) — the lattice appears too restrictive and compensates with an explosive mode, so long-horizon simulation and `dc_gain` are meaningless for those fits. The **dose response is sublinear** — fitting one input channel per (site, amplitude) pair puts the 2 mW gain at ~1.4× the 1 mW gain, not the 2× that `amp_mode='weight'` assumes (negligible effect on held-out score). And the **stimulated site ranks only ~15.8 of 52 readouts by peak response**, which bears directly on whether a site-local B is even the right prior. **`validate_alignment()` added and wired into `main()`** as a standing check, because a frame-level X/U misalignment would not error, it would quietly yield a small smeared plausible B: it trigger-averages X on the true onset times and compares against the independently built H, giving **corr +0.93 (on-site trace) and +0.94 (52×52 peak map)** over 5200 onsets with none dropped. It encodes the two traps that cost real time — `build_input(fractional=True)` splits each onset across two bracketing frames so **U's nonzero frames are not onsets and their heights are not amplitudes**, and the fractional-vs-percent unit conversion. **Two real bugs fixed:** `run()` raised `StopIteration` whenever `models` omitted the autonomous baseline (now nan); and `condition_report`'s machine-eps rank tolerance called this data full rank (smallest eigenvalue 5.6e-12 sits just above `w[0]·N·eps` = 2.6e-12) — now a relative 1e-8 floor, which correctly reports **rank 50/52**, printed on every run.
**Why:** the whole point of the with-input extension is to decide whether the stimulus enters only at the stimulated node (`b_mask='diag'`, all spread carried by `(I − ΣA_k)⁻¹`) or injects broadly (`b_mask='free'`). A weight matrix that drives B to zero regardless of the data makes that question unanswerable, and it did so silently — the fits converged, the table printed, and the numbers looked merely surprising rather than broken.
**Next:** **The pre-2026-08-10 gdarx comparison numbers are superseded and must not be quoted** — they were produced under the full-Σ objective. Two follow-ups the rank deficiency raises: (a) **VARX's held-out win survives scrutiny** — scoring inside the top-17 signal subspace vs the remaining 35 near-null directions puts **84% of its advantage in the signal subspace** (MSE 0.434 vs GVAR-free 0.483), so its *predictions* are sound — but its design is rank deficient, so **its individual A coefficients are not uniquely determined and must not be read as connectivity**; if A is to be interpreted, refit in the top-17 PC basis or ridge the design. (b) The universal ρ > 1 on graph-constrained fits deserves its own look — either the lattice is the wrong graph for widefield ROIs, or the 20 s detrend is leaving a slow component the AR part is chasing. Not yet done: a stability-constrained fit, and the `input_gain` vs `dc_gain` comparison on a fit that is actually stable enough for the DC gain to mean something.

### 2026-08-10 — TF block reframed from SAMENESS to ROBUSTNESS; new 4-panel τ/variability set (TF-A…TF-D)
**Changed/Found:** User (2026-08-10): *"each session needs its own controller anyway and results show robustness so it works"* — this is a **reframe of the LTI claim and it is the stronger version**, so it is recorded as a decision rather than a styling choice. The weak claim ("the plant is the same in every session") is a hostage to fortune: τ will move between animals/expression/windows/days, and the moment it does a referee has a hole. The strong claim matches how the rig is actually operated — **per-session gain tuning is already the documented method (`fig:cost_landscape`), so between-session plant variation is an expected operating condition, not a threat. What must hold is (a) each session's plant is low-order LTI over its OWN drive range, and (b) the plant family is tight enough that a design transfers.** New **`utils/imp_tf_robust_fig.m`** cuts the four panels that argument needs: **TF-A** τ_slow per session + trial-bootstrap CI over the cross-session mean±SD band; **TF-B** between-session SD vs mean within-session SD with the ratio annotated (the number that separates real inter-experiment variability from fit noise); **TF-C** τ from per-amplitude refits — **the load-bearing panel**, because a τ that slopes with amplitude *inside* a session genuinely breaks the design (a controller cannot be robust to its own plant moving with the command it sends), whereas between-session drift is absorbed by re-tuning; **TF-D** cross-session **model-swap R² matrix** (session i's fitted model against session j's measured h(t)) at **free gain** — free gain is the correct question, not a concession, because gain is re-tuned per session by construction, so the matrix asks whether the *dynamics* transfer. Diagonal ≈ off-diagonal ⇒ designs transfer. **Both outcomes are publishable and the console verdicts are worded to pick the sentence:** ratio≈1 + high swap R² → "one plant, robust design"; ratio≫1 + high swap R² → "the plant varies, per-session tuning handles it, here is the range", which is a *better* Methods story and directly motivates the auto-tuner. Only a low swap R² is a problem, and then Methods must state that per-session identification is required. **Bug caught before it bit:** `imp_tf_paper_fig` and `imp_tf_robust_fig` both wrote `tf_tau_forest.pdf` and would have silently overwritten each other — the forest now belongs to the robust block alone and `imp_tf_paper_fig` is the shape panel (2C-i) only. Also removed a dead `plot(... randn(n,1)*0 ...)` axis-stabiliser left in TF-B. `imp_tf_run.m` calls both; PAPER.md gains the five panel rows and the framing block. All files Code Analyzer clean.
**Why:** the figure previously tried to prove sameness, which is both harder and less true than what the experiment actually needs. Robustness is the claim the data can carry and the one the control-theory framing wants.
**Next:** **NOT RUN.** ⚠ **Layout is unresolved and blocks assembly:** Fig 2 row 1 already overflows (18.1/17) and five new panels do not fit the three-row plan — TF-A…TF-D as their own row is 4+4+5+4.5+3×0.3 = **18.4, still over**; either drop TF-C to 4 cm (→17.4 ✓), move TF-D to supplementary, or put the whole block in supplementary with only 2C-i in the main figure. Decide before assembly. Also: TF-D's free-gain choice means the panel says nothing about **gain** spread — if a referee asks whether the actuator gain is stable across sessions, that is `gRatio`/`dcgain` and currently sits only in the `imp_tf_xsess` workbench; consider a fifth panel or a supplementary row if it is challenged.

### 2026-08-10 — `imp_tf_run.m`: one-command TF driver + a 2-panel paper figure replacing the 6-panel [TFX] dashboard
**Changed/Found:** User (2026-08-10): the `[TFX]` figure from `imp_tf_xsess.m` is "too confusing" and they had lost track of what the figure is even for. Both complaints have the same cause and it is worth stating plainly: **`imp_tf_xsess`'s 6-panel output is a WORKBENCH, not a panel.** It shows h(t) overlay, τ per session, gFree-vs-amplitude with the LTI line, gRatio, ρ and full-vs-LOAO simultaneously — six questions at once — because it was built to decide whether the fit is trustworthy. A paper panel makes ONE claim. New **`utils/imp_tf_paper_fig.m`** cuts the two panels that carry the actual argument: **2C-i** peak-normalised h(t), measured SOLID vs fitted DASHED, one line per session on the session gradient (6×4 cm) → *same shape everywhere, and a low-order linear model reproduces it*; **2C-ii** τ forest, per-session slowest τ with its bootstrap CI over a cross-session mean ± SD band (4×4 cm) → *same number, within uncertainty*. Peak-normalisation in 2C-i is deliberate — it removes the gain difference so the panel is about SHAPE only; size is a separate claim living in 2B and gRatio. The fit is normalised on the MEASURED trace and the same scale applied to the fit, so the fit is still judged against the data rather than rescaled to match. Legend labels the ENCODING (measured / LTI fit), not the sessions — session identity is the gradient and belongs in the caption, not in n legend rows. New **`impulse-analysis/imp_tf_run.m`** is the one-command driver: appends AL_0048 (inhibitory site, via `load_bilateral_impulse.m`, since `loadData` cannot open a Signals experiment), fits every session full-range, computes the **common amplitude window and refits everything there as PRIMARY** (h(t) is amp²-weighted and the sessions do not span the same drive range, so an unrestricted cross-session τ comparison is confounded by drive range), emits the two panels, and prints a summary in the words the caption needs — per-session order/τ/CI/R²pool/LOAO, between-session SD vs mean within-session bootstrap SD **and their ratio with a plain-language verdict** (<1.5 = one shared time constant; >3 = report τ as a range, not a value). Supporting change: `utils/imp_tf_fit_session.m` now returns **`T.h_meas`** (the empirical amp²-weighted normalised response it actually fitted) so a figure can plot measured-vs-fit without refitting. Three MATLAB gotchas handled: script local functions must sit at EOF; `warning()` rejects a bare `ME.message` without an identifier (used `fprintf(2,...)`); two stale `%#ok<LAXES>` suppressions removed. All files Code Analyzer clean.
**Why:** the LTI premise is what licenses the PI controller, the gain-grid methods figure, and the impulse-τ ↔ step-τ equivalence — and it is currently demonstrated on ONE session, which is an example, not a claim about the preparation. The figure exists to turn it into a claim. That purpose was buried under the diagnostics.
**Next:** **NOT RUN** — user runs `load_experiments` → `imp_tf_run`. The driver prints the caption obligations rather than leaving them to memory: **AL_0041 e1/e2 are the SAME animal**, so between-session spread mixes within- and between-animal variability; and **AL_0048 is inhibitory-side only with its readout ~2.6 mm from the illuminated spot**, i.e. a CONNECTED region, which must be flagged if this panel backs an actuator-TF claim. `imp_tf_xsess.m` is deliberately KEPT as the diagnostic workbench — if the between/within ratio comes back >3, its gRatio and per-amplitude-pole panels are where the explanation will be, and they should go to supplementary rather than into 2C.

### 2026-08-10 — `r_lean` registry-only mode in `load_sessions.m` (unblocks every cross-session batch)
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/load_sessions.m` gains `r_lean`. Set `r_lean = 1; load_sessions;` and it builds `mouse`/`fields` (mn/td/en/trials/newbuild + `pathCtrl` + `hasCache`) and loads **no `d`/`data` at all**, then returns before the variance-aggregation block. Default behaviour is untouched (`r_lean` unset ⇒ 0 ⇒ full load). **Why it was needed:** each controller cache is 1–3.5 GB because `d` carries the full 2000-component SVD, so the 15-session load is ~40 GB and OOMs at m13 (RESEARCH 2026-07-30) — yet `ctrl_roi_build_all.m`, `imp_reject_across_sessions.m` and `ctrl_ols_xsess.m` **all already lazy-load each session and free it again** (`ctrl_roi_build_all` L161–168 loads, L268 `rmfield`s), so what they actually need is the registry, not the data. Until now the only way to run them was the ad-hoc hand-edited stand-in copy of `load_sessions.m` used on 2026-08-02 — i.e. a second registry that can drift from the real one. **Two traps found while wiring it:** (1) the script opened with **`clear all`, which wiped the caller's `r_lean` before the flag was ever read** and would have made it a silent no-op — changed to `clearvars -except r_lean` (still a clean workspace, just no longer flushing cached *functions*; the targeted `clear <fn>; rehash` remains the right tool for the GUI-holds-a-stale-.m case, per [[reference_matlab_function_cache]]); (2) the post-loop aggregation dereferences `mouse.<f>.data.nc` unconditionally, so lean mode needed an explicit `return` guard rather than just skipping the load. Code Analyzer clean (only the pre-existing preallocation infos in the aggregation block remain).
**Why:** the per-session-ROI rebuild is the current blocker on every Fig-4 number, and it could not even be started without a way to get `mouse`/`fields` into the workspace on this machine.
**Next:** **NOT RUN** — user runs it. Order: `r_lean = 1; load_sessions` → `ctrl_roi_build_all` (`XR.redraw='all'`, `XR.tune=true`) → `ctrl_ols_xsess` → `imp_reject_across_sessions` → `imp_state_across_sessions`. If any batch script turns out to touch an aggregation array this guard skips, it should be fixed to lazy-load rather than by widening the guard.

### 2026-08-10 — ENERGY RATIO implemented (Nick 2026-07-28); `internal_model_principle`'s inline metric copy retired
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/imp_reject_core.m` now returns **ER = ‖A−ref‖²/‖G−ref‖²** alongside the legacy ρ, and `internal_model_principle.m` + `imp_reject_across_sessions.m` both report it. **The substantive finding is in the denominator.** Nick asked for `‖y_actual‖²/‖y_disturbance‖²` with **1 = no work done, <1 = controller gain** — and that property only holds if the disturbance is referenced to `ref` as well. The legacy ρ divides by **‖G‖, i.e. G referenced to ZERO**, so a do-nothing controller returns `‖G−ref‖/‖G‖`, a quantity that depends on how far the brain's natural level happens to sit from the target and therefore drifts with session, mouse and state. **That is why the published levels look the way they do (OL 1.306, CL 0.879): the LEVEL of ρ was never interpretable, only the OL-vs-CL contrast was.** With ER, `A ≡ G ⇒ ER ≡ 1` identically, so "the controller did work" becomes readable off a single condition instead of requiring the paired comparison — ER is the squared sensitivity |S|² in energy terms. ER is computed on all three windows with the **0–3 s stim window as primary** (Nick said stim window; ER is well-posed there because numerator and denominator share the reference, unlike ρ which needed the settled 1–3 s window to be meaningful). Reported per Nick's spec: **median ± IQR separately per condition**, quartiles, fraction of trials with ER<1, one-sample signrank of each condition against 1, and in the cross-session batch a **session-level paired Wilcoxon signed-rank** plus a bootstrap CI on the per-session gain. ρ is retained verbatim so every pre-2026-08-10 number stays reproducible; both printouts carry an explicit "NOT interchangeable, quote one or the other" warning. **Separate bug fixed in passing:** `imp_reject_core`'s header claimed to be the single source of truth for both streams, but `internal_model_principle.m` carried an **inline copy** of the `rejW`/`poolW` lambdas and never called it (§[IMP-REJECT] L462–463) — the two streams could silently drift. It now calls the core. All three files Code Analyzer clean. One MATLAB gotcha avoided: the first draft put a `ternER` local function mid-script, which is a parse error — script local functions must sit at EOF — replaced with a 2-element cell indexed by `logical+1`.
**Why:** user (2026-08-10) said "do it" on the metric conversion. It also unblocks the Methods paragraph, which is 🔴 and explicitly gated on the new units.
**Next:** **NOT RUN.** Re-run `internal_model_principle.m` on m4 and `imp_reject_across_sessions.m` on the batch **after** the per-session ROI rebuild, not before — the 7/7 ρ result rests on six sessions carrying m4's seeded ROI, so recomputing ER on the seeded caches would just produce a second number needing the same retraction. ⚠ **Predict, then check:** ER should place OL nearer 1 than ρ did (ρ put OL *above* 1, which under ER's reading would mean open loop actively amplifies the disturbance — an artefact of the zero-referenced denominator, not a finding). If OL still lands well above 1 under ER, that is a real result about the laser's own transient and needs its own explanation.

### 2026-08-05 — GEOMETRY FIXED: one resolved display view per session (cp_orient), used by every render and every click
**Changed/Found:** The controller stack drew brains in **two different frames**: `cp_roi_masks` hardcoded `imagesc(mimg.')` (transposed, midline horizontal) and stored clicks in that frame, while `ctrl_ols_spont.m`'s VAL kernel map, `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m`'s affected map and `ctrl_affected_gui.m` all drew NATIVE. You clicked in one frame and verified in another, with nothing enforcing agreement — and `impulse-analysis/CLAUDE.md` ("correct view is TRANSPOSED") directly contradicts `ctrl_ols_spont.m`'s "midline vertical in native" for the same mouse and the same `mimg`. New **`utils/cp_orient.m`** + **`cp_orient_img/_fwd/_inv.m`** establish one contract: geometry stays NATIVE (row,col), data is never rotated, and a single per-session transform is applied only at render time. Of the 8 dihedral views the three degrees of freedom are settled separately, and **two of them by the data**: (1) TRANSPOSE — objective, by best vertical **mirror-symmetry correlation** of the mean image (the same test that settled the AL_0048 bregma question, 0.821 vs 0.170; the printout IS the probe, and it flags when the two scores are within 0.05 and therefore not decisive); (2) LEFT/RIGHT — objective, flip so the site's hemisphere (ipsi/target) lands on the right, matching the existing figure convention; (3) UP/DOWN — **explicitly NOT inferable** (mirror symmetry is blind to a vertical flip, and controller sessions carry no bregma registration), so it costs one keystroke in a preview figure, once, when the ROI is drawn, and is cached to `data/cp_orient_ctrl_<tag>.mat`. Rewired: `cp_roi_masks` takes `opts.T` and draws in that view, converting clicks back to native before storage; `ctrl_ols_spont.m` resolves the view (confirm prompt only when redrawing), passes it to the draw, saves it as `OLS.Torient`, and renders its kernel map — image, hemisphere tints, midline, grid, site, homotopic mirror — entirely through it; `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m`'s affected map and `ctrl_affected_gui.m`'s deflection map, contra outline, target box, site, grid AND click-inverse all go through the same object. **Storage format is unchanged and old ROI files stay valid**: this function's internal frame already had x = native row and y = native col, so `(bx,by)` always meant native (row,col) — the transpose was only how those two numbers were being *plotted*. Callers that pass no `T` (impulse side, `contra_prediction.m`) keep the legacy behaviour exactly. All Code Analyzer clean. **NOT RUN.**
**Why:** display-only, so no fitted number moves — except through the one path that matters: a mis-oriented drawing surface makes a human draw a wrong outline, and the outline defines which pixels count as contra, which is the predictor set for the entire decomposition.
**Next:** The first session run will print both symmetry scores and so **settle the impulse-doc vs controller-comment contradiction** — whichever loses needs its doc corrected, and if the margin is under 0.05 the test is not decisive and the view must be judged by eye. `ols_tf_pipeline.m` keeps its own `pick_orient`/`resolve_orient`/`Torient` (with the `ant_rc` anterior-up tiebreaker added 2026-08-02): deliberately NOT touched here, because that file is being edited in a parallel impulse session — consolidating the two into `cp_orient` is a follow-up, and until then AL_0033 could in principle be drawn in one view and analysed in another across the two streams. Also: the 7 existing ROIs were drawn in the legacy transposed view and Stage-1 caches without `Torient` fall back to native rendering, so they are self-consistent but not in the resolved view until redrawn via `ctrl_roi_build_all.m`.

**Changed/Found:** User (2026-08-05): before fitting they want to *see* the ipsi trial responses, tune the affected-pixel sensitivity, and have every model (pixel set) clear a spontaneous-R² floor. Implemented: **`utils/ctrl_r2_floor.m`** (single source of truth, 0.85, carrying the reasoning and the 0.90→0.85 history in its help). **`ctrl_affected_gui.m`** extended into the pre-fit workbench — (1) third panel: **ipsi trial browser** (all trials faint, mean ±SEM, single-trial highlight via slider, OL/CL/both, `ref` and stim window marked) built from canonical `data.dFk`, so an unusable session is seen *before* a predictor is fitted; (2) **`[COMPUTE-GRAM]`**: since every candidate is a SUBSET of one grid and the z-scoring is per-pixel, the normal equations for any subset are submatrices of one Gram matrix — precomputed once, so each fit is O(nU³) instead of a pass over 60k frames, and is algebraically identical to Stage 2 (same z-score, same `1e-6*mean(column energy)` ridge, same train/test frames); (3) **"R² vs threshold" sweep** — 14 thresholds, printing and plotting held-out R², unaffected-px count and Local% together, with the floor and the full-grid ceiling drawn on; (4) **the gate itself**: Build refuses to write `ctrl_aff_thr_<tag>.mat` below the floor (status text turns red and says to loosen the cut) unless a "save below floor" checkbox is ticked, which stamps `forced_below_floor` into the cache; (5) `loadUVt` → **`cp_loadUVt`**, which unblocks m6/m7/m8/m11/m12 — the GUI could not open on those five at all; (6) a `BATCH_selField` hook. Gate plumbed downstream: `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m` prints PASS/FAIL and saves `gate_pass`/`r2_floor`; `ctrl_roi_build_all.m` gains `XR.tune` (opens the GUI between Stage 1 and Stage 2 so the threshold is tuned before the predictor is committed), reports ceiling *and* deployed R² separately, and gives a failing session its own status `lowR2` instead of `built`; `ctrl_ols_xsess.m` excludes below-floor sessions from every combined statistic and lists them. All Code Analyzer clean. **NOT RUN.**
**Why:** the gate is the structural answer to the T1 objection: `Local = Actual − Global` hands *everything the predictor misses* to Local, so a weak Global manufactures a large Local out of prediction error alone. A floor makes that failure mode impossible to reach silently.
**Next:** ⚠ **The gate and the headline pull in opposite directions and must be reported as a pair.** Every threshold that keeps more pixels raises R² *and* gives Global more capacity to explain the ipsi response, which shrinks Local — that is exactly what the new sweep plot shows on one pair of axes, and it is the tradeoff being made whenever a threshold is chosen. Never quote a Local share without the deployed R² beside it. Also: the floor is on the DEPLOYED model, not the ceiling; m4's deployed R² was 0.68 at `aff_dip_thr=1.33` and 0.855 at the looser 2026-07-19 cut, so **the existing 7 sessions were built at thresholds that may not clear 0.85 — expect some to come back `lowR2` and need retuning.** Check whether the admissible threshold window is even non-empty on the weak-predictor sessions (m6 kept only 2 unaffected px).

Everything downstream (Fig 6 TRIALPRED, §17c/§17c2 STATEDEP, `ALLSESS`) therefore ran on the prior-free model, which is exactly the configuration that lost the residual capture — the sweep could not have changed anything it reported on. **FIX:** compute + pick moved to a new **§17c0**, placed before §17e/§17d; §17f reduced to a stub that draws from the stored `RIDGESWEEP` via a new `ridge_sweep_figure` local function (pure drawing, so re-plotting never re-fits). Added `ridge_pick='auto'` + `ridge_r2min=0.92` (user's stated acceptable held-out spontaneous R²): the pick takes the grid point with the LOWEST leak among those clearing the R² floor, then writes `select_ridge`, `lamSel` **and** `sellamR` so the §10T3 "Refit SELECT model" button stays consistent with the batch. If no grid point clears the floor it warns, falls back to the best-R² point, and says not to read the leak. Code Analyzer: new warnings are all the file's existing constant-folding class (literal `ridge_pick='auto'` making the `off` branch look unreachable).

Answer was: none, and the prior-free dense fit — the sweep was diagnostic-only by accident of placement. Then re-read Fig 5 panel 1: the SHAPE still decides whether this is a real operating point (knee = separable) or a diagonal (every point of leak costs proportional R², i.e. an identifiability limit, cf. `[CP-KRECON]`). ### 2026-08-05 — Add §17f [RIDGE-SWEEP]: the spont-R² vs leak trade-off curve for the far-from-ipsi prior
**Changed/Found:** New §17f in `ols_tf_pipeline.m`. Sweeps `select_ridge` over `[0 1e-4 … 3]` (fractions of `mean(diag(Gz))`), refitting the dense weighted-L2 SELECT model per amp from the §17a operators only — no upstream refit, so it runs in seconds. Per grid point: held-out **spontaneous** R² (on the §6 test split, the only data R² is scored on here), leak = Global dip as % of Actual, and — as an independent check that the prior is doing what it claims — the `|w|`-weighted mean distance of the fitted weights from the ipsi site. Three panels: the R²-vs-leak trade-off itself (points annotated with their ridge value, a star on the current setting), both objectives against the knob, and the weight-distance diagnostic. Prints a stderr block if NO grid point gets leak under 50%, naming that as an identifiability result rather than a tuning failure. Returns `RIDGESWEEP`.
**Why:** Greedy pruning did not recover the capture lost when SELECT was de-sparsified, which is consistent with the user's own 2026-07-06 diagnosis (WIP header): network-correlated "clean" pixels reconstruct the dip, so dropping a pixel just lets the refit reallocate its weight onto correlated neighbours — the stim-predictive signal is a distributed DIRECTION, not a set of identifiable pixels, matching `[CP-KRECON]`. The remaining honest lever is the far-from-ipsi prior, which is a statement about where bleed and direct effects live, formed WITHOUT reference to the dip — so unlike a KKT equality or an evoked-subspace projection it does not make capture true by construction, and leak stays a measurement. A sweep beats guessing a value: the operating point should be chosen off the curve.
**Next:** UNRUN. Read panel 1 first — the SHAPE of the curve is the finding. A knee (leak falls sharply while R² barely moves) means the two directions are separable and there is a defensible operating point. A straight diagonal means every point of leak costs proportional R², i.e. they are NOT separable and no setting is principled — in which case the honest write-up is the identifiability limit, not a tuned number. Reference: `[CP-CLEANRES]` (S13, RRR lineage) held the residual at ~73% of the actual dip, so ~30% leak is the regime to aim at. Cross-check panel 3: if weight distance does NOT rise with ridge, the prior is not biting and the sweep is measuring something else. Do not adopt a value until the §17e greedy status is also known — if greedy reported anything other than CONVERGED it never applied, and the "greedy didn't work" observation is about dense SELECT, not about greedy.

### 2026-08-05 — Add §17e [GREEDY-BLIND]: pooled pixel-pruning layer restoring residual capture without a KKT constraint
**Changed/Found:** New `utils/imp_greedy_blind.m` + new §17e in `ols_tf_pipeline.m`, sitting BETWEEN the detector and the fit (`detector → U → greedy prune → dense weighted-ridge fit on survivors`); `select_l1frac` stays 0, so pruning does the blinding and the fit keeps maximising spontaneous R². **POOLED** (user's choice): candidates = the INTERSECTION of the per-amp unaffected sets, so ONE predictor set serves every amplitude and per-amp leak stays comparable. Weights are NEVER constrained — each step refits the unconstrained weighted-ridge spont fit on the survivors, so this is structurally unlike the retired §17b KKT (which imposes one linear equality on a ~400-dim vector, always succeeds, and therefore reports ~100% capture regardless of the data). **Drop rule** = leak-contribution ÷ R²-cost, where the cost of removing pixel *i* is the leave-one-covariate-out quantity `b_i²/[M⁻¹]_ii` (one inverse per step; RFE-style batch of 1% of the live set keeps the search fast). **Two stopping conditions:** mean |leak| ≤ `greedy_tolL`=0.10 → CONVERGED; held-out spont R² < `greedy_r2floor`=0.90 × full-set R² → **FAILED_R2**, and on any failure §17d falls back to the full detector set with a warning rather than silently receiving a half-pruned set. **Both controls built in, not optional:** (a) RANDOM-EXCLUSION — same drop count chosen at random, and the function prints a stderr warning if greedy fails to beat it, which is precisely the `[CP-STIMAFF]` S14 outcome in the RRR lineage; (b) TRIAL-SPLIT — selection uses `evDip` from a seeded half of the trials (`evZcA`/`aAcA`, built in §17a where the per-trial block already exists, so no second SVD reconstruction) and the reported leak is recomputed on the held-out half (`leakVal`), with a stderr warning if blindness fails to transfer. `R.leakSel` is labelled in-sample and must not be quoted. Code Analyzer: helper clean; script keeps its pre-existing warning set.
**Why:** De-sparsifying SELECT cost the residual most of the stim effect, because the L1 + distance prior had been doing double duty as the stim-rejection layer. User asked for a dedicated layer instead, and correctly pushed back that GREEDY is not structurally circular the way KKT is — it only chooses a subset, and it can fail. The corollary is that its CAPTURE is still not the informative statistic (the stopping rule guarantees it on convergence); the informative numbers are the R² price of blindness and whether that price beats random exclusion, which is why both controls are compiled in rather than left as follow-ups.
**Next:** UNRUN. Read the output in this order: (1) status — FAILED_R2 is a RESULT, meaning the stim-predictive and spont-predictive directions are not separable at that floor, consistent with `[CP-KRECON]`'s distributed-coupling finding; (2) greedy-vs-random — if greedy does not beat random the residual is NOT validated no matter how good capture looks; (3) held-out `leakVal`, never `leakSel`. Only then look at capture. If it converges, check where the dropped pixels sit — near ipsi, or overlapping the `bledA` bleed map would be independent evidence the layer found something real. `greedy_tolL`/`greedy_r2floor` are first guesses. §18's engine still runs the unpruned dense fit — repoint only after §17e is shown to work on the primary session.

### 2026-08-05 — SELECT de-sparsified: `select_l1frac = 0` (dense fit, maximise spontaneous R²) + `select_ridge` knob
**Changed/Found:** `ols_tf_pipeline.m` — `select_l1frac` 0.15 → **0**, so §17d SELECT keeps EVERY stim-unaffected predictor instead of a sparse subset. `select_wlasso` gained a closed-form branch for `l1frac<=0` (`a = (Gs + lamR·I)\cs`) rather than driving `cd_lasso` to the same answer with a zero penalty. **Key coupling, surfaced rather than left implicit:** the far-from-ipsi prior was carried ENTIRELY by the per-column L1 weights `1/gamma_i`, so removing L1 removes the distance prior too. Under the rescaling `b_i = gamma_i a_i` a ridge `lamR‖a‖²` equals `lamR·Σ(b_i/gamma_i)²` — i.e. the SAME distance prior re-expressed as a weighted L2 — so the fix is a real ridge, not a new penalty: new knob `select_ridge` (fraction of `mean(diag(Gz))`, default 0) wired through all three call sites via a dedicated `lamSel`, kept separate from `lamR` so raising it cannot perturb the other fits. Sites: §17d, the §10T3 "Refit SELECT model" button (`sellamR`), and §18's `local_stimblind_session` (reads `cfg.select_ridge`, with a fallback so an older `cfg` still runs). Dead `lamR` removed from §18's engine. Code Analyzer: pre-existing warning set.
**Why:** User: no sparse constraint on this model — the focus is R² for residual prediction, and R² is measured on spontaneous data only. Correct on the second point: held-out R² here is scored on interstim spontaneous frames; the stim windows are judged by leak/capture, never by R². Sparsity was costing predictive accuracy on exactly the data R² is computed from.
**Next:** UNRUN. **Watch leak, not just R².** With `select_l1frac=0` AND `select_ridge=0` there is no distance prior at all — near-ipsi unaffected pixels can now take weight, and those are the ones most able to absorb stim signal, so the expected direction is higher spontaneous R² AND higher LEAK / smaller Local. That trade is the whole reason the prior existed. If leak jumps materially, raise `select_ridge` (a weighted L2 tightens the prior without zeroing weights) rather than restoring L1. Compare the §17d printout's `predR2 pre/post` and `dipGlob` against the pre-change run before adopting. Numbers are NOT comparable to any sparse-SELECT result, including the bilateral Python port (`impulse_ols.py`, `l1frac=0.15`), which still runs the sparse version.

### 2026-08-05 — Recovery test moved from the FIT to the DATA: g406 @ 2.7 V was rejected with its trace visibly recovered
**Changed/Found:** User checked pixel activity for **g406 @ 2.7 V (AL_0041 e2)** and found it misclassified: inspector read `trough 143 ms (band [69 286]) | recovery 0.57 (max 0.30) | full trough −0.74 @ 143 ms -> not (recovery ... dip does not come back)`, while the evoked trace has plainly returned. Diagnosis: the trough test PASSED (143 ms inside the band, and later than ipsi's ~114.5 ms as expected for a downstream pixel), so the failure was `RECfrac` alone — and `RECfrac` was measured on the **fitted** response at a **single instant** (`capN` = the ipsi recovery time). Both choices were wrong: (a) the fixed-order TF is known to lag the sharp real dip (TASKS #183), so a fit still 57% down at the window edge says nothing about whether the RECORDING recovered; (b) requiring a contra pixel to be back exactly when ipsi is back contradicts the asymmetry the trough band already encodes — contra is driven THROUGH the network and may legitimately recover later. (b) was my own error from the previous revision. **FIX:** shape is now judged on the **trial-averaged evoked**, using the SAME recovery definition ipsi uses (§10 ~line 383: first return after the trough to within `max(2·baselineSD, recTolFac·|trough|)`). New per-pixel data landmarks `TRdatMs`/`RECdatMs`/`DIPdat`/`hasRec` computed from the existing `muMap` — **no refit, and independent of the TF cache**. Gate is now `g_tr` on `TRdatMs` and `g_rec = hasRec & RECdatMs <= tf_recMaxFac·recMs(ai)` with new knob `tf_recMaxFac = 2.0`; recovery is searched over the WHOLE fit window, not up to `capN`. `tf_recFracMax` demoted to diagnostic. Batch now prints how many px-amp the retired fitted-recovery rule would have rejected that the data rule accepts — that count is a direct measure of the #183 sluggish-fit problem. Inspector recomputes the data landmarks per click, reports fit trough + recFrac alongside as diagnostics, and distinguishes "never returns within the fit window" from "returns too late". All three rule sites (gate/slider/inspector) updated together; `tf_sensKey` gained `recMaxFac`/`recMs`/`recTolFac`. Code Analyzer: back to the pre-existing warning set.
**Why:** The detector answers a question about the recording, so it must measure the recording. Using the fit as the shape source made the detector inherit every deficiency of the fixed-order model, and the project already knows that model is sluggish. Measuring on the evoked also unifies the definition — ipsi's own landmarks were always computed on its trial-averaged evoked, never on a fit.
**Next:** UNRUN. Re-open the selector on AL_0041 e2 and re-check g406 @ 2.7 V — it should now pass on a DATA recovery well inside `2.0 × ipsi recovery`. Then watch the new `[fit-vs-data]` count: if it is LARGE, the sluggish-fit problem is widespread and TASKS #183 P1 (score the fit on the dip window rather than the full 0–1000 ms) should be done before the TF fits are used for anything quantitative — the detector no longer depends on them, but §10T's order-lock and every TF claim still do. `tf_recMaxFac=2.0` is a first guess; if genuinely-affected pixels still miss, raise it or drop the upper bound entirely and require only that a recovery EXISTS. Selections invalidated again (key changed).

### 2026-08-05 — Gate window LEARNED from the ipsi inhibition lobe (per amp, per session); fixed 400 ms demoted to fallback
**Changed/Found:** `ols_tf_pipeline.m` — the shape gate's window is no longer the hard-coded `tf_dipCapSec=0.4`. Per amp it is now `capNa(ai) = numel(inhCols{ai})` = onset → **ipsi recovery**, and the trough band is `trBandA(ai,:) = troughMs(ai) * tf_troughFac` with `tf_troughFac=[0.6 2.5]` — both from the §10 landmarks already computed per amp per session. New knobs `tf_capFromIpsi` (true) / `tf_troughFac`; `tf_dipCapSec` + `tf_troughMs` survive only as the fallback when an amp has no usable recovery landmark, and that fallback now **warns** naming the amps instead of reverting silently. `DIPgate`/`TRcapMs`/`RECfrac` are built in a per-amp loop (windows differ per amp, so the old vectorised `min` over a common `capN` no longer applies). Batch prints the learned window and trough band per amp. All three rule sites updated in lockstep — gate (`trBandA(:,1).'` implicit expansion), slider (`DB.trBandA(ai,:)`), inspector (`DB.capNa(ai)`, and its title now shows the lobe length and flags ` FALLBACK`). `tf_sensKey` gained `trBandA`/`capNa`/`capFromIpsi`/`troughFac`, so a landmark change invalidates saved selections. Code Analyzer: unchanged warning set.
**Why:** User: the 400 ms window should be learned from the ipsi window. The right landmark is recovery rather than a scaled trough because `rebCols{ai}` starts at `rc+1` — capping at recovery makes the gate window EXACTLY the ipsi inhibition lobe and disjoint from the rebound lobe **by construction**, which is the property `dip_win_s=0.300` was hand-tuned to approximate. It also removes a genuine inconsistency: `dip_win_s` documents itself as the single source of truth for the dip window while `tf_dipCapSec` was a second, hard-coded one used only by the detector. The trough band is asymmetric because a contra pixel driven through the network should trough with ipsi or LATER, never earlier — a symmetric band spends its lower half on physically implausible latencies, and session-adaptivity matters for AL_0048 (readout 2.6 mm off the illumination, no reason to share AL_0033's latency).
**Next:** UNRUN. **Known consequence, do not read past it:** the gate window now grows with amplitude (the dip genuinely lasts longer), so per-amp affected COUNTS are no longer the same test across amps — anything comparing them, notably the dose-graded bleed SLOPE test, must account for that. Saved selections are invalidated again by the key change; every session needs a fresh CONFIRM. Watch the printed per-amp lobe lengths against the §15 landmarks (trough 114–143 ms, median recovery ~314 ms) — a lobe much longer than ~350 ms means that amp's ipsi recovery was late or the landmark is wrong, and the fallback warning should be checked for. AL_0048's learned window describes a connected region's dynamics, not stimulated tissue.

### 2026-08-05 — BUG: the TF affected-detector gates on DEPTH only, so monotone RAMPS score as the most affected pixels
**Changed/Found:** User spotted it on **g241 @ 3.7 V, AL_0041 2025-12-02 e2**: a good TF fit whose response just keeps descending was classified affected, when the target shape is dip → return. Verified in code (not by refitting that pixel): `DIPgate = min(YItf(:,1:capN,:))` is a pure DEPTH statistic over [0, `tf_dipCapSec`] and the gate is `DIPgate<0 & -DIPgate>preThr/tf_sens`. A monotonically descending fit attains its minimum at the LAST sample of the cap window, so it not only passes but scores **deeper** than a genuine dip-and-recover with the same early slope ⇒ ramps were *preferentially* selected. Three separable defects: (1) no shape/recovery test in the default path at all; (2) `tf_reqReb` (the only shape criterion) defaults FALSE, and would not have helped anyway; (3) `reboundRatio` is computed by `proto_chars` over the full fit window `nT` while the gate uses `capN` — different windows — and it measures *turnaround*, not return-to-baseline (dip −5 recovering only to −4.5 scores 0.1 and passes a 0.05 floor). **FIX:** new shape gate, both tests on the SAME `capN` window — `TRcapMs` (trough must fall inside `tf_troughMs=[60 250]` ms; a ramp's trough is pinned to the 400 ms window edge and fails on this alone) and `RECfrac = y(capN)/dip` (≤ `tf_recFracMax=0.30`; ~1 for a ramp, ~0 recovered, <0 overshoot). Applied identically in all THREE places the rule lives: the batch gate, the live slider `tfmap_sens`, and the click inspector `tfmap_click` (which now names which shape test failed and prints trough/recovery in its title). Gate params added to the `tf_sens` cache key so selections confirmed under the old depth-only rule self-invalidate. Batch printout now reports per-test pass counts plus how many px-amp the shape gate rejected that the old rule accepted. Code Analyzer: two new benign "preallocated value might be unused" on the `g_tr`/`g_rec` guard defaults (the `tf_useShape=false` path), same constant-folding class as the file's existing warnings.
**Why:** **Rebound is deliberately NOT a criterion** (user 2026-08-05): a small genuine effect may have no rebound at all, so requiring one would reject real pixels. Recovery is the right test — it accepts a response that merely returns to baseline. This also corrected my own reasoning: I had argued a single real pole is "structurally incapable" of the target shape, which was only true when a rebound was required — `y(t) = −A·e^(−t/τ)` is dip-then-return, so a 1-pole fit is a legitimate small effect and the structural test reduces to stability + timescale (reject `|pole|≥1`, reject dominant τ ≳ half the window).
**Next:** UNRUN. Re-open the §10T3 selector on AL_0041 e2 and click g241 @ 3.7 V — the inspector should now say `not (trough … outside [60 250] -> ramp/edge-trough)` or `not (recovery … -> dip does not come back)`. **All previously confirmed selections are invalidated by design** (the key changed), so every session needs a fresh CONFIRM and any affected-set-dependent result from before today is not comparable. `tf_troughMs`/`tf_recFracMax` are first-pass values from the §15 landmarks (trough 114–143 ms, median recovery ~314 ms) — tune on the selector. Note this ALSO bears on TASKS #183 (detector misses real pixels): that is a recall complaint, this is a precision one, and both are symptoms of gating on depth instead of shape. Deferred: the pole-based structural test (stability + dominant τ), which needs `sys` retained per pixel — currently only the impulse response `YItf` is cached.

### 2026-08-05 — GOTCHA: `ols_tf_pipeline.m` §18 ALLSESS is unreachable without CONFIRMing the §10T3 selector
**Changed/Found:** No code change — diagnosis. `imp_state_xsess` failed with "[XSESS] no ALLSESS in the workspace" after an `OLS_OVERRIDE`-driven run with `RUN_ALLSESS=true, allSelExp=[3 1 2]`. Cause: `ols_tf_pipeline.m:755` calls `uiwait(figT)` on the §10T3 [AFFECT-TF-SELECT] figure and **blocks there** until "CONFIRM selection & build model" is pressed. §17d SELECT, §17c STATEDEP and §18 ALLSESS are all downstream of that gate, so closing/dismissing the selector (or never confirming) ends the run before `ALLSESS` is created — with no error, since the `else` branch at :759 only warns. Setting `RUN_ALLSESS=true` is therefore NOT sufficient to get the cross-session batch. Two working paths: (a) press CONFIRM and let it run through; (b) add `affect_mode='matched'` to `OLS_OVERRIDE` — the escape already documented in the §1 config comment (:82) — which skips the TF gate. (b) is safe for the *cross-session* numbers specifically because §18's engine `local_stimblind_session` keys off the energy-based `bledA` map and never reads `affected_tf`; but it does mean that run's single-session §17d/§17c output for `selExp` is matched-filter-gated, not TF-gated, and must not be mixed with confirmed-TF single-session numbers.
**Why:** The batch is gated on an interactive confirmation by deliberate design (selection must precede modelling), but nothing in the `RUN_ALLSESS` knob comment or in `imp_state_xsess`'s error message says so — the error tells you to set `RUN_ALLSESS=true`, which is exactly what had already been done. That mismatch will cost the next person the same session.
**Next:** Make the failure self-explaining rather than re-derivable: either (i) have §18 error early with "selector not confirmed — press CONFIRM or set affect_mode='matched'" when `RUN_ALLSESS` is true and the gate has not been passed, or (ii) auto-skip the `uiwait` when `RUN_ALLSESS` is true. Also amend `imp_state_xsess`'s error text at line 35 to name the CONFIRM gate. Decide (i) vs (ii) with the user — (ii) silently changes what selection the primary session is built on.
